7.2.1.1: Om, salutation to him who is the cause of the turning of the wheel of all worldly existence, whose chest is marked with saffron from the pair of Gaurī's breasts. ॥1॥
7.2.1.2: Sūta said: Having told of the grace that Upamanyu obtained from the Lord, Vāyu rose from his observance when the sun had reached the middle of the sky. ॥2॥
7.2.1.3: And all those sages dwelling in the Naimiṣa forest, having made the resolve that now this matter should be asked, ॥3॥
7.2.1.4: having performed their own duties daily as before, they, seeing the venerable one approaching, sat down around him. ॥4॥
7.2.1.5: Then, at the end of his observance, that lord born of the sky took the excellent seat prepared in the middle of the assembly of sages. ॥5॥
7.2.1.6: Seated comfortably, Vāyu, revered by the worlds, holding in his heart the glorious manifest power of the Lord, spoke this: ॥6॥
7.2.1.7: I take refuge in that Mahādeva, the all-knowing, the unconquered, whose manifestation is this entire world of moving and unmoving beings. ॥7॥
7.2.1.8: Hearing this auspicious speech, the sages, whose sins were destroyed, spoke these excellent words in order to hear the full account of Śiva's glory. ॥8॥
7.2.1.9: The sages said: The account of the great-souled Upamanyu has been told by you, lord — what he obtained from the Supreme Lord through austerity, even undertaken for the sake of milk. ॥9॥
7.2.1.10: He, the elder brother of Dhaumya, was seen by Vāsudeva Kṛṣṇa of unwearied deeds; then by him (Kṛṣṇa), having performed the Pāśupata vow, ॥10॥
7.2.1.11: the supreme knowledge was obtained — this we have heard already. How did Kṛṣṇa obtain the supreme Pāśupata knowledge? ॥11॥
7.2.1.12: Vāyu said: Although the eternal Vāsudeva had descended of his own will, he, as if censuring the human condition, performed purification of the body. ॥12॥
7.2.1.13: For, to perform austerity for the sake of a son, he went to the hermitage of that great sage, frequented by sages, and there he saw the sage, ॥13॥
7.2.1.14: his whole body white with ash, his forehead marked with the tripuṇḍra, wearing a rudrākṣa garland as ornament, adorned with a crown of matted locks, ॥14॥
7.2.1.15: surrounded by sages who were his disciples, as the Veda is by the śāstras — Upamanyu, of great splendour, tranquil, devoted to meditation on Śiva. ॥15॥
7.2.1.16: Seeing him, Kṛṣṇa, with the hair of his whole body thrilled, bowed; with great reverence, having circumambulated him three times, he offered praise with deep delight, shoulders bent, palms joined. ॥16॥
7.2.1.17: Merely by the sage's glance, all of wise Kṛṣṇa's impurity was destroyed — that born of māyā and that born of karma as well. ॥17॥
7.2.1.18: Then Upamanyu, according to rule, having smeared that Kṛṣṇa, whose impurity was destroyed, with ash, with the mantras beginning agni in due order, ॥18॥
7.2.1.19: then, having made him perform the actual Pāśupata vow lasting twelve months, the sage bestowed on him the highest knowledge. ॥19॥
7.2.1.20: From that time on, sages of praiseworthy vows, all divine Pāśupatas, surrounded Kṛṣṇa and attended upon him. ॥20॥
7.2.1.21: Then, at the guru's command, Kṛṣṇa of supreme power performed austerity for the sake of a son, directing it to Śaṅkara together with Ambā. ॥21॥
7.2.1.22: By that austerity, at the end of a year, the Supreme Lord was seen — Śiva, endowed with supreme splendour, with Ambā and with his gaṇas. ॥22॥
7.2.1.23: Bowing to Hara of lovely form, who had appeared to grant a boon, Kṛṣṇa offered praise properly, with joined palms. ॥23॥
7.2.1.24: He obtained a son of his own, given to Viṣṇu by Śiva — accompanied by Ambā and the gaṇas — whose mind was pleased by the austerity. ॥24॥
7.2.1.25: Because Mahādeva, with Ambā (sa-amba), gave him his son, therefore he named Jāmbavatī's son Sāmba. ॥25॥
7.2.1.26: Thus all this has been told: how Kṛṣṇa of immeasurable deeds gained knowledge from the great sage and gained a son from Śaṅkara. ॥26॥
7.2.1.27: Whoever constantly recites this, hears it, or causes it to be heard, attains the knowledge gained by Viṣṇu and rejoices together with him. ॥27॥
7.2.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named Kṛṣṇa obtains a son, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
7.2.2.1: The sages said: What is that Pāśupata knowledge? How is Śiva the Lord of creatures (Paśupati)? And how was Dhaumya's elder brother questioned by Kṛṣṇa, whose deeds are effortless? ॥1॥
7.2.2.2: Relate all this fully, O Vāyu, embodiment of Śaṅkara; for in the three worlds there is no other speaker equal to you, O lord. ॥2॥
7.2.2.3: Sūta said: Hearing these words of the great sages, Prabhañjana (Vāyu), having remembered Śiva the Lord, began to speak. ॥3॥
7.2.2.4: Vāyu said: Long ago, on Mount Mandara, the supreme Pāśupata knowledge was told to the Goddess by Maheśa himself, the god called Śrīkaṇṭha. ॥4॥
7.2.2.5: That very knowledge was asked about by Kṛṣṇa, who is Viṣṇu, source of the universe: the bound-creature-hood of the gods and others, and the lordship of Śiva. ॥5॥
7.2.2.6: As it was taught to Kṛṣṇa by the sage Upamanyu, so I shall tell it in brief; listen to it attentively. ॥6॥
7.2.2.7: Once, Viṣṇu, bearing the form of Kṛṣṇa, bowed duly to Upamanyu as he sat, and spoke these words. ॥7॥
7.2.2.8: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O revered one, I wish to hear the divine Pāśupata knowledge spoken by the God to the Goddess, and also his glory, in full. ॥8॥
7.2.2.9: How is the God the Lord of creatures? Who are declared to be the creatures (paśus)? By what fetters are they bound, and how are they released? ॥9॥
7.2.2.10: Thus urged by the great-souled one, the glorious Upamanyu bowed to the God and the Goddess and spoke just as he had been asked. ॥10॥
7.2.2.11: Upamanyu said: All beings from Brahmā down to the immobile plants, subject to the sway of saṃsāra, are declared to be the paśus of the trident-bearing God of gods. ॥11॥
7.2.2.12: Because he is their lord, Śiva, Lord of the gods, is called Paśupati. That Lord binds the paśus with fetters such as mala and māyā. ॥12॥
7.2.2.13: He alone is their liberator when properly worshipped with devotion. These twenty-four principles, māyā, karma and the guṇas— ॥13॥
7.2.2.14: —these are called the objects (viṣayas), the fetters that bind souls. Having bound the paśus, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, ॥14॥
7.2.2.15: with these fetters the Lord God makes them carry out his own work. By the command of that Maheśa, Prakṛti brings forth intellect suited to the soul; ॥15॥
7.2.2.16: she gives birth to intellect; intellect produces ego; ego produces the eleven senses and likewise the five subtle elements, ॥16॥
7.2.2.17: by the command of Śiva, God of gods, giver of welfare. The subtle elements too, by his mighty command, ॥17॥
7.2.2.18: bring forth all the gross elements in due order; and they in turn produce the bodily union of embodied beings from Brahmā down to grass. ॥18॥
7.2.2.19: All the gross elements generate this by Śiva's command. Intellect determines; ego claims as mine; ॥19॥
7.2.2.20: the citta perceives, and the mind forms intentions; the ear and other senses grasp their objects, sound and the rest, separately— ॥20॥
7.2.2.21: only their own, not others, through the divine power of the God's command. And those which are speech and the rest, the organs of action, ॥21॥
7.2.2.22: perform each its own function and nothing else, by Śiva's command. Sound and the rest are grasped, and speech and the rest are performed, ॥22॥
7.2.2.23: for Śambhu's weighty command cannot be transgressed by anyone. Space grants room to all beings, ॥23॥
7.2.2.24: the all-pervading ether, solely by the command of the Supreme Lord. And likewise, under different names such as prāṇa, the world inside and outside— ॥24॥
7.2.2.25: all of it the Wind sustains by the command of Śarva. Fire carries the oblation of the gods and the offering (kavya) of the ancestors who partake of it, ॥25॥
7.2.2.26: and Fire performs cooking and the like by the Supreme Lord's command. By his command the waters give life and so on to all. ॥26॥
7.2.2.27: The Earth constantly upholds the world by the command of the Lord of the universe. Indra protects the gods, slays the asuras and guards the three worlds, ॥27॥
7.2.2.28: the king of the gods doing so by his command, which no god can transgress. Varuṇa ever exercises lordship over the waters, ॥28॥
7.2.2.29: and binds with his nooses those deserving punishment, by his command alone. The lord of the yakṣas, the lord of wealth, constantly gives wealth ॥29॥
7.2.2.30: to beings according to their merit, by the instruction of the Supreme Person. Īśāna perpetually bestows prosperity, and knowledge on the wise, ॥30॥
7.2.2.31: and restraint of the wicked—Īśāna does this by Śiva's command. Śeṣa bears the earth on his head by Śiva's appointment— ॥31॥
7.2.2.32: he whom they call the tāmasic, fierce (Raudra), end-bringing form of Hari. The four-faced Brahmā creates everything by the Lord's command, ॥32॥
7.2.2.33: and with other forms of his own he protects and at the end destroys. Viṣṇu protects the universe by the command of the Death of Death (Śiva), ॥33॥
7.2.2.34: and also creates and devours it with his own three bodies. Hara withdraws the whole world at the end, by his command alone, ॥34॥
7.2.2.35: and that Soul of the universe, divided threefold, also creates and protects. Time makes everything; Time destroys creatures; ॥35॥
7.2.2.36: Time preserves the universe—by the command of the Death of Death. Sustaining the world with his three portions and directing rain with his rays, ॥36॥
7.2.2.37: that Sun rains from the sky by the command of the God of gods. The Moon nourishes all kinds of plants and gladdens beings, ॥37॥
7.2.2.38: and the Moon is drunk by the gods, by the command of him whose ornament is the moon. The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, the two Aśvins and likewise the Maruts, ॥38॥
7.2.2.39: sky-goers, sages, Siddhas, serpents, humans, wild animals, cattle, birds, insects and the like, and immobile beings, ॥39॥
7.2.2.40: rivers, oceans, mountains, forests and lakes, the Vedas with their limbs, the śāstras, mantras, hymns of praise, sacrifices and the rest— ॥40॥
7.2.2.41: The worlds from Kālāgni up to Śiva, together with their lords, and the countless cosmic eggs (brahmāṇḍa) and their enveloping sheaths, ॥41॥
7.2.2.42: present, past and future, in their entirety; the directions and the intermediate directions, and the divisions of time beginning with the kalā, ॥42॥
7.2.2.43: and whatever is seen or heard in this world — all that is governed by the power of Śaṅkara's command. ॥43॥
7.2.2.44: By the power of his command the earth stands here, as do the mountains, the clouds, the oceans, the hosts of luminaries, the gods headed by Śakra — whatever exists, stable or enduring, sentient or insentient. ॥44॥
7.2.2.45: Upamanyu said: O Kṛṣṇa, hear this exceedingly wonderful deed wrought by the command of Śambhu of immeasurable acts, which I heard from the mouth of the Veda (śruti). ॥45॥
7.2.2.46: Long ago, it is said, the gods together with Indra, having conquered the asuras in battle, were quarrelling with one another, each saying, I am the victor, I. ॥46॥
7.2.2.47: Then Maheśvara himself, assuming a splendid guise, his body devoid of his own distinguishing marks, appeared in their midst as a yakṣa. ॥47॥
7.2.2.48: Taking up a single blade of grass on the ground, he said to those gods: Whoever is able to alter this, he indeed is the conqueror of the daityas. ॥48॥
7.2.2.49: Hearing the yakṣa's words, Śacī's lord, the wielder of the thunderbolt, somewhat angered, laughed at him and set about taking up the grass. ॥49॥
7.2.2.50: That grass could not be taken up even in thought; nevertheless, the bearer of the thunderbolt somehow hurled his thunderbolt to cut it. ॥50॥
7.2.2.51: That thunderbolt, struck by that grass as if it met on all sides with an adamant of its own, fell with its point turned aside. ॥51॥
7.2.2.52: Then the other guardians of the worlds, mighty and greatly enraged, hurled their own weapons by the thousands at the grass. ॥52॥
7.2.2.53: A great fire blazed up, a fierce wind blew, and the lord of the waters swelled, as when the dissolution (pralaya) has arrived. ॥53॥
7.2.2.54: Thus what the gods undertook with effort against the grass proved futile, ah Kṛṣṇa, through the yakṣa's own power. ॥54॥
7.2.2.55: Then the lord of the gods, indignant, said to the yakṣa: Who are you? Thereupon he vanished even as they looked on. ॥55॥
7.2.2.56: Meanwhile the Goddess Haimavatī, adorned with divine ornaments, radiant and sweetly smiling, appeared on the stage of the sky. ॥56॥
7.2.2.57: Seeing her, the gods headed by Śakra, filled with wonder, bowed and asked about the yakṣa: Who is that extraordinary yakṣa? ॥57॥
7.2.2.58: The Goddess said with a smile: He is beyond your perception. By him this wheel called saṃsāra, comprising the moving and the unmoving, is made to revolve. ॥58॥
7.2.2.59: By him the universe is made in the beginning, by him it is withdrawn again. There is none who could control him; by him everything is controlled. ॥59॥
7.2.2.60: Having said this, the great Goddess vanished right there; and all the gods, amazed, bowed to her and went to heaven. ॥60॥
7.2.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The greatness of Śiva, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
7.2.3.1: Upamanyu said: Listen, O Kṛṣṇa: this entire world, moving and unmoving, is pervaded by the forms that are the very self of Maheśa Śiva, the Supreme Self. ॥1॥
7.2.3.2: That Śiva, whose self is immeasurable, presides over all this through his own forms; thus is all this handed down in tradition. ॥2॥
7.2.3.3: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Maheśāna and Sadāśiva are to be known as his forms, by which this universe is pervaded. ॥3॥
7.2.3.4: There are also five other bodies, called the Brahmans; there exists nothing here that is not pervaded by those bodies. ॥4॥
7.2.3.5: Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Vāmadeva and Sadyojāta: these Brahmans are the five renowned forms of the god. ॥5॥
7.2.3.6: His form called Īśāna, the first and most venerable, directly presides over the knower of the field (kṣetrajña), the enjoyer of Prakṛti. ॥6॥
7.2.3.7: The form called Tatpuruṣa of Sthāṇu, the lord possessing form, presides over the unmanifest, the object of enjoyment, which is the substrate of the guṇas. ॥7॥
7.2.3.8: The highly worshipped form of Pinākin called Aghora presides over the principle of intellect (buddhi-tattva), endowed with the eight limbs beginning with dharma. ॥8॥
7.2.3.9: Those versed in the Āgamas call the form named Vāmadeva of Mahādeva, the ordainer, the presiding deity of ego (ahaṅkāra). ॥9॥
7.2.3.10: The wise declare the form named Sadyojāta of Śambhu of boundless splendour to be the presiding deity of the mind. ॥10॥
7.2.3.11: The wise know this form of the Lord named Īśāna as the ruler of the ear, of speech, of sound, and likewise of all-pervading ether. ॥11॥
7.2.3.12: All who are expert in the meaning of the Purāṇas know the lordly form called Tatpuruṣa as the ruler of skin, hand, touch and air. ॥12॥
7.2.3.13: The sages declare the form named Aghora to be the presiding deity of the eye, of the feet, of visible form, and likewise of fire. ॥13॥
7.2.3.14: They know the form named Vāmadeva, devoted to them, as the ruler of the tongue, of the anus, of taste, and likewise of water. ॥14॥
7.2.3.15: They declare the form named Sadyojāta as the ruler of the nose, of the generative organ, of smell, and of the earth. ॥15॥
7.2.3.16: These five forms of the god, the sole causes of all welfare, should be constantly worshipped with effort by men who seek welfare. ॥16॥
7.2.3.17: The world consists of the eight forms of that God of gods; the universe abides in him, he pervading it, like clusters of gems on a thread. ॥17॥
7.2.3.18: Śarva, Bhava, Rudra, Ugra, Bhīma, Paśupati, Īśāna and Mahādeva are the eight renowned forms. ॥18॥
7.2.3.19: Earth, water, fire, wind, ether, the knower of the field, the sun and the moon are presided over by the eight forms of Maheśa beginning with Śarva. ॥19॥
7.2.3.20: The form named Śarva, called Śārvī, whose nature is the all-bearing earth, supports the universe of moving and unmoving beings: such is the conclusion of scripture. ॥20॥
7.2.3.21: The form of Bhava, the Supreme Self, consisting of water, which gives life to the whole world, is celebrated as Bhāvī. ॥21॥
7.2.3.22: The form of Rudra called Raudrī, fiery, auspicious, of terrible appearance, abides pervading the universe, present outside and within. ॥22॥
7.2.3.23: Having the nature of wind, it sets this world in motion, sustains it, and itself moves; the good call this form of Ugra, the ordainer, Augrī. ॥23॥
7.2.3.24: Giving room to all, all-pervading, of the nature of space, the form of Bhīma called Bhīmā divides the multitude of beings. ॥24॥
7.2.3.25: Presiding over all souls, dwelling in all bodies, the form of Paśupati should be known as the cutter of the bonds of the bound souls. ॥25॥
7.2.3.26: Illuminating the whole world, the form of Maheśa called Īśāna, known as the Sun, moves through the sky. ॥26॥
7.2.3.27: The nectar-rayed moon, who nourishes the universe, is that form of Mahādeva named Mahādeva. ॥27॥
7.2.3.28: The self is the eighth form of that Śiva, the Supreme Self, pervading the other forms; therefore the universe has Śiva as its essence. ॥28॥
7.2.3.29: Just as the branches of a tree flourish by watering its root, so by the worship of Śiva the world, which is his body, flourishes. ॥29॥
7.2.3.30: They know the worship of Śiva to be the granting of fearlessness to all, the favouring of all, and the doing of good to all. ॥30॥
7.2.3.31: Just as here a father is pleased by the happiness of his sons, grandsons and others, so Śaṅkara is pleased by the happiness of all. ॥31॥
7.2.3.32: If harm is done to any embodied being whatsoever, that is surely a wrong done to the Eight-formed One; there is no doubt. ॥32॥
7.2.3.33: Worship with your whole being Rudra, the supreme cause, Śiva, who abides presiding over the universe in the form of his eight forms. ॥33॥
7.2.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named Upamanyu's teaching to Kṛṣṇa, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
7.2.4.1: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Lord, I have heard how this entire universe is pervaded by the forms of Śarva, the Supreme Lord of immeasurable splendour. ॥1॥
7.2.4.2: Now I wish to know the true nature of the two Supreme Rulers, and how this universe, which consists of female and male nature, is presided over by the two of them. ॥2॥
7.2.4.3: Upamanyu said: I shall tell you briefly the glorious manifestation of Śiva and Śivā and their true nature; to tell it in full is not possible even for Bhava himself. ॥3॥
7.2.4.4: The Great Goddess is Śakti herself, and Mahādeva is the possessor of Śakti; all this, moving and unmoving, is but a fraction of their glory. ॥4॥
7.2.4.5: Some reality is of insentient form, some reality is of the nature of consciousness; this pair is respectively pure and impure, higher and lower. ॥5॥
7.2.4.6: The circle of conscious beings that transmigrates, joined with the circle of insentient things, is the impure and lower; the other is the higher and auspicious. ॥6॥
7.2.4.7: Both the lower and the higher, this pair of conscious and insentient nature — lordship over it belongs by nature to Śiva and Śivā. ॥7॥
7.2.4.8: The universe is under the control of Śiva and Śivā; they are not under the control of the universe. Since this universe is what is to be ruled, therefore Śiva and Śivā are the Lords of the universe. ॥8॥
7.2.4.9: As Śiva is, so is the Goddess; as the Goddess is, so is Śiva. One should know no difference between these two, as between the moon and moonlight. ॥9॥
7.2.4.10: Just as this moon does not shine without moonlight, so Śiva, though existing, does not shine without Śakti. ॥10॥
7.2.4.11: For just as this sun does not exist without its radiance, so radiance does not exist without that sun, being wholly dependent on it. ॥11॥
7.2.4.12: Thus mutual dependence exists between Śakti and the possessor of Śakti: there is no Śakti without Śiva, and no Śiva without Śakti. ॥12॥
7.2.4.13: She through whom Śiva is ever potent in granting enjoyment and liberation to embodied beings — she is the primordial, sole, supreme Śakti, made of consciousness, resting in Śiva. ॥13॥
7.2.4.14: Whom they declare, by virtue of those various corresponding qualities, to be of the same nature as Śiva, the Lord of all, the Supreme Self. ॥14॥
7.2.4.15: That one supreme Śakti, whose form is consciousness and whose nature is to bring forth, divides the universe in many ways and arranges it by Śiva's will. ॥15॥
7.2.4.16: She is remembered as threefold: the root Prakṛti, Māyā, and the one with three guṇas; by her, Śivā, this world has been spread out and variously transformed. ॥16॥
7.2.4.17: The Śaktis are indeed distinguished as one, as two, as hundreds of thousands — in many ways, according to their function. ॥17॥
7.2.4.18: By Śiva's will the supreme Śakti, having become one with the Śiva-principle, then springs forth at the beginning of creation, like oil from sesame. ॥18॥
7.2.4.19: Then, when that Śakti was stirred by the power called Kriyā arising from the possessor of power, Nāda first appeared. ॥19॥
7.2.4.20: From Nāda issued Bindu; from Bindu the god Sadāśiva; from him Maheśvara was born, and from Maheśvara Śuddhavidyā. ॥20॥
7.2.4.21: She is the Trident-bearer's power, sovereign of speech, called Vāgīśā, who unfolds in the form of letters as Mātṛkā. ॥21॥
7.2.4.22: Then, through the entering of Ananta, Māyā emitted Kāla, Niyati, Kalā and Vidyā; from Kalā came Rāga and Puruṣa. ॥22॥
7.2.4.23: From Māyā again arose the Unmanifest, consisting of the three guṇas; and from that triple Unmanifest the three guṇas became separated. ॥23॥
7.2.4.24: They are sattva, rajas and tamas, by which the whole world is pervaded. From the guṇas, as they were agitated, arose the three forms called the Lords of the guṇas, ॥24॥
7.2.4.25: and the principles beginning with Mahat came into being in due order. From them, by Śiva's command, arose countless cosmic eggs and bodies, presided over by the Vidyeśas beginning with Ananta, the sovereigns. ॥25॥
7.2.4.26: The divisions of Śakti are proclaimed according to the differences of various bodies; they are to be known as of many forms through the distinction of gross and subtle. ॥26॥
7.2.4.27: That Śakti of Rudra is Raudrī; of Viṣṇu she is held to be Vaiṣṇavī; of Brahmā she is called Brahmāṇī; and of Indra she is named Aindrī. ॥27॥
7.2.4.28: What need of saying more here? Whatever is called the universe is pervaded by Śakti as its very self, as the body is by the inner Self. ॥28॥
7.2.4.29: Therefore the whole world, unmoving and moving, is made of Śakti. That which is called Kalā is the supreme Śakti of the Supreme Self. ॥29॥
7.2.4.30: Thus this supreme Śakti, following the will of the Lord, creates whatever universe there is, stationary and moving — this is the settled conclusion. ॥30॥
7.2.4.31: Through his own three powers — knowledge, action and will (the desire to act) — the Lord, the possessor of power, eternally pervades the universe and presides over it. ॥31॥
7.2.4.32: This should be thus, this should not be thus — of such a nature is the eternal will-power of Maheśa, which regulates effects. ॥32॥
7.2.4.33: The power of knowledge, in the form of intellect, determines truly the effect, the instrument, the cause and the purpose. ॥33॥
7.2.4.34: The power of action, whose form is resolve, fashions in an instant the whole world and every effect, as desired and as determined. ॥34॥
7.2.4.35: In accordance with these powers, she whose nature is to bring forth from Śakti, impelled by the supreme Śakti, gives birth to the whole world, the arising of the triad. ॥35॥
7.2.4.36: Thus, through union with Śakti, Śiva is called the possessor of Śakti; and this world, arising from Śakti and the possessor of Śakti, is both Śākta and Śaiva. ॥36॥
7.2.4.37: Just as a son is not born without a father and a mother, so this moving and unmoving world does not exist without Bhava and Bhavānī. ॥37॥
7.2.4.38: The universe originates from the female and the male, consists of female and male, is the glory of the female and the male, and is presided over by the female and the male. ॥38॥
7.2.4.39: Śiva is called the Supreme Self, and she is proclaimed Śivā; Śiva is called Sadāśiva, and Śivā is Manonmanī; Śiva is to be known as Maheśvara, and Śivā is called Māyā. ॥39॥
7.2.4.40: Puruṣa is the Supreme Lord (Parameśāna), Prakṛti is the Supreme Goddess (Parameśvarī); Rudra is Maheśvara himself, and Rudrāṇī is Rudra's beloved. ॥40॥
7.2.4.41: Viṣṇu is the god Viśveśvara Śiva, and Lakṣmī is Viśveśvara's beloved Pārvatī. When Śiva is the creator, he is Brahmā, and Brahmāṇī, Brahmā's beloved, is she. ॥41॥
7.2.4.42: The blessed Śambhu is the Sun, and the blessed Śivā is its radiance. The enemy of Manmatha is great Indra, and the daughter of the lord of mountains is Śacī. ॥42॥
7.2.4.43: Mahādeva is Fire (Jātavedas), and she who has half of Śarva's body is Svāhā. The god Tryambaka is Yama, and his beloved is the mountain's daughter. ॥43॥
7.2.4.44: The blessed Lord is Nirṛti, and the delight of the mountain is Nairṛtī. The blessed Rudra is Varuṇa, and the daughter of the earth-bearer Himālaya is Vāruṇī. ॥44॥
7.2.4.45: He whose crest is the young moon is Vāyu, and Śivā, who charms Śiva's mind, is his consort. The beheader of the sacrifice is the Yakṣa Kubera, and the daughter of the lord of the Himālaya is Ṛddhi. ॥45॥
7.2.4.46: He whose crest is the half-moon is the Moon, and Rudra's beloved is Rohiṇī. The supreme Lord is Īśāna, and his noble consort is the Supreme Goddess. ॥46॥
7.2.4.47: He who wears Ananta the serpent as a bracelet is Ananta, and the beloved of Ananta Śiva is Anantā. The enemy of Time is Kālāgnirudra, and the beloved of the ender of Time is Kālī. ॥47॥
7.2.4.48: Śambhu is the Manu called Puruṣa Svāyambhuva, and Śiva's beloved is Śatarūpā. Dakṣa is Mahādeva himself, and Prasūti is the Supreme Goddess. ॥48॥
7.2.4.49: Bhava is Ruci, and Bhavānī is called Ākūti by the wise. The god who destroyed Bhaga's eyes is Bhṛgu, and the beloved of the three-eyed one is Khyāti. ॥49॥
7.2.4.50: The blessed Rudra is Marīci, and Śarva's beloved is Sambhūti. The bearer of the Gaṅgā should be known as Aṅgiras, and Umā herself is regarded as Smṛti. ॥50॥
7.2.4.51: He who wears the moon on his head is Pulastya, and the beloved of the Pināka-bearer is Prīti. The destroyer of Tripura is Pulaha, and his beloved is Śiva's beloved. ॥51॥
7.2.4.52: The destroyer of the sacrifice is declared to be Kratu, and the Lord's beloved is Sannati. The three-eyed one is Atri, and Umā herself is regarded by the wise as Anasūyā. ॥52॥
7.2.4.53: The god who slew Kāla is Kaśyapa, and Maheśvarī is the mother of the gods Aditi. The enemy of Manmatha is Vasiṣṭha, and the Goddess herself is Arundhatī. ॥53॥
7.2.4.54: All males are Śaṅkara; all females are Maheśvarī. Therefore all women and men are the manifestations of those two alone. ॥54॥
7.2.4.55: The blessed Lord is the experiencer of objects; the Supreme Goddess is the object. All that is to be heard is Umā's form; the hearer is he whose excellent weapon is the trident. ॥55॥
7.2.4.56: Śaṅkara's beloved bears the whole range of things to be asked about; the asker is he alone, the soul of the universe, who has the young moon as his ornament. ॥56॥
7.2.4.57: Bhava's beloved bears the form of things to be seen; the seer is the god Viśveśvara, whose crest-jewel is the crescent moon. ॥57॥
7.2.4.58: All tastes are the Great Goddess; the taster is the god Śiva. All objects of love are Girijā, and the lover is the poison-eater. ॥58॥
7.2.4.59: The goddess Maheśvarī always bears the state of being the object of thought; the thinker is he alone, the soul of the universe, Mahādeva, Maheśvara. ॥59॥
7.2.4.60: Bhava's beloved bears the form of things to be known; the knower is that same blessed god whose crest is the lovely moon. ॥60॥
7.2.4.61: The blessed Lord, the Pināka-bearer, is the life-breath of all living beings; and Ambikā, in the form of water, is the sustenance of the life of all. ॥61॥
7.2.4.62: The Goddess, beloved of the destroyer of Tripura, bears the state of the field (kṣetra); then the blessed destroyer of Death bears the state of the knower of the field (kṣetrajña). ॥62॥
7.2.4.63: The god armed with the trident is the day; the beloved of the trident-bearer is the night. The god Śaṅkara is the sky; Śaṅkara's beloved is the earth. ॥63॥
7.2.4.64: The blessed Lord is the ocean; the daughter of the lord of mountains is the shore. The god with the bull-banner is the tree; the beloved of Viśveśvara is the creeper. ॥64॥
7.2.4.65: The blessed chastiser of the three cities bears everything masculine, and the Goddess who delights the god bears everything feminine. ॥65॥
7.2.4.66: The beloved of all bears the entire network of words, and he whose crest is the lovely moon bears the whole nature of meaning. ॥66॥
7.2.4.67: Whatever power is declared of whatever thing, each such power is the goddess Viśveśvarī, and each possessor of power is wholly Maheśvara. ॥67॥
7.2.4.68: Whatever is supreme, whatever is pure, whatever is meritorious and whatever is auspicious — each of these, the illustrious ones declare, is the unfolding of the splendour of those two. ॥68॥
7.2.4.69: Just as the flame of a lit lamp illumines a house, so this splendour of those two pervades and illumines the world. ॥69॥
7.2.4.70: The graded excellence of the universe, from a blade of grass up to the form of Śiva, follows the degree of nearness to those two — so says the supreme scripture. ॥70॥
7.2.4.71: These two, whose nature comprises all forms and who bestow every good, are always to be worshipped, bowed to and meditated upon. ॥71॥
7.2.4.72: O Kṛṣṇa, I have told you today this true nature of the two Supreme Lords according to my understanding, but not in its full extent. ॥72॥
7.2.4.73: For how can the true nature of the two Supreme Lords be told, which lies beyond even the minds of all the great ones? ॥73॥
7.2.4.74: It lies within the reach of those devoted to none else, whose minds are offered to the Lord; for others it does not rise into the intellect, while for them it rises exactly as it is. ॥74॥
7.2.4.75: This manifestation that has been described is the material one, and is regarded as the lower; the knowers of secrets know another, supreme, non-material and secret one. ॥75॥
7.2.4.76: That from which words turn back together with the mind and the senses — this is the supreme, non-material manifestation of the Supreme Lord. ॥76॥
7.2.4.77: That alone is here the supreme abode, that alone is here the supreme goal, that alone is here the ultimate limit — the manifestation of the Supreme One. ॥77॥
7.2.4.78: To attain it, those who have mastered their breath and conquered their senses strive here, so that the door of the prison-house of the womb is shut without a gap. ॥78॥
7.2.4.79: One who knows the manifestation of Śiva and Śivā — the reviving herb for those slain by the bite of the serpent of saṃsāra — fears nothing from anywhere. ॥79॥
7.2.4.80: He who truly knows both the supreme and the lower manifestation transcends the lower glory and attains the supreme glory. ॥80॥
7.2.4.81: O Kṛṣṇa, I have thus told you the true nature of the two Supreme Selves, Śiva and Śivā. Though it is a secret, you are worthy of it, since you are a devotee of Bharga (Śiva). ॥81॥
7.2.4.82: One should never declare the glory of the two Lords to those who are not disciples, nor to non-Śaivas, nor to non-devotees — this is the injunction of the Veda. ॥82॥
7.2.4.83: Therefore, O most auspicious one, you should certainly not tell it to outsiders; tell it to those who are like you and fit, and not otherwise. ॥83॥
7.2.4.84: Whoever imparts this glory of Śiva and Śivā to worthy persons is freed from the ocean of saṃsāra and attains union (sāyujya) with Śiva. ॥84॥
7.2.4.85: By reciting it, crores of great sins are destroyed; by repeating it three or four times, even more than those are destroyed. ॥85॥
7.2.4.86: Hostile enemies perish and friends likewise increase; Śaiva knowledge grows, and the mind turns toward truth. ॥86॥
7.2.4.87: There arises supreme devotion to Śiva together with Ambā, with his attendants and his retinue; and whatever else is most desired, that he attains without doubt. ॥87॥
7.2.4.88: If a devotee of Śiva, pure within, recites it with confidence, and if the fruit is obstructed by powerful past karmas, he should repeat it again and again; for him nothing here is hard to attain. ॥88॥
7.2.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The yoga of the glories of Gaurī and Śaṅkara, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
7.2.5.1: Upamanyu said: This whole universe, moving and unmoving, is the body of the God of gods; yet the bound souls (paśu) do not know it to be so, because of the heaviness of their bonds. ॥1॥
7.2.5.2: O delight of the Yadus, the great sages, not knowing his supreme, undifferentiated nature, speak of that One in many ways. ॥2॥
7.2.5.3: Some call Mahādeva, the Supreme without beginning or end, both the lower form of Brahman and likewise the higher, which is Brahman itself. ॥3॥
7.2.5.4: The lower Brahman is declared to consist of the elements, the senses, the inner organ, primordial matter and the sense-objects; the higher Brahman is of the nature of consciousness. ॥4॥
7.2.5.5: It is called Brahman because of its vastness or because of its power to expand. Both of these are forms of Brahman, belonging to the Lord who is master of Brahman. By some the Lord is said to have the nature of knowledge and nescience. ॥5॥
7.2.5.6: They call knowledge the conscious and nescience the unconscious; and the universe, consisting of knowledge and nescience, belongs to the all-pervading teacher of the universe, ॥6॥
7.2.5.7: it is indeed his form, without doubt, since the universe is under his control. Error, knowledge and the Supreme — thus they know the highest form of Śarva. ॥7॥
7.2.5.8: Mistaken cognition of objects, in its many kinds, is called error; awareness of things in their true form is proclaimed knowledge. ॥8॥
7.2.5.9: The reality free from conceptual distinctions is called the Supreme; its opposite is termed asat (non-being) by the expounders of the Veda. ॥9॥
7.2.5.10: Because he is lord of both, Śiva is called the lord of being and non-being. Some call him of the nature of the perishable and imperishable; others, beyond the perishable and imperishable. ॥10॥
7.2.5.11: The perishable is all beings; the unchanging is called the imperishable. Both are forms of the supreme Lord, since they are under his control. ॥11॥
7.2.5.12: Beyond these two is Śiva, the tranquil, remembered as transcending the perishable and imperishable. Him who is of the form of the aggregate and the individual, and the cause of the aggregate and the individual — ॥12॥
7.2.5.13: some sages call Śiva, the supreme cause. They call the aggregate the unmanifest, and likewise the individual the manifest. ॥13॥
7.2.5.14: These two are forms of the supreme Lord, since they proceed from his will. Because he is the cause of both, Śiva is the supreme cause — ॥14॥
7.2.5.15: so say those who know the meaning of causation: the cause of the aggregate and the individual. By some the Lord is said to have the nature of genus and individual. ॥15॥
7.2.5.16: That which persists throughout every body is called the genus; the individual is of the nature of distinction, resting upon that collection of bodies. ॥16॥
7.2.5.17: Since genera and individuals are sustained by his command, therefore Mahādeva is regarded as having genus and individual for his body. ॥17॥
7.2.5.18: Śiva is said to be the self of primordial matter, spirit, the manifest and time. They call pradhāna Prakṛti, and likewise the knower of the field Puruṣa. ॥18॥
7.2.5.19: The wise call the twenty-three principles the manifest; time is the sole cause of the transformation of the world of effects. ॥19॥
7.2.5.20: Of these the Lord is the ruler, the sustainer, the one who sets them in motion and withdraws them, the sole cause of their appearance and disappearance, self-ruling and unborn. ॥20॥
7.2.5.21: Therefore Maheśvara, having the form of pradhāna, puruṣa, the manifest and time, is declared their cause, guide, ruler and sustainer. ॥21॥
7.2.5.22: By some the Lord is said to be Virāj and Hiraṇyagarbha: Hiraṇyagarbha is the cause of the worlds, and Virāj is the universe as a whole. ॥22॥
7.2.5.23: By the seers Śiva is called the Inner Controller and the Supreme; others declare him to be Prājña, Taijasa and Viśva. ॥23॥
7.2.5.24: Some call him terrible, others know him as wholly gentle; still others call him the knower, the means of knowing, the known and cognition. ॥24॥
7.2.5.25: Others call him the agent, the action, the effect, the instrument and the cause; others declare him the self of waking, dream and deep sleep. ॥25॥
7.2.5.26: Some call him the Fourth (turīya), others that beyond the Fourth; some call him without qualities, others know him as possessing qualities. ॥26॥
7.2.5.27: Some call him subject to transmigration, others free from it; some call him independent, others know him as dependent. ॥27॥
7.2.5.28: Some call him terrible, others know him as wholly gentle; some call him full of passion, and likewise others free from passion. ॥28॥
7.2.5.29: Some call him actionless, and other people active; some call him without senses, and likewise others possessed of senses. ॥29॥
7.2.5.30: Some call him permanent, others impermanent; some indeed call him formless, others know him as having form. ॥30॥
7.2.5.31: Some call him invisible, others know him as visible; some call him expressible, others inexpressible; some call him of the nature of sound, and others beyond sound. ॥31॥
7.2.5.32: Some call him made of thought, others devoid of thought; some call him of the nature of knowledge, and others discerning knowledge (vijñāna). ॥32॥
7.2.5.33: Some call him knowable, some unknowable; some call him the highest, and likewise others the lower. ॥33॥
7.2.5.34: The true nature of the Supreme Being, being thus variously conceived, the sages do not ascertain, on account of their manifold notions. ॥34॥
7.2.5.35: But those who have taken refuge in the supreme Lord with their whole being, they indeed know Śiva, the supreme cause, without effort. ॥35॥
7.2.5.36: As long as the bound soul does not see the ancient Seer, who has no lord over him, the ruler of the world, so long does he, fettered, remain in sorrow in this saṃsāra, turning like the rim of a wheel. ॥36॥
7.2.5.37: When the seer beholds the gold-hued Maker, the Lord, the Person, the source of Brahmā, then the knower, shaking off merit and demerit, stainless, attains supreme equality with him. ॥37॥
7.2.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The yoga of knowing the state of Paśupati, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
7.2.6.1: Upamanyu said: Śiva has no bondage of the āṇava impurity, nor of kārya karma, nor that arising from māyā; nor that of prakṛti, nor that of the intellect, nor likewise that consisting of ego (ahaṅkāra). ॥1॥
7.2.6.2: He has no bondage of the mind, nor of thought, nor of the senses; nor bondage of the subtle elements (tanmātras), nor any bondage of the gross elements. ॥2॥
7.2.6.3: For Śambhu of boundless splendour there is no time (kāla), no kalā, no nescience (avidyā), likewise no niyati; no attachment and no aversion. ॥3॥
7.2.6.4: Nor does he have clinging to life (abhiniveśa), nor good and bad deeds, nor their ripening, nor pleasure and pain which are their fruit. ॥4॥
7.2.6.5: Nor has he any connection with latent dispositions (āśaya), nor with the impressions of actions, nor with enjoyments and the impressions of enjoyments ranging over the three times. ॥5॥
7.2.6.6: He has no cause, no maker, no beginning, no end, nor any middle; no action, no instrument, nothing not to be done, nor anything to be done. ॥6॥
7.2.6.7: He has no kinsman or non-kinsman, no controller or impeller; no master, no guru, no protector, none superior and likewise none equal. ॥7॥
7.2.6.8: He has no birth and death, nothing desired or undesired; no injunction and no prohibition, no liberation and no bondage. ॥8॥
7.2.6.9: Whatever is inauspicious, none of it is ever his; and all that is auspicious is his, since Śiva is the Supreme Self. ॥9॥
7.2.6.10: That Śiva, presiding over all this by his own powers, remains unfallen from his own nature; therefore he is known as Sthāṇu (the Steadfast). ॥10॥
7.2.6.11: Since the world of moving and unmoving beings is presided over by Śiva, Śarva is known as having all forms; knowing him thus, one is not deluded. ॥11॥
7.2.6.12: Śarva, Rudra—salutation to him—the great Person, higher than being, golden-armed, the Blessed One, lord of gold, the Lord; ॥12॥
7.2.6.13: the lord of Ambikā, Īśāna, bearer of the Pināka bow, who rides the bull; the one Rudra, the supreme Brahman, the Person dark and tawny; ॥13॥
7.2.6.14: the size of a hair-tip, to be meditated upon in the middle of the heart, within the small inner space (dahara); golden-haired, lotus-eyed, ruddy and coppery; ॥14॥
7.2.6.15: that god who moves down among beings, blue-necked, golden; gentle, non-terrible, and likewise mixed; imperishable, immortal, undecaying. ॥15॥
7.2.6.16: He is the supreme distinct Person, the Blessed One, the ender of Death (Antaka), free from the sentient and insentient, and higher than the highest, beyond the manifest world. ॥16॥
7.2.6.17: When knowledge and lordship are seen in Śiva in their pre-eminence, the wise declare him to be established as surpassing even the lords of the worlds. ॥17॥
7.2.6.18: He alone, in the beginning, is the teacher of the full extent of the scriptures to the Brahmās born in each successive creation, who exist within the limits of time. ॥18॥
7.2.6.19: He is the guru even of the gurus who are bound by the limits of time; the lord of all, he is free from the limits of time. ॥19॥
7.2.6.20: His power is pure, innate, and surpassing all; his knowledge is incomparable and eternal; his body is utterly stainless; ॥20॥
7.2.6.21: his lordship is without rival, his bliss absolute; so too are his strength, the might of his splendour, valour, forbearance and compassion. ॥21॥
7.2.6.22: Being entirely full, he has no purpose of his own in creation and the rest; the fruit of all his activity is solely grace for others. ॥22॥
7.2.6.23: The praṇava (Om) is the word that denotes that Śiva, the Supreme Self; among words such as Śiva, Rudra and so on, the praṇava is held to be the highest. ॥23॥
7.2.6.24: Through meditation on Śambhu, who is denoted by the praṇava, and also through its repetition, whatever supreme attainment there is becomes attainable—of this there is no doubt. ॥24॥
7.2.6.25: Therefore the wise who have mastered the Āgamas, regarding the denoted and the denoting as one, call the god the One Syllable. ॥25॥
7.2.6.26: Its measures (mātrās) are declared at the summit of the Veda to be four: akāra, ukāra, makāra, and the nāda (resonance). ॥26॥
7.2.6.27: They call akāra the Ṛgveda; ukāra is said to be the Yajus; makāra the Sāman; and its nāda is held to be the Atharvan scripture. ॥27॥
7.2.6.28: Akāra is the great seed, rajas, the four-faced creator Brahmā; ukāra is prakṛti, the womb, sattva, the preserver Hari. ॥28॥
7.2.6.29: Makāra is puruṣa, the seed, tamas, Hara the destroyer; the nāda is the supreme Person, the Lord, attributeless and actionless—Śiva. ॥29॥
7.2.6.30: Having expressed this entire universe threefold by the three measures, the praṇava makes known the Self that is Śiva by the half-measure. ॥30॥
7.2.6.31: Than whom there is nothing higher or other, than whom there is nothing subtler nor greater; who, the One, stands motionless like a tree in heaven—by that Person this whole universe is filled. ॥31॥
7.2.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The truth of Śiva, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
7.2.7.1: His natural power (śakti) is knowledge (vidyā), distinct from the universe. It shines in the form of the One and of the many, like the radiance of the sun. ॥1॥
7.2.7.2: From her arose infinite powers, such as will, knowledge and action, and also Māyā and the rest, just as sparks arise from fire. ॥2॥
7.2.7.3: From her indeed arose Sadāśiva, Īśvara and the others, Vidyā, the Vidyeśvaras and the rest, the puruṣas, and Prakṛti, higher than the high. ॥3॥
7.2.7.4: The principles from Mahat down to the particular elements (viśeṣa), the forms beginning with Aja (Brahmā), and whatever else exists—all that is her effect; there is no doubt. ॥4॥
7.2.7.5: That Śakti is all-pervading, subtle, of the nature of awakened consciousness and bliss. The god Śiva, adorned with the moon, is called the possessor of Śakti. ॥5॥
7.2.7.6: Śiva is what is to be known; Śivā is knowledge, wisdom, śruti and smṛti. She is steadfastness, stability, firm abiding, and the powers of knowledge, will and action. ॥6॥
7.2.7.7: She is the command, the supreme Brahman, the two knowledges, higher and lower, pure knowledge and pure kalā—since everything is made by Śakti. ॥7॥
7.2.7.8: Māyā, Prakṛti, the individual soul, modification and transformation, the non-existent and the existent—whatever there is, all this is pervaded by her. ॥8॥
7.2.7.9: That goddess, by her Māyā, deludes the whole cosmic egg with its moving and unmoving beings without effort, and also releases it in play. ॥9॥
7.2.7.10: Together with her, who is of twenty-seven kinds, the Lord of all abides pervading the universe; therefore liberation here proceeds from him. ॥10॥
7.2.7.11: Long ago some sages, expounders of Brahman seeking liberation, their minds possessed by doubt, reflected on the truth as it is. ॥11॥
7.2.7.12: What is the cause? From where were we born? By what do we live? Where is our foundation? By whom are we governed? ॥12॥
7.2.7.13: By whom are we constantly kept in pleasures and in their opposites, ceaselessly? By whom was the inviolable order of the universe established? ॥13॥
7.2.7.14: Time, inherent nature, destiny, chance—these do not fit here; nor the elements, the womb, or the person; or is it a combination of these, or something beyond them? ॥14॥
7.2.7.15: Since time and the rest are insentient, and though the self is sentient, it experiences pleasures and pains because it is a created being and not a master—so it was pondered. ॥15॥
7.2.7.16: Following the yoga of meditation on that, they saw directly the Lord's power, which cuts the bonds, deeply hidden by its own qualities. ॥16॥
7.2.7.17: Their bonds cut by her, they beheld with divine sight Mahādeva, the possessor of Śakti, the cause of all causes. ॥17॥
7.2.7.18: He is the one who, immeasurable, by this power presides over all causes together with time and the self—who presides over everything. ॥18॥
7.2.7.19: Then, through grace, through the supreme yoga, and through the yoga of devotion they had perceived, they attained the divine goal. ॥19॥
7.2.7.20: Therefore, those who behold Śiva in the heart together with that Śakti have eternal peace, not others—so says the Śruti. ॥20॥
7.2.7.21: There is never any separation of the possessor of Śakti from Śakti. Therefore, because of the identity of Śakti and the possessor of Śakti, bliss comes from the two together. ॥21॥
7.2.7.22: Surely a sequence of knowledge and action is intended for liberation; yet when there is grace, that liberation rests in the palm of one's hand. ॥22॥
7.2.7.23: Whether a god or a demon, a beast or a bird, a parrot or even a worm—one is liberated by his grace. ॥23॥
7.2.7.24: Whether in the womb or being born, a child or a youth, old or dying, dwelling in heaven or in hell, ॥24॥
7.2.7.25: fallen or righteous, learned or foolish—when there is grace one is liberated that very instant; there is no doubt of this. ॥25॥
7.2.7.26: Out of compassion the Supreme Lord becomes gracious even to unworthy devotees, having removed their various impurities; there is no doubt. ॥26॥
7.2.7.27: That devotion arises from grace alone, and grace arises from devotion; discerning the difference of stages, the wise man is not confused about this. ॥27॥
7.2.7.28: This devotion, preceded by grace and bestowing enjoyment and liberation, cannot be attained by men in a single birth. ॥28॥
7.2.7.29: Maheśvara becomes gracious to those perfected over many births, who follow the Vedic and Smṛti rules, who are dispassionate and awakened. ॥29॥
7.2.7.30: When the Lord of gods is gracious, there arises in that bound soul a slight devotion, led by understanding: I have a Lord. ॥30॥
7.2.7.31: Then the man becomes engaged in austerity and various Śaiva duties; in performing them comes repeated practice of them, and from that supreme devotion arises. ॥31॥
7.2.7.32: By that supreme devotion supreme grace is obtained; from grace comes liberation from all bonds, and for the liberated one, bliss. ॥32॥
7.2.7.33: Even a mortal of slight devotion, after three births, will not be subject to the torment of the womb-machine; of this there is no doubt. ॥33॥
7.2.7.34: Service, whether with its auxiliary parts or without, is called devotion. It is further divided threefold according to its means: mind, speech and body. ॥34॥
7.2.7.35: Contemplation of Śiva's form and the like is known as mental service; japa and the like is verbal service; ritual worship and the like is bodily. ॥35॥
7.2.7.36: This service with three means is also called Śiva-dharma; and it has been declared fivefold by Śiva, the Supreme Self. ॥36॥
7.2.7.37: In brief: austerity, ritual action, japa, meditation and knowledge. Action is worship of the liṅga and the like; austerity is the Cāndrāyaṇa vow and the like. ॥37॥
7.2.7.38: Japa is the threefold repetition of the mantra of Śiva; meditation is contemplation of Śiva; and the knowledge taught in the Śaiva Āgamas is what is here called knowledge. ॥38॥
7.2.7.39: The Śivāgama was spoken by Śrīkaṇṭha Śiva to Śivā out of compassion for those who take refuge in Śiva; it is the sole means to the highest goods. ॥39॥
7.2.7.40: Therefore a wise man seeking the highest good should increase his devotion to Śiva, the supreme cause, and give up attachment to sense-objects. ॥40॥
7.2.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The account of the truth of Śiva, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
7.2.8.1: Kṛṣṇa said: O blessed one, I wish to hear the knowledge of Śiva, the essence of the Vedas, which Śiva himself expounded for the liberation of those who take refuge in him. ॥1॥
7.2.8.2: That knowledge is beyond the reach of non-devotees, the unintelligent and the undisciplined; it is endowed with five topics, is secret, and is reviled by the unwise. ॥2॥
7.2.8.3: In places it is contrary to the dharmas established for the varṇas and āśramas, in places in accord with them; it was drawn out in its entirety from the Veda with its six limbs, and from Sāṅkhya and Yoga. ॥3॥
7.2.8.4: It was spoken by the Supreme Lord, vast in extent, measuring a hundred crore verses by count of text. In it, how is the worship of the Lord to be performed? ॥4॥
7.2.8.5: Who is entitled to worship and the rest? How are the yoga of knowledge and the like practised? O you of good vows, please tell all that in full detail. ॥5॥
7.2.8.6: Upamanyu said: Condensing it, I shall tell the Śaiva doctrine, declared in the Veda and expounded by Śiva, free of praise, blame and the like, producing immediate conviction, ॥6॥
7.2.8.7: born of the guru's grace, divine, granting liberation without effort. I shall tell it briefly; its full extent cannot be told. ॥7॥
7.2.8.8: Long ago, with the desire to create, Śiva, the immovable Great Lord, the Master, endowed with real effect and cause, manifested himself from the Unmanifest. ॥8॥
7.2.8.9: And then the Lord, the seer surpassing the universe, generated Brahmā, the first god among the gods, the lord of sacred speech (brahmaṇaspati). ॥9॥
7.2.8.10: Brahmā, as he was being born, beheld the god, his father; and the progenitor god looked upon him being born, by his command. ॥10॥
7.2.8.11: Looked upon by Rudra, that god, the lord, created the universe, and he established the order of varṇas and āśramas, each separately. ॥11॥
7.2.8.12: He created Soma for the sake of sacrifice; from Soma were born heaven, earth, fire, the sun, sacrifice, Viṣṇu and the lord of Śacī (Indra). ॥12॥
7.2.8.13: They and other gods praised Rudra with the Rudrādhyāya; the Lord stood before the gods with a gracious face. ॥13॥
7.2.8.14: For the sake of his own play, the Great Lord took away their knowledge; then the gods, bewildered, asked him: Who are you? ॥14॥
7.2.8.15: The blessed Rudra said: I alone am the ancient one. I was in the very beginning, and I exist now, O best of gods, ॥15॥
7.2.8.16: and I shall be. There is no other apart from me. I alone satisfy the whole world with my own radiance. ॥16॥
7.2.8.17: There is none greater than or equal to me; he who knows me is liberated. Having said this, the blessed Rudra vanished right there. ॥17॥
7.2.8.18: Not seeing that Lord, praising him with Sāman chants, and performing the Pāśupata vow set forth in the Atharvaśiras, ॥18॥
7.2.8.19: the immortals then had all their limbs covered with ash. Then, to grant them grace, the Lord of creatures (paśupati), the Master, ॥19॥
7.2.8.20: the Lord, together with his attendants and with Umā, made himself present. Him whom yogins, sleepless, with breath mastered and sins burnt away, ॥20॥
7.2.8.21: see in the heart, that god the foremost of gods beheld. Her whom they call the supreme Power, following the Lord's will, ॥21॥
7.2.8.22: her, the lovely-eyed one, they saw at the left side of the Great Lord. Those who have shaken off saṃsāra and attained the supreme Śaiva state, ॥22॥
7.2.8.23: and those others who are eternally perfected—those lords of the gaṇas too were seen. Then the gods praised the Great Lord together with the Goddess ॥23॥
7.2.8.24: with divine hymns to Maheśvara, Vedic and also Purāṇic. The god with the bull-banner, looking at the gods with compassion, ॥24॥
7.2.8.25: well pleased, said in a voice naturally sweet, I am satisfied. Then the gods, bowing to the bull-bannered one whose mind was well pleased, reverently asked him this most worthy question: ॥25॥
7.2.8.26: The gods said: O blessed one, by what path are you to be worshipped on earth? Who is entitled to worship? Please tell us truly. ॥26॥
7.2.8.27: Then Hara, best of gods, glancing at the Goddess with a smile, revealed his own supreme, awesome form in the nature of the sun, ॥27॥
7.2.8.28: endowed with all sovereign qualities, supreme, consisting of all radiance, surrounded by powers, forms, limbs, planets and gods, ॥28॥
7.2.8.29: eight-armed, four-faced, wondrous, half-woman. Seeing this wondrous form, the gods led by Viṣṇu, ॥29॥
7.2.8.30: understood the god to be the sun and the Goddess the moon, and the rest as the five elements, and the moving and unmoving world as composed of that. ॥30॥
7.2.8.31: Having spoken thus, they offered him arghya and bowed to him: ॥31॥
7.2.8.32: To you, vermilion-hued, of beautiful disc, adorned with gold-coloured ornaments, lotus-eyed, holding a lotus, the cause of Brahmā, Indra and Nārāyaṇa— ॥32॥
7.2.8.33: accepting this excellent arghya offered to you, filled with fine gems, with golden water, rich with fine saffron and the like, with kuśa grass and flowers, together with a golden vessel—O Lord, be gracious. ॥33॥
7.2.8.34: Obeisance to you, Śiva, the peaceful, with your gaṇas, the first cause; to you who are Rudra, Viṣṇu and Brahmā, whose form is the sun. ॥34॥
7.2.8.35: Whoever, concentrated, worships Śiva in the solar disc and offers the excellent arghya at dawn, midday and evening, ॥35॥
7.2.8.36: or bows, or recites these verses that are the very mouth of the Veda—nothing is hard for him to obtain; if he is a devotee, he is surely liberated. ॥36॥
7.2.8.37: Therefore one should always worship Śiva in the form of the sun, with mind, deed and speech, for the sake of dharma, desire, wealth and liberation. ॥37॥
7.2.8.38: Then the Great Lord Hara, abiding in the disc, looking at the gods, gave them the scripture surpassing all Āgamas and vanished. ॥38॥
7.2.8.39: Knowing that in it the entitlement to worship belongs to brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas and vaiśyas, the gods bowed to the lord of gods and went back as they had come. ॥39॥
7.2.8.40: Then, after a long time, when that scripture had disappeared, Maheśvarī, seated on his lap, questioned her husband. ॥40॥
7.2.8.41: Urged by her, the Goddess, the God adorned with the moon raised his hand and spoke the scripture that surpasses all the Āgamas. ॥41॥
7.2.8.42: And at the command of Parameṣṭhin Brahmā it was propagated in the world by me, by the teacher Agastya, and by the great sage Dadhīca. ॥42॥
7.2.8.43: The trident-bearer himself, too, descending onto the earth in the successive cycles of the yugas, establishes a lineage of knowledge for the liberation of those who take refuge in him. ॥43॥
7.2.8.44: Ṛbhu, Satya, Bhārgava, Aṅgiras, Savitṛ, O twice-born ones; Mṛtyu, the wise Śatakratu, Vasiṣṭha the foremost of sages; ॥44॥
7.2.8.45: Sārasvata, Tridhāman, Trivṛta the foremost of sages, Śatatejas, and Dharma himself, known as Nārāyaṇa; ॥45॥
7.2.8.46: Svarakṣa, the wise Āruṇi, and likewise Kṛtañjaya; Māmateya, Bharadvāja, Gautama, the excellent seer; ॥46॥
7.2.8.47: Vācaḥsravas, a sage in person, likewise the pure Sūkṣmāyaṇi, the sage Tṛṇabindu, Kṛṣṇa, Śakti, and next Śākteya; ॥47॥
7.2.8.48: Jātūkarṇya, and Hari himself as the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana. Let you hear in order of these incarnations of Vyāsa, lords of yoga in the kalpa. ॥48॥
7.2.8.49: In the Liṅga Purāṇa, O you of good vows, are described the incarnations of Vyāsa at the ends of the Dvāpara ages, as well as the incarnations of the trident-bearer as yoga-teachers, and likewise among his disciples. ॥49॥
7.2.8.50: In each of these incarnations the Lord has four disciples of great vigour; and their disciples and their disciples' disciples number in hundreds and thousands. ॥50॥
7.2.8.51: By honouring them in the world, by carrying out the Śaiva injunctions and so on, the fortunate are liberated, as are those wholly imbued with devotion. ॥51॥
7.2.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The incarnations of Vyāsa, in the knowledge of the truth of Śiva, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
7.2.9.1: Kṛṣṇa said: O Lord, tell me of the incarnations of Śarva who, in all the cycles of the yugas, appeared in the guise of teachers of yoga, and also of his disciples. ॥1॥
7.2.9.2: Upamanyu said: Śveta, Sutāra, Madana, Suhotra and Kaṅka; Laugākṣi, Mahāmāya and likewise Jaigīṣavya; ॥2॥
7.2.9.3: Dadhivāha, Ṛṣabha, the sage Ugra, and Atri; Supālaka, Gautama, and likewise the sage Vedaśiras; ॥3॥
7.2.9.4: Gokarṇa, Guhāvāsin, and Śikhaṇḍin, who is remembered as another; Jaṭāmālin, Aṭṭahāsa, Dāruka and likewise Lāṅgulin; ॥4॥
7.2.9.5: Mahākāla, Śūlin, Daṇḍin and Muṇḍīśa; Sahiṣṇu, Somaśarman, and Lakulīśvara. ॥5॥
7.2.9.6: These, in this Vārāha kalpa, in the period of the seventh Manu, are the teachers of yoga, twenty-eight in number, appearing in the succession of the yugas. ॥6॥
7.2.9.7: Each of these has four disciples of tranquil mind, beginning with Śveta and ending with Ruṣya; I shall name them in order. ॥7॥
7.2.9.8: Śveta, Śvetaśikha, Śvetāśva and Śvetalohita; Dundubhi, Śatarūpa, Ṛcīka and likewise Ketumān; ॥8॥
7.2.9.9: Vikośa, Vikeśa, Vipāśa and Pāśanāśana; Sumukha, Durmukha, Durgama and Duratikrama; ॥9॥
7.2.9.10: Sanatkumāra, Sanaka, Sananda and Sanātana; Sudhāman, Virajas, Śaṅkha and Aṇḍaja; ॥10॥
7.2.9.11: Sārasvata, Megha, Meghavāha and Suvāhaka; Kapila, Āsuri, Pañcaśikha and Bāṣkala; ॥11॥
7.2.9.12: Parāśara, Garga, Bhārgava and likewise Aṅgiras; Balabandhu, Nirāmitra, Ketuśṛṅga and Tapodhana; ॥12॥
7.2.9.13: Lambodara, Lamba, Lambātman and Lambakeśaka; Sarvajña, Samabuddhi and likewise Sādhyasiddhi; ॥13॥
7.2.9.14: Sudhāman, Kaśyapa, Vasiṣṭha and likewise Virajas; Atri, Ugra, Guruśreṣṭha, then Śravana and Śraviṣṭaka; ॥14॥
7.2.9.15: Kuṇi, Kuṇibāhu, Kuśarīra and Kunetraka; Kāśyapa, Uśanas, Cyavana and Bṛhaspati; ॥15॥
7.2.9.16: Utathya, Vāmadeva, Mahākāla and Mahānila; Vācaḥśravas, Suvīra, Śyāvaka and Yatīśvara; ॥16॥
7.2.9.17: Hiraṇyanābha, Kauśalya, Lokākṣi and likewise Kuthumi; Sumantu, Jaimini, Kubandha and Kuśakandhara; ॥17॥
7.2.9.18: Plakṣa, Dārbhāyaṇi, Ketumān and likewise Gautama; Bhallavin, Madhupiṅga and likewise Śvetaketu; ॥18॥
7.2.9.19: Uśija, Bṛhadaśva, Devala and Kavi; Śālihotra, Suveṣa, Yuvanāśva and Śaradvasu; ॥19॥
7.2.9.20: Akṣapāda, Kaṇāda, Ulūka and Vatsa; Kulika, Garga, Mitraka and Ruṣya. ॥20॥
7.2.9.21: These are the disciples of Maheśa who appeared in the form of yoga-teachers; their number is one hundred together with twelve. ॥21॥
7.2.9.22: All are Pāśupatas, perfected ones, their bodies smeared with ash, knowers of the true meaning of all scriptures, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. ॥22॥
7.2.9.23: All delight in the Śaiva way of life and are devoted to the knowledge of Śiva; all are free from attachment, their minds attached to Śiva alone. ॥23॥
7.2.9.24: They are steadfast, enduring all pairs of opposites, delighting in the welfare of all beings; upright, gentle, self-possessed, having conquered anger and having conquered the senses. ॥24॥
7.2.9.25: Adorned with garlands of rudrākṣa, their foreheads marked with the tripuṇḍra; some with a tuft of matted hair, some wholly matted-haired, some without matted hair, some with shaven heads. ॥25॥
7.2.9.26: Living mostly on fruits and roots, devoted to breath-control (prāṇāyāma), filled with the sense of identity with Śiva, solely intent on meditation on Śiva; ॥26॥
7.2.9.27: they have utterly crushed the sprouting shoots of the poison-tree of saṃsāra, and are fully ready to depart for the supreme city of Śiva. ॥27॥
7.2.9.28: Whoever, regarding these as true preceptors, constantly worships Śiva, attains union (sāyujya) with Śiva; there need be no doubt about this. ॥28॥
7.2.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The yoga incarnations of Śiva, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
7.2.10.1: Kṛṣṇa said: O venerable one, chief of all yogins, lord of the gaṇas, lord of sages, equal in splendour to the six-faced Skanda, treasury of all knowledge, O teacher, ॥1॥
7.2.10.2: Most likely you, having descended upon the earth to cut asunder the bonds of men, abide here having assumed the body of a great sage, O supreme lord. ॥2॥
7.2.10.3: For otherwise, in this world, who other than you—be he a god or even a demon—could know the supreme state whose nature is Śiva? ॥3॥
7.2.10.4: Therefore, having drunk the nectar of Śiva-knowledge poured forth from your mouth, as if directly from the Pināka-bearer himself, my mind has not become satisfied. ॥4॥
7.2.10.5: O venerable one, what did the Supreme Goddess, seated on the lap of her husband, the very maker of all the worlds, ask her husband? ॥5॥
7.2.10.6: Upamanyu said: Fittingly have you asked, O Kṛṣṇa; I shall tell it exactly as it was to you, a devotee of Bhava, disciplined and of auspicious mind. ॥6॥
7.2.10.7: On the divine Mandara, the best of mountains, with its lovely caves, the divine Mahādeva, together with the Goddess, became absorbed in meditation. ॥7॥
7.2.10.8: Then the Goddess's dear friend Śubhāvatī, with a smiling face, brought blossoming, exceedingly lovely flowers. ॥8॥
7.2.10.9: Then Hara, the best of gods, having placed the Goddess on his own lap and adorned her with those flowers, sat there himself greatly delighted. ॥9॥
7.2.10.10: Then the goddesses who moved in the inner apartments, wearing divine ornaments, and the intimate chiefs of the gaṇas, served the Great Mistress of all worlds— ॥10॥
7.2.10.11: —and her husband, the all-complete Great Lord of all worlds; with fly-whisks in their hands they attended upon the Goddess and the God. ॥11॥
7.2.10.12: Then pleasing conversations took place, for the delight of the Great Lord and Lady and for the protection of those people in the world who have taken refuge in Śiva. ॥12॥
7.2.10.13: Then, seeing the opportunity, the Great Mistress of all worlds questioned her husband, the Great Lord of all worlds. ॥13॥
7.2.10.14: The Goddess said: By what means is Mahādeva brought under the control of mortals of dull mind, souls who are incapable of grasping the truth of the Self and the like, and whose selves are undisciplined? ॥14॥
7.2.10.15: Īśvara said: Not by ritual action, not by austerity, not by recitations, not by postures and the like, not by knowledge, nor by anything else am I brought under control without faith. ॥15॥
7.2.10.16: If people have faith in me, from whatever cause, I become controllable, touchable, visible, worshipable, and one who may be conversed with. ॥16॥
7.2.10.17: Therefore faith in me must be cultivated by one who wishes to bring me under control. The cause of faith here is the guarding of one's own dharma by those belonging to the varṇas. ॥17॥
7.2.10.18: Only the man who abides in the dharma of his own varṇa and āśrama comes to have faith in me, not anyone else. ॥18॥
7.2.10.19: The entire dharma of those in the āśramas here, established by the Veda, was formerly declared by Brahmā, preceded by my very command. ॥19॥
7.2.10.20: But that dharma of the Grandsire involves rites requiring much wealth; it is not abundant in ultimate fruit and is accompanied by hardship and toil. Through that great dharma, having obtained faith, which is very hard to gain— ॥20॥
7.2.10.21: —those of the varṇas who take refuge in me, with no other refuge, attain dharma, desire, wealth and liberation by an easy path. ॥21॥
7.2.10.22: The conduct of varṇa and āśrama has been arranged anew by me. In it, only my devotees among those of the varṇas— ॥22॥
7.2.10.23: —have eligibility, not others: this is my firm command. By the path thus commanded, those of the varṇas who take refuge in me— ॥23॥
7.2.10.24: —freed by my grace from the bonds of mala, māyā and the rest, having reached my supreme abode, from which return is hard, and having attained supreme likeness to me, have gone to bliss. ॥24॥
7.2.10.25: Therefore, whether one has obtained it or not, if he is my devotee, resorting to the varṇa-dharma declared by me, he should lift up himself by himself. ॥25॥
7.2.10.26: This is indeed a gain of what was not gained, greater by crores upon crores of times. Therefore one should practise the varṇa-dharma received from my own mouth. ॥26॥
7.2.10.27: For, O auspicious one, my incarnations exist in all the Manvantaras in the guise of yoga-teachers, O noble lady, and their lineages by the thousands. ॥27॥
7.2.10.28: For the undisciplined, the unintelligent and the undevoted, O Queen of gods, knowledge of this lineage is hard to obtain; therefore one should resort to it with effort. ॥28॥
7.2.10.29: That is loss, that is a great flaw, that is delusion, that is blindness and dumbness—that one, excluded from the path of liberation, should labour elsewhere. ॥29॥
7.2.10.30: Knowledge, ritual action, conduct and yoga—thus, O Queen of gods, my eternal dharma is declared to have four quarters. ॥30॥
7.2.10.31: Knowledge of paśu (the bound soul), pāśa (the bond) and pati (the Lord) is called jñāna. The purification of the six paths according to rule, dependent on the guru, is called kriyā. ॥31॥
7.2.10.32: The practice of the dharma of my worship and the like, enjoined according to varṇa and āśrama and prescribed by me alone, is called caryā. ॥32॥
7.2.10.33: The cessation of other mental activities in one whose mind is fixed on me, by the very path taught by me, is called yoga. ॥33॥
7.2.10.34: O Goddess, this purification of the mind is superior to a multitude of horse-sacrifices and also grants liberation; yet it is hard to attain for those who crave sense-objects. ॥34॥
7.2.10.35: Yoga, which removes former sins, is said to belong only to the dispassionate one who has conquered the group of senses through yama and niyama. ॥35॥
7.2.10.36: From dispassion knowledge arises; from knowledge yoga proceeds. ॥36॥
7.2.10.37: One who knows yoga, even if fallen, is liberated; there is no doubt about this. Compassion should be practised constantly, and non-violence, the gathering of knowledge, ॥37॥
7.2.10.38: truthfulness, non-stealing, belief in the scriptures, faith and control of the senses; teaching and study, sacrificing and officiating at sacrifices likewise; ॥38॥
7.2.10.39: meditation, contemplation of the Lord, and constant devotion to knowledge. The brāhmaṇa who conducts himself thus for the attainment of the yoga of knowledge— ॥39॥
7.2.10.40: —very soon, having gained realised knowledge, he attains yoga as well. O beloved, the knower, having burned this body in an instant with the fire of knowledge, the knower of yoga will cast off the bondage of karma through my grace. ॥40॥
7.2.10.41: Action that consists of merit and demerit is an obstacle to liberation. Therefore the yogin should, as a rule, give up both merit and demerit. ॥41॥
7.2.10.42: One is bound by performing action with desire for its fruit, not by the mere performance of action. Therefore one should give up the fruit of action. ॥42॥
7.2.10.43: O beloved, first, having fully worshipped me outwardly through the sacrifice of action, and having become devoted to the yoga of knowledge, one should afterwards practise yoga thoroughly. ॥43॥
7.2.10.44: Once my true nature is known, embodied beings who are yoked in yoga, to whom a clod, a stone and gold are alike, do not worship me through the sacrifice of action. ॥44॥
7.2.10.45: The excellent sage who is ever yoked, my devotee and composed, the yogin devoted to the yoga of knowledge, would attain union (sāyujya) with me. ॥45॥
7.2.10.46: But those members of the classes (varṇin) who have taken refuge in me yet whose minds are not free of attachment are entitled only to knowledge, conduct and ritual, being fit for these. ॥46॥
7.2.10.47: My worship should be known as twofold: external and internal. And by the distinction of speech, mind and body, they know my worship to be threefold. ॥47॥
7.2.10.48: Austerity, ritual action, repetition of mantra, meditation and knowledge, in that order: thus that same worship is again declared by the wise to be fivefold. ॥48॥
7.2.10.49: Worship of me and the like that is known to others is external; that same, when known only to oneself, is called internal. ॥49॥
7.2.10.50: The mind inclined towards me is called mind, not mere mind; speech devoted to my name is indeed regarded as speech, not any other. ॥50॥
7.2.10.51: The body marked with the signs prescribed by my teaching, such as the tripuṇḍra, and devoted to service of me, is truly a body, and no other. ॥51॥
7.2.10.52: Worship of me is to be known as action (karma); among external things, sacrifice and the like is not so called. Wasting the body for my sake is austerity; the kṛcchra penances and the like are not considered so. ॥52॥
7.2.10.53: Japa is the repeated practice of the five-syllabled mantra, and of the praṇava, and recitation of the Rudrādhyāya and the like, not the study of the Vedas and the like. ॥53॥
7.2.10.54: Meditation is contemplation of my form and the like, not absorptions on objects such as the self. Knowledge is understanding the meaning of my Āgamas, not knowing other subjects. ॥54॥
7.2.10.55: Whether in the external or the internal, wherever the mind finds delight owing to previous impressions, O Devī, one should practise steadfastness in that principle. ॥55॥
7.2.10.56: The internal is better than the external, a hundred times superior, because it is free from admixture and because faults, even visible ones, cannot arise in it. ॥56॥
7.2.10.57: One should know purity as internal; external cleanliness is not called purity, since one whose self is devoid of inner purity is impure even when outwardly pure. ॥57॥
7.2.10.58: Worship, both external and internal, must be preceded by heartfelt feeling (bhāva); O Devī, worship without feeling is solely a cause of deception. ॥58॥
7.2.10.59: What can men do for me, who have accomplished all and am pure? Whether external or internal, it is the feeling that is accepted by me. ॥59॥
7.2.10.60: O Devī, action whose sole essence is feeling, done by mind, deed and speech without ever expecting a fruit, is my eternal dharma. ॥60॥
7.2.10.61: O Ruler of the gods, refuge in me taken with a fruit in view is slight, since one who seeks fruit is capable of abandoning me when it is absent. ॥61॥
7.2.10.62: Yet even for a seeker of fruit whose mind is firmly set on me, I am the giver of fruit according to his feeling, O blameless one. ॥62॥
7.2.10.63: Those whose mind is inclined toward me without regard for fruit, even if they later pray for a fruit, they too are devotees dear to me. ॥63॥
7.2.10.64: Those who, solely by the force of former impressions, having considered fruit and no-fruit, helplessly take refuge in me, are held to be dearest to me. ॥64॥
7.2.10.65: For them there is truly no gain higher than gaining me; and for me too, O Supreme Goddess, there is no gain other than gaining them. ॥65॥
7.2.10.66: Through my grace, their feeling, offered to me, bestows the fruit, supreme nirvāṇa, as if by force. ॥66॥
7.2.10.67: They declare eightfold the marks of those great souls, devoted to none other, whose minds are surrendered to me, and who are qualified for my dharma. ॥67॥
7.2.10.68: Affection for my devotees, rejoicing in my worship, worshipping me oneself, and bodily exertion for my sake; ॥68॥
7.2.10.69: devotion in hearing my stories, changes in voice, eyes and limbs from emotion, constant remembrance of me, and being one who lives depending on me; ॥69॥
7.2.10.70: In whomever this eightfold sign is found, even in a mleccha, he is the foremost of brāhmaṇas, a sage, glorious; he is an ascetic, and he is a learned man. ॥70॥
7.2.10.71: A knower of the four Vedas is not thereby dear to me; but one who is my devotee, even a dog-eater, to him one should give, from him one may receive, and he is to be honoured just as I am. ॥71॥
7.2.10.72: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I am not lost to him, and he is not lost to me. ॥72॥
7.2.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named Devotion to Śiva, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
7.2.11.1: Īśvara said: Now, O Ruler of the gods, I shall tell in brief the duties of the classes (varṇa-dharma) for the devotees who are qualified, learned, and foremost among the twice-born. ॥1॥
7.2.11.2: Bathing three times a day, the fire-rite, worship of the liṅga in due order, giving, an attitude of devotion towards the Lord, compassion everywhere and at all times, ॥2॥
7.2.11.3: truthfulness, contentment, faith in the scriptures, non-violence towards all creatures, modesty, reverent trust, study, yoga, and constant teaching, ॥3॥
7.2.11.4: exposition, celibacy, listening to scripture, austerity, forbearance, purity, the tuft of hair and sacred thread, the turban and the upper garment, ॥4॥
7.2.11.5: not resorting to what is forbidden, wearing ashes and rudrākṣa beads, worship on the festival days, O Goddess, especially on the fourteenth lunar day, ॥5॥
7.2.11.6: drinking the brahmakūrca every month according to rule, and especially worshipping me after bathing me with that very mixture, O beloved, ॥6॥
7.2.11.7: complete renunciation of food from all sorts of rites, avoidance of food from ancestral offerings (śrāddha), likewise of stale food, and especially of barley-gruel, ॥7॥
7.2.11.8: and avoidance of liquor, of what smells of liquor, and of food-offerings — this is common to all classes, and especially binding on brāhmaṇas. ॥8॥
7.2.11.9: Forbearance, tranquillity, contentment, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, knowledge of me, dispassion, the use of ashes, ॥9॥
7.2.11.10: and withdrawal from all attachment — these ten are especially the marks of yogins; further, eating alms-food by day. ॥10॥
7.2.11.11: This is held to be the same for those in the forest-dweller stage. No food is to be eaten at night by any of the celibate students. ॥11॥
7.2.11.12: Teaching and officiating at sacrifices are not prescribed by me here for the kṣatriya, and especially not for the vaiśya; for them there is non-acceptance of gifts. ॥12॥
7.2.11.13: Protection of all classes, slaying of enemies in battle, and the destruction of harmful birds and beasts and of wicked men, ॥13॥
7.2.11.14: distrust everywhere but trust in my yogins, union with women at the proper times, and the guarding of the army, ॥14॥
7.2.11.15: knowing the affairs of the world through spies constantly sent about, always bearing weapons, and wearing ashes as armour — ॥15॥
7.2.11.16: this is the summary of duty for kings who abide in my way of life. Tending cattle, trade and agriculture are declared the duties of the vaiśya. ॥16॥
7.2.11.17: Service to the other classes is declared the duty of the śūdra, as well as making gardens and resorting to my sacred places. ॥17॥
7.2.11.18: For the householder, going only to his lawful wife is prescribed; celibacy for forest-dwellers, ascetics and students. ॥18॥
7.2.11.19: For women, service to the husband is the eternal duty, no other; and, O auspicious one, worship of me too, if there is the husband's permission. ॥19॥
7.2.11.20: The woman who abandons service to her husband and is intent on vows — that woman goes to hell; there need be no doubt about this. ॥20॥
7.2.11.21: Now I shall tell the eternal duty of a woman bereft of her husband: vows, giving, austerity, purity, sleeping on the ground, eating only at night, ॥21॥
7.2.11.22: celibacy, constant bathing with ashes or with water, tranquillity, silence, forbearance, and regular sharing of food according to rule, ॥22॥
7.2.11.23: fasting according to rule on the eighth and fourteenth days, especially on the full-moon day, and on the eleventh, and worship of me. ॥23॥
7.2.11.24: Thus, O Goddess, has been told by me in brief the duty of those who follow the stages of life — of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas and vaiśyas, of ascetics and of students, ॥24॥
7.2.11.25: likewise of forest-dwellers and householders, O beautiful one, and of śūdras and women: this is the eternal dharma. ॥25॥
7.2.11.26: I am to be meditated upon by you, O Ruler of the gods; the six-syllable mantra is always to be repeated; and the entire dharma taught in the Veda is to be observed — this is the summary of the meaning of dharma. ॥26॥
7.2.11.27: Now, those men in the world who have taken a body by their own will, who are endowed with intense devotion and joined with impressions from former lives — ॥27॥
7.2.11.28: whether detached from or attached even to the objects of sense such as women, they are not stained by sins, as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water. ॥28॥
7.2.11.29: For those pure, discerning ones who possess knowledge of me as the Self and are purified by my grace, the maintaining of the āśrama rules is merely a burden. ॥29॥
7.2.11.30: For them, as for me, there is nothing to be done or not done, no samādhi or ultimate resort, no injunction and no prohibition. ॥30॥
7.2.11.31: Just as here for me, who am wholly complete, nothing remains to be achieved, so too for them who have accomplished their purpose — there is no doubt. ॥31॥
7.2.11.32: They are Rudras who, having come down from Rudra's world, have assumed human state for the benefit of my devotees; there is no doubt of this. ॥32॥
7.2.11.33: Just as my command sets Brahmā and the others in motion, so their direction sets other men in motion. ॥33॥
7.2.11.34: Because they are the bearers of my command, and through the excess of their true devotion, by merely beholding me in them the destruction of all sins comes about. ॥34॥
