7.2.11.35: And for men devoted to me there arise signs indicating excellent fruit, which reveal matters not seen before. ॥35॥
7.2.11.36: Trembling and sweating, shedding of tears, faltering of the voice in the throat, and the experience of bliss and the like may occur suddenly and repeatedly. ॥36॥
7.2.11.37: By these unfailing signs, singly or all together, and by states of feeling mild, middling or intense, those best of men are to be recognised. ॥37॥
7.2.11.38: Just as iron, through being pervaded by fire, is no longer mere iron, so through my presence they are not mere humans. ॥38॥
7.2.11.39: A wise man should not despise these Rudras bearing mortal bodies, thinking them to be ordinary men because of their likeness in hands, feet and so on. ॥39॥
7.2.11.40: Contempt shown towards them by men of deluded mind takes away life, fortune, family and good character, and brings hell. ॥40॥
7.2.11.41: For the great souls who have been lifted up and who depend on nothing other than me, even the position of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the Lord of the gods Indra becomes as light and worthless as cotton. ॥41॥
7.2.11.42: The lordship belonging to the lords of the guṇas — whether pertaining to buddhi, to prakṛti, or likewise to puruṣa — is impure; therefore it is to be abandoned by those who seek the state beyond the guṇas. ॥42॥
7.2.11.43: Now, what is the use of saying much? The sole means for attaining the highest good is the attachment of the mind to me, by whatever cause it may arise. ॥43॥
7.2.11.44: Upamanyu said: Thus, by Śiva, the lord Śrīkaṇṭha, the Supreme Self, this compendium of the essential meaning of knowledge was spoken for the welfare of the worlds. ॥44॥
7.2.11.45: The Vedas and śāstras in their entirety, together with the itihāsas and purāṇas, and all the sciences, are an elaborate exposition of this compendium of knowledge. ॥45॥
7.2.11.46: Knowledge, the knowable, what is to be practised, eligibility, the means, and the goal — because it is a compendium of these six topics, this is called the Compendium. ॥46॥
7.2.11.47: Knowledge is that which is imparted under the authority of the guru; the knowable is the bond (pāśa), the bound soul (paśu) and the Lord (pati); what is to be practised is the worship of the liṅga and the like; and the eligible one is whoever is a devotee. ॥47॥
7.2.11.48: The means is Śiva's mantra and the like; the goal is equality with Śiva. From knowing this compendium of six topics, omniscience is said to arise. ॥48॥
7.2.11.49: First, having worshipped Śiva externally with devotion through ritual sacrifice and the like, according to one's means, one should afterwards become devoted to internal worship. ॥49॥
7.2.11.50: He whose delight, owing to the weight of his merit, is in the inner worship and not in the outer — for that great soul no external rite need be performed. ॥50॥
7.2.11.51: For one who is satisfied with the nectar of knowledge, a Śaiva whose self has become Śiva through devotion, there is never, O Kṛṣṇa, any duty, either inward or outward. ॥51॥
7.2.11.52: Therefore, having gradually given up the external and likewise the internal, and having beheld the knowable through knowledge, one should give up knowledge as well. ॥52॥
7.2.11.53: If the mind is not one-pointed on Śiva, what is gained by action, even when performed? If the mind is indeed one-pointed, what need is there of action, even when performed? ॥53॥
7.2.11.54: Therefore, whether without performing rites or performing them in sequence, internal and external, by whatever means, one should fix the mind on Śiva. ॥54॥
7.2.11.55: For the good whose minds are fixed on Śiva and whose intellects are firmly established, there is supreme bliss here and hereafter — everywhere. ॥55॥
7.2.11.56: Here, through this mantra Om namaḥ Śivāya, come the accomplishments; therefore it should be mastered for prosperity both higher and lower. ॥56॥
7.2.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The knowledge of Śiva, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
7.2.12.1: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O best of great sages, O all-knowing one, O great ocean of all knowledge, I wish to hear, as it truly is, the greatness of the five-syllabled mantra. ॥1॥
7.2.12.2: Upamanyu said: The greatness of the five-syllabled mantra cannot be told in full even in hundreds of crores of years; therefore hear it in brief. ॥2॥
7.2.12.3: In the Veda and in the Śiva-Āgama, in both, this six-syllabled mantra is the accomplisher of every aim for all devotees of Śiva. ॥3॥
7.2.12.4: That utterance, consisting of Śiva, has few syllables yet is rich in meaning; it is the essence of the Veda, the giver of liberation, established by Śiva's command, and free from doubt. ॥4॥
7.2.12.5: That utterance of the Supreme Lord is endowed with manifold powers (siddhi), divine, delighting the minds of people, of well-ascertained meaning, and profound. ॥5॥
7.2.12.6: For the accomplishment of every aim of all embodied beings, the Omniscient One proclaimed the mantra oṃ namaḥ śivāya, easy for the mouth to pronounce. ॥6॥
7.2.12.7: That primordial six-syllabled mantra is the seed of all knowledge; it should be understood as extremely subtle yet of great meaning, like the seed of the banyan tree. ॥7॥
7.2.12.8: The God beyond the three guṇas, omniscient, maker of all, the Lord, the all-pervading Śiva, abides in the one-syllabled mantra Om. ॥8॥
7.2.12.9: The subtle one-syllabled Brahmans, Īśāna and the rest, are established in due order in the mantra namaḥ śivāya. In the subtle six-syllabled mantra Śiva has the five Brahmans as his body. ॥9॥
7.2.12.10: He abides in it directly and by his own nature through the relation of the denoted and the denoting. Śiva, being immeasurable, is the denoted; the mantra is held to be that which denotes him. ॥10॥
7.2.12.11: This relation of denoted and denoter between the two is beginningless, just as this terrible ocean of saṃsāra has been proceeding without beginning. ॥11॥
7.2.12.12: So too Śiva, beginningless, stands as the liberator from saṃsāra. Just as medicine is by its nature the counteragent of diseases, ॥12॥
7.2.12.13: so Śiva is held to be the counteragent of the ills of saṃsāra. If this Lord of the world did not exist, this universe would be mere darkness, ॥13॥
7.2.12.14: because Prakṛti is insentient and the soul (puruṣa) is ignorant. Whatever is insentient—Pradhāna, atoms and the like— ॥14॥
7.2.12.15: is not seen to be an agent by itself without an intelligent cause. And the teaching of dharma and adharma, bondage and liberation, as established by reflection, ॥15॥
7.2.12.16: and the first creation of souls do not come about without an omniscient one—just as the sick, joyless, suffer without a physician. ॥16॥
7.2.12.17: Therefore there exists a beginningless, omniscient, all-complete Sadāśiva, the Lord, the rescuer of souls from the ocean of saṃsāra. ॥17॥
7.2.12.18: Free from beginning, middle and end, naturally pure, the Lord, omniscient and all-complete—thus is Śiva to be known in the Śiva-Āgama. ॥18॥
7.2.12.19: This mantra is his name, and he is held to be what it names. Because of this relation of name and named, the mantra is established as the supreme Śiva himself. ॥19॥
7.2.12.20: This much indeed is the knowledge of Śiva, this much the supreme state: the six-syllabled utterance of Śiva, oṃ namaḥ śivāya. ॥20॥
7.2.12.21: This Śaiva utterance, of the nature of Śiva, is an injunction, not mere eulogy (arthavāda). Śiva, who is omniscient, entirely complete and naturally pure, ॥21॥
7.2.12.22: and the bestower of grace on the worlds—how could he speak of what is false? A thing as it really stands, with its merits and faults by its nature, ॥22॥
7.2.12.23: and its fruit in full, as far as it extends—so the Omniscient One would declare it. Only one who is seized by faults such as passion and ignorance would speak falsehood. ॥23॥
7.2.12.24: Those two faults do not exist in the Lord; how then could he speak otherwise? The stainless utterance composed by the omniscient Śiva, who knows no fault whatsoever, is authoritative—there is no doubt. ॥24॥
7.2.12.25: Therefore the words of the Lord are to be trusted by the wise regarding the true nature of merit and sin; one who lacks faith in them goes downward. ॥25॥
7.2.12.26: Whatever most excellent words are spoken by tranquil great sages for the attainment of heaven and liberation should be known as well-spoken (subhāṣita). ॥26॥
7.2.12.27: Speech that follows passion, hatred, falsehood, anger, lust and craving is called ill-spoken, because it is a cause of hell. ॥27॥
7.2.12.28: What use is speech, even if refined (saṃskṛta), soft or charming, if it is born of ignorance and passion and causes the afflictions of saṃsāra? ॥28॥
7.2.12.29: Speech by hearing which good arises and passion and the rest are destroyed should be known as beautiful, even if it is ill-formed. ॥29॥
7.2.12.30: Though mantras are many, nowhere is there any equal to the stainless mantra composed by the omniscient Śiva. ॥30॥
7.2.12.31: The Vedas and śāstras together with their auxiliaries are contained in the six-syllabled mantra; therefore there is no other mantra anywhere equal to it. ॥31॥
7.2.12.32: The six-syllabled mantra is diversified in many ways into seven crore great mantras and subsidiary mantras, as a sūtra is unfolded in the form of its commentary (vṛtti). ॥32॥
7.2.12.33: All the teachings on Śiva and all the fields of knowledge are, in brief, a commentary (bhāṣya) on the six-syllabled sūtra. ॥33॥
7.2.12.34: What need has he of many mantras or of very extensive scriptures, in whose heart this mantra oṃ namaḥ śivāya is established? ॥34॥
7.2.12.35: He who has made firm the practice of the mantra oṃ namaḥ śivāya has studied, has heard, has done everything and performed every rite. ॥35॥
7.2.12.36: He on the tip of whose tongue the three syllables śivāya, joined with namaḥ and the rest, abide—his life is fruitful. ॥36॥
7.2.12.37: Whether an outcaste or a base person, a fool or a learned man, one who is devoted to japa of the five-syllabled mantra is freed from the cage of sin. ॥37॥
7.2.12.38: Thus it was spoken by the Supreme Lord, the trident-bearer, when asked by the Goddess, for the welfare of all mortals, and especially of the twice-born. ॥38॥
7.2.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The greatness of the five-syllabled mantra, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
7.2.13.1: The Goddess said: In the Kali age, when time is defiled, hard to conquer and hard to overcome, when the world is shrouded in the darkness of unrighteousness and has turned its face away from dharma, ॥1॥
7.2.13.2: when the conduct of the varṇas and āśramas has dwindled, when calamity has arrived, when all eligibility for rites is doubtful, or when its reversal is certain, ॥2॥
7.2.13.3: then, when instruction is obstructed and the succession of teacher and disciple has vanished — by what means are your devotees liberated, O Maheśvara? ॥3॥
7.2.13.4: Īśvara said: Taking refuge in my supreme, heart-pleasing five-syllabled vidyā, and with their minds purified by devotion, the men born in Kali are liberated. ॥4॥
7.2.13.5: Even for those tainted by faults of mind, speech and body beyond telling or remembering, for the ungrateful, the slanderers, the deceitful, ॥5॥
7.2.13.6: the greedy and the crooked-minded — if their hearts incline toward me, my five-syllabled vidyā carries them across the fear of saṃsāra. ॥6॥
7.2.13.7: Thus, O Devī, I have vowed again and again on earth: even a fallen devotee of mine would be liberated by this vidyā. ॥7॥
7.2.13.8: The Goddess said: If a mortal has fallen entirely, he becomes unfit for rites; and a rite performed by one unfit leads indeed to hell. How then would a fallen one be liberated by this vidyā? ॥8॥
7.2.13.9: Īśvara said: What you have said is true; yet listen, O beautiful one, to that which I formerly kept hidden, regarding it as a secret. ॥9॥
7.2.13.10: If a fallen man, deluded, worships me with mantras other than my five-syllabled mantra, he would undoubtedly go to hell. ॥10॥
7.2.13.11: Those who live on water, those who live on air, and others emaciated by vows — by these vows they do not attain union with my world. ॥11॥
7.2.13.12: But whoever worships me even once with devotion through the five-syllabled mantra alone, he too would reach my abode, solely by the greatness of this mantra. ॥12॥
7.2.13.13: Therefore austerities, sacrifices, vows and observances — these are not equal even to a ten-millionth part of worship with the five-syllabled mantra. ॥13॥
7.2.13.14: Whether bound or freed from the noose, whoever worships me with the five-syllabled mantra would be liberated; there is no need for deliberation here. ॥14॥
7.2.13.15: Whether without Rudra-initiation or with it, fallen or foolish, the man who worships me even once with the five-syllabled mantra is liberated. ॥15॥
7.2.13.16: O Devī, if one worships me with devotion with the six-syllabled or likewise the five-syllabled mantra, together with the brahma- and aṅga-mantras, he is liberated. ॥16॥
7.2.13.17: Fallen or not fallen, my devotee who has conquered anger should worship me with this mantra, whether he has received it from a guru or not. ॥17॥
7.2.13.18: Yet here, one who has received it is countless millions of times superior to one who has not. Therefore, O Devī, having received it, one should worship me with this mantra. ॥18॥
7.2.13.19: But he who, having received it, worships me fully with devotion, endowed with friendliness and other virtues and devoted to celibacy, would attain likeness to me. ॥19॥
7.2.13.20: What need to say more here? All devotees are eligible for my five-syllabled mantra; therefore it is indeed the most excellent. ॥20॥
7.2.13.21: By the power of the five-syllabled mantra the worlds, the Vedas, the great sages, the eternal dharmas, the gods and this entire universe endure. ॥21॥
7.2.13.22: When dissolution arrives and all moving and unmoving beings perish, everything, having entered into Prakṛti, will dissolve there. ॥22॥
7.2.13.23: I alone remain, O Devī; there is no second anywhere. Then the Vedas and all the śāstras abide in the five-syllabled mantra. ॥23॥
7.2.13.24: They do not perish at all, being protected by my power. Then creation arose from me through the differentiation of Prakṛti and the selves, ॥24॥
7.2.13.25: and of those whose selves are the embodiments of the guṇas; then came an intermediate dissolution. At that time the god Nārāyaṇa sleeps, having assumed a body made of māyā, ॥25॥
7.2.13.26: resting on the serpent-couch amid the waters. From the lotus of his navel was born the five-faced Grandfather Brahmā. ॥26॥
7.2.13.27: Desiring to create the three worlds but unable, being without helpers, he first created ten mind-born sages of immeasurable vigour. ॥27॥
7.2.13.28: For the increase of their accomplishment, the Grandfather said to me: O Mahādeva, O Maheśvara, grant power to my sons. ॥28॥
7.2.13.29: Thus entreated by him, I, bearing five faces, uttered the five syllables in order to the lotus-born Brahmā. ॥29॥
7.2.13.30: Receiving them with his five mouths, that Grandfather of the worlds came to know me, Maheśvara, through the relation of the signified and the signifier. ॥30॥
7.2.13.31: Having learned its application according to rule, Prajāpati, the mantra now perfected in him, gave the mantra and its true meaning to his sons. ॥31॥
7.2.13.32: And they, having received that jewel of mantras directly from the Grandfather of the worlds, desiring to worship me by the path he had enjoined, ॥32॥
7.2.13.33: — on a lovely peak of Meru is a mountain named Muñjavān, splendid, ever dear to me, always guarded by my devotees — ॥33॥
7.2.13.34: near it, eager to create the world, they performed intense austerity for a thousand divine years, living on air. ॥34॥
7.2.13.35: Seeing their devotion, I at once became visible to them; the ṛṣi, metre, kīlaka, bīja, śakti and deity of the mantra, ॥35॥
7.2.13.36: the nyāsa, the six limbs, the binding of the directions and the application — all of it I declared to those noble ones for the growth of the world's creation. ॥36॥
7.2.13.37: Then those sages, strengthened by austerity through the greatness of the mantra, duly spread out creation, with gods, asuras and humans. ॥37॥
7.2.13.38: Now the form of this supreme vidyā is told: first namaḥ should be uttered, and after that śivāya. ॥38॥
7.2.13.39: This is that five-syllabled vidyā, abiding at the crown of all the Śrutis, the eternal seed of everything that is born. ॥39॥
7.2.13.40: First issued from my mouth, she is the very expression denoting me; in form she shines like heated gold, with full, high breasts. ॥40॥
7.2.13.41: She is four-armed and three-eyed, with the young moon as her crest. She holds a lotus and a blue water-lily in her hands. She is gentle, and her hands show the gestures of granting boons and dispelling fear. ॥41॥
7.2.13.42: She is endowed with all auspicious marks and adorned with every ornament. She is seated on a white lotus seat, and her hair is dark and curly. ॥42॥
7.2.13.43: Her five syllables are of five kinds of colour, each with a radiating circle of rays: yellow, black, smoky, golden, and red. ॥43॥
7.2.13.44: If these are to be used separately, they are adorned with bindu and nāda. The bindu resembles a half-moon, and the nāda has the shape of a lamp-flame. ॥44॥
7.2.13.45: O fair-faced one, the second syllable is the bīja among the seeds of this mantra. One should declare the fifth, together with the fourth preceded by a long vowel, to be the śakti. ॥45॥
7.2.13.46: Vāmadeva is said to be the seer, and paṅkti the metre. The deity of this mantra, O fair-faced one, is I, Śiva, myself. ॥46॥
7.2.13.47: O lovely-hipped one, Gautama, Atri, Viśvāmitra, Aṅgiras, and Bharadvāja are held to be the seers of the syllables, in order. ॥47॥
7.2.13.48: Gāyatrī, anuṣṭubh, triṣṭubh, bṛhatī, and virāṭ are the metres, and Indra, Rudra, Hari, Brahmā, and Skanda are their deities. ॥48॥
7.2.13.49: O fair-faced one, they declare my five faces to be their places, from the eastern face up to the upper one, beginning with na, in due order. ॥49॥
7.2.13.50: The first syllable and the fourth are udātta; the second and the fifth are svarita; and the third is held to be nihita (low-pitched). ॥50॥
7.2.13.51: One should know its names as Mūlavidyā, Śiva, Śaiva, Sūtra, and Pañcākṣara. It is my great Śaiva heart. ॥51॥
7.2.13.52: The syllable na is called the head, ma is called the crest-lock, śi likewise the armour, and va is called the eye. ॥52॥
7.2.13.53: The syllable ya is the weapon. When namaḥ, svāhā, vaṣaṭ, huṃ, vauṣaṭ, and also phaṭ are added at the end of the syllables, then they become limbs (aṅga). ॥53॥
7.2.13.54: Even there, this is the root mantra, through combination with a slight difference; and there too the fifth syllable is adorned with the twelve vowels. ॥54॥
7.2.13.55: Therefore, with this mantra, by way of mind, speech, and body, one should perform the worship of us two, and likewise japa, homa, and the rest. ॥55॥
7.2.13.56: According to one's understanding, according to the time, according to scripture, according to one's mind, according to one's capacity, according to one's means, according to propriety, and according to one's delight — ॥56॥
7.2.13.57: — whenever it is done with devotion, wherever it is done, and by whomever it is done, O Devī, worship will lead to liberation. ॥57॥
7.2.13.58: Whatever is done with a mind attached to me, O beautiful one, is dear to me and auspicious, whether done in proper order or out of order. ॥58॥
7.2.13.59: Even so, for those devotees of mine who are not utterly helpless, I myself have laid down the rules in all the scriptures. ॥59॥
7.2.13.60: There, first, I shall explain the auspicious receiving of the mantra, without which japa is fruitless, and by which it becomes fruitful. ॥60॥
7.2.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the five-syllabled mantra, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
7.2.14.1: Īśvara said: O fair-faced one, mantra-repetition that lacks the guru's sanction, lacks the prescribed rites, lacks faith, and lacks the fee offered for the sanction is fruitless, even if it is repeated constantly. ॥1॥
7.2.14.2: A mantra perfected through sanction, perfected through rites, perfected through faith, is of my very nature; if it is thus accompanied by the fee as well, there is success in the mantra, bearing great fruit. ॥2॥
7.2.14.3: Having approached a guru—a brāhmaṇa preceptor who knows the truth, who practises japa, is endowed with good qualities, and is devoted to meditation and yoga— ॥3॥
7.2.14.4: one should, endowed with purity of disposition, strive to please him by speech, by mind, by body, and by wealth. ॥4॥
7.2.14.5: The brāhmaṇa should always worship the preceptor with the utmost effort. Elephants, horses, chariots, jewels, fields and houses, ॥5॥
7.2.14.6: ornaments, garments, grains and riches—these one should give to the guru with devotion, when one has the means. ॥6॥
7.2.14.7: If one desires success for oneself, one should not be miserly with wealth. Afterwards, having offered one's own self to the guru together with one's belongings, ॥7॥
7.2.14.8: having thus worshipped him properly according to one's capacity, without deceiving, one should receive from the guru the mantra and also knowledge, in due order. ॥8॥
7.2.14.9: The guru, thus pleased, taking the disciple—who is a worshipper, has dwelt with him for a year, is eager to serve, free of ego, bathed, pure and fasting— ॥9॥
7.2.14.10: having bathed him for purification with ghee from a full pot, and with water purified by mantras and mixed with sacred substances, ॥10॥
7.2.14.11: having adorned the well-dressed disciple with fragrances, garlands, garments and ornaments, having had the auspicious-day blessing (puṇyāha) recited, and having honoured the brāhmaṇas, ॥11॥
7.2.14.12: on a seashore, by a river, in a cow-pen, or in a temple, or in a clean place or a house, at a time conducive to success, on a suitable lunar day, ॥12॥
7.2.14.13: under a constellation and an auspicious yoga free from all defects—then, bestowing grace, he should impart my knowledge according to rule. ॥13॥
7.2.14.14: In a secluded place, with a very serene mind, he should pronounce it correctly with proper intonation; having uttered it and made the disciple utter that supreme mantra of us two, ॥14॥
7.2.14.15: saying, may it be propitious, may it be auspicious, may it be splendid, may it be dear—thus the guru should give the mantra, and after that the sanction too. ॥15॥
7.2.14.16: Having thus received the mantra and the sanction from the guru, the disciple, composed, having made the formal resolve, should repeat it daily, beginning with the preliminary observance (puraścaraṇa). ॥16॥
7.2.14.17: As long as he lives he should repeat it daily one thousand and eight times; becoming single-minded and devoted to it, he attains the supreme state. ॥17॥
7.2.14.18: One who, eating only at night and self-restrained, reverently repeats the mantra a lakh times for each syllable, multiplied by four, is known as a performer of puraścaraṇa. ॥18॥
7.2.14.19: He who, having performed the puraścaraṇa, then becomes a daily reciter—there is none equal to him in the world; he becomes perfected and a bestower of perfection. ॥19॥
7.2.14.20: Having bathed, having fixed a pleasing seat in a clean place, having contemplated me together with you in the heart, and then having contemplated one's own guru, ॥20॥
7.2.14.21: facing north or east, silent and with one-pointed mind, having purified the five elements by burning, flooding and the like, ॥21॥
7.2.14.22: having performed the mantra-placements (nyāsa) and so on, his body made fruitful thereby, meditating on the forms of us two and restraining the prāṇa and apāna breaths, ॥22॥
7.2.14.23: remembering the seat of the mantra, its own form, its seer, metre, presiding deity, seed-syllable, power, and also its sentence, one should repeat the five-syllabled mantra. ॥23॥
7.2.14.24: Those versed in the meaning of the Āgamas declare mental repetition to be the highest, whispered repetition the middling, and verbal audible repetition the lowest. ॥24॥
7.2.14.25: In order, they say, the highest has Rudra as its deity, the middling has Viṣṇu as its deity, and the lowest has Brahmā as its deity. ॥25॥
7.2.14.26: When one utters the mantra with the voice, with high, low and circumflex accents, its words and syllables distinct or indistinct, this is known as verbal japa. ॥26॥
7.2.14.27: That which is uttered slightly by mere movement of the tongue, unheard by others or heard only a little, is called whispered (upāṃśu). ॥27॥
7.2.14.28: The repeated contemplation by the intellect of sound and meaning along the series of syllables, from letter to letter and word to word, is called mental japa. ॥28॥
7.2.14.29: Verbal japa counts as only one; whispered is said to be worth a hundred; mental is declared worth a thousand; and the sagarbha japa is a hundred times more. ॥29॥
7.2.14.30: Japa joined with breath-control is called sagarbha. Even breath-control without japa (agarbha) is praised at the beginning and end. ॥30॥
7.2.14.31: Restraining the breaths, the wise one who knows the mantra's meaning should recollect the mantra forty times; one unable to do so should repeat it according to capacity. ॥31॥
7.2.14.32: One should perform breath-control five times, three times, or once, either agarbha or sagarbha; of these, the sagarbha is commended. ॥32॥
7.2.14.33: Japa accompanied by meditation is said to be a thousand times greater even than the sagarbha. Of these five kinds, one japa should be performed according to one's capacity. ॥33॥
7.2.14.34: Counting japa on the fingers is thus declared to yield a single measure; one should know counting by the lines of the fingers to be eightfold, and with putrajīva seeds tenfold more. ॥34॥
7.2.14.35: With conch-shell beads it is a hundredfold, with coral a thousandfold, with crystal ten-thousandfold, and with pearls it is said to be a hundred-thousandfold. ॥35॥
7.2.14.36: With lotus-seeds it is a millionfold, and with gold beads it is said to be ten millionfold; with a knot of kuśa grass and with rudrākṣa beads it becomes infinitely multiplied. ॥36॥
7.2.14.37: In the practice of japa, a rosary made of thirty beads gives wealth; one of twenty-seven beads bestows nourishment. ॥37॥
7.2.14.38: One made of twenty-five beads grants liberation; with fifteen beads it yields the fruits of hostile magic (abhicāra). ॥38॥
7.2.14.39: One should know the thumb as granting liberation, the index finger as destroying enemies, the middle finger as giving wealth; and this ring finger brings peace. ॥39॥
7.2.14.40: Among these, a rosary of one hundred and eight beads is the very best; a rosary numbering one hundred is excellent, and one of fifty is middling. ॥40॥
7.2.14.41: A rosary of fifty-four beads is declared to be excellent and dear to the heart. With such a rosary one should perform japa, and should not show it to anyone. ॥41॥
7.2.14.42: The little finger is said to be kṣariṇī, causing the merit to leak away; the others are auspicious in the act of japa. One should count the japa with the thumb together with the other fingers. ॥42॥
7.2.14.43: For japa done without the thumb is fruitless. Japa at home one should know as of ordinary value; in a cowshed they know it to be a hundredfold. ॥43॥
7.2.14.44: In a sacred forest and likewise in a garden it is said to be a thousandfold; on a holy mountain ten thousandfold; at a river it is declared to be a hundred thousandfold. ॥44॥
7.2.14.45: In a temple they declare it ten-millionfold, and in my presence infinite. In the presence of the sun, fire, the guru, the moon, a lamp and water, ॥45॥
7.2.14.46: and of brahmins and cows, japa is commended. Japa facing east brings control over others, and facing south is for hostile rites (abhicāra). ॥46॥
7.2.14.47: One should know facing west as bestowing wealth, and facing north gives peace. In the presence of the sun, fire, brahmins, gods and gurus, ॥47॥
7.2.14.48: and of other venerable beings who are present, one should not repeat the mantra with face turned away. Wearing a turban, wearing a jacket, naked, with hair untied, with the neck covered, ॥48॥
7.2.14.49: with impure hands, unclean, or while lamenting, one should never do japa. Anger, intoxication, sneezing—these three—spitting and yawning, ॥49॥
7.2.14.50: and the sight of dogs and lowly persons one should avoid during japa. If these occur, one should sip water, or remember me together with you, ॥50॥
7.2.14.51: or gaze at the heavenly lights, or perform breath-control. Without a seat, or lying down, walking, or standing up, ॥51॥
7.2.14.52: on a street, in an inauspicious place, or in darkness one should not do japa. One should not do japa with legs stretched out, nor in the cock posture, ॥52॥
7.2.14.53: or mounted on a vehicle or a bed, or distraught with worry. If one is able, one should observe all this; if unable, one should do japa according to one's capacity. ॥53॥
7.2.14.54: What is the use of saying much here? Hear my word in brief: one of good conduct who does japa purely and meditates attains welfare. ॥54॥
7.2.14.55: Right conduct is the highest dharma; right conduct is the highest wealth; right conduct is the highest knowledge; right conduct is the highest goal. ॥55॥
7.2.14.56: A man devoid of right conduct is censured in the world, and he will not be happy in the hereafter either; therefore one should be possessed of right conduct. ॥56॥
7.2.14.57: Whatever action is enjoined for a person in the Veda and in the śāstra by Vedic authorities, his proper practice of that is good conduct, and nothing else. ॥57॥
7.2.14.58: And because it is practised by the good (sat), it is called sadācāra. They say that the root cause of that good conduct is faith (āstikya). ॥58॥
7.2.14.59: If a man is a believer (āstika), even if he slips from good conduct through negligence and the like, he is never corrupted; therefore one should adopt faith. ॥59॥
7.2.14.60: Just as here there is happiness and sorrow through good and evil deeds, so also it exists in the hereafter—this conviction is called āstikya. ॥60॥
7.2.14.61: I shall tell you another secret; this must be guarded, beloved. It should not be told to just anyone, to an unbeliever, or to a paśu (one in bondage). ॥61॥
7.2.14.62: For one devoid of good conduct, for the fallen and for the outcaste, there is no protection higher than the Pañcākṣara in the Kali age. ॥62॥
7.2.14.63: Whether one is walking or standing, acting as one pleases, impure or pure, this mantra is never fruitless. ॥63॥
7.2.14.64: For men without proper conduct, whose six paths (ṣaḍadhvan) have not been purified, even if not imparted by a guru, this mantra is never fruitless. ॥64॥
7.2.14.65: Even for an outcaste, a fool, a deluded person, one who is fallen, one without restraint, a lowly person—this mantra is never fruitless. ॥65॥
7.2.14.66: For one who, though in any condition whatever, has supreme devotion to me, it surely succeeds, without doubt—but not for anyone else. ॥66॥
7.2.14.67: For this mantra, beloved, the ascendant, lunar day, asterism, weekday, yoga and the like need not be considered at all; it is never asleep, but always awake. ॥67॥
7.2.14.68: This great mantra is never at any time hostile to anyone; it will be either well-accomplished, accomplished, or to be accomplished. ॥68॥
7.2.14.69: Imparted by a guru who has attained perfection, it is called well-accomplished (susiddha); but if given by one not perfected, it is merely accomplished-to-be-accomplished (siddha-sādhya). ॥69॥
7.2.14.70: Whether practised to perfection or not, it surely succeeds, no doubt, for one endowed with exceeding faith in me, in the mantra and likewise in the guru. ॥70॥
7.2.14.71: Therefore, abandoning other mantras, which are fraught with danger on account of the requirements of eligibility, the wise man should resort directly to the supreme vidyā, the Pañcākṣarī. ॥71॥
7.2.14.72: When other mantras are accomplished, this mantra is not thereby accomplished; but when this great mantra is accomplished, those too become accomplished. ॥72॥
7.2.14.73: Just as, O Maheśvarī, even when the gods are attained I am not attained, but when I am attained they are attained—the same rule holds for these mantras. ॥73॥
7.2.14.74: The defects that belong to all other mantras do not arise in this one at all, since this mantra operates without regard to caste and the like. ॥74॥
7.2.14.75: Even so, one should not rashly employ it for petty ends or against adversaries, for this mantra is of great power. ॥75॥
7.2.14.76: Upamanyu said: Thus the procedure of the Pañcākṣara, just as it is, was told directly to Mahādevī by Mahādeva, the trident-bearer, for the welfare of the worlds. ॥76॥
7.2.14.77: Whoever recites this with devotion, or listens to it attentively, is freed from all sins and attains the supreme goal. ॥77॥
7.2.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The glory of the five-syllabled mantra, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
7.2.15.1: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Blessed One, O Lord, you have told me the greatness of the mantra and the procedure for its application, just as if it were the Veda itself. ॥1॥
7.2.15.2: Now I wish to hear about the supreme Śaiva rite of consecration; in the account of receiving the mantra it was only hinted at a little, not explained in detail. ॥2॥
7.2.15.3: Upamanyu said: Well then, I shall tell you of the consecration, supreme and holy, which purifies all sins, as expounded by Śiva. ॥3॥
7.2.15.4: Because through it a man becomes properly qualified for worship and the rest, it is called saṃskāra; it is the purification of the six paths. ॥4॥
7.2.15.5: Since by it knowledge is given (dīyate) and the bondage of fetters is destroyed (kṣīyate), this very saṃskāra is also called dīkṣā. ॥5॥
7.2.15.6: In the Śaiva scripture, initiation is taught by Śiva, the Supreme Self, as threefold: Śāmbhavī, Śāktī and Māntrī. ॥6॥
7.2.15.7: By the mere glance of the guru, by his touch, or even by his speech, there instantly arises in a creature an awareness that brings about the destruction of the fetters. ॥7॥
7.2.15.8: That initiation is called Śāmbhavī; it is again divided in two—intense and more intense—according to the difference in the destruction of the fetters. ॥8॥
7.2.15.9: That by which liberation comes at once is held to be the more intense; the intense one completely purifies the sins of a man while he is still living. ॥9॥
7.2.15.10: The Śāktī initiation, consisting of knowledge, is performed by the guru entering the disciple's body by the path of yoga, with the eye of knowledge. ॥10॥
7.2.15.11: The Māntrī initiation, consisting of ritual action, preceded by the fire-pit and the maṇḍala, is to be performed externally by the guru, for those disciples of slow and slower receptivity. ॥11॥
7.2.15.12: The disciple deserves grace in accordance with the descent of divine power, because, in brief, following Śaiva dharma has that as its root. ॥12॥
7.2.15.13: Where the power has not descended, there no purification arises—neither knowledge, nor Śaiva conduct, nor liberation, nor attainments. ॥13॥
7.2.15.14: Therefore, having carefully observed the signs of an abundant descent of power, the guru should purify the disciple either by knowledge or by ritual. ॥14॥
7.2.15.15: He who out of delusion acts otherwise, that foolish one perishes. Therefore the guru should examine the disciple in every way. ॥15॥
7.2.15.16: The mark of the descent of power is the arising of awakening and bliss, because that supreme Power has the form of awakening and bliss. ॥16॥
7.2.15.17: The sign of bliss and awakening is transformations of the inner faculty, such as appear as trembling, horripilation, and changes in the voice, eyes and limbs. ॥17॥
7.2.15.18: The disciple too should examine the guru by these signs, as seen in those in contact with him, those associated with him in Śiva-worship and the like, or those devoted to him. ॥18॥
7.2.15.19: Since the disciple is the one to be taught, he has reason for reverence toward the guru; therefore with every effort he should show reverence to the guru. ॥19॥
7.2.15.20: He who is the guru is declared to be Śiva; he who is Śiva is known as the guru. Or rather, the guru is Śiva himself, abiding in the form of knowledge. ॥20॥
7.2.15.21: As is Śiva, so is knowledge; as is knowledge, so is the guru. The fruit from worship of Śiva, knowledge and the gurus is the same. ॥21॥
7.2.15.22: This guru embodies all the gods and consists of all mantras; therefore with every effort one should bear his command upon one's head. ॥22॥
7.2.15.23: If one seeks the highest good, one should not transgress the guru's command even in thought, since one who obeys the guru's command attains the wealth of knowledge. ॥23॥
7.2.15.24: Whether walking, standing, sleeping or eating, one should not undertake any other act; if one does anything in his presence, let it all be with the guru's permission. ॥24॥
7.2.15.25: In the guru's house or in his presence one should not sit as one pleases, since the guru is God in person and his house is a temple. ॥25॥
7.2.15.26: Just as through association with sinners one becomes fallen by their sin, and just as here gold gives up its impurity through contact with fire, so too a man gives up sin through contact with the guru. ॥26॥
7.2.15.27: Just as a pot of ghee placed near a fire melts, so sin melts away in the presence of the teacher. ॥27॥
7.2.15.28: Just as a blazing fire burns both dry and wet, so this guru too, when pleased, burns away sin in an instant. ॥28॥
7.2.15.29: By mind, deed or speech one should not provoke the guru's anger. ॥29॥
7.2.15.30: By his anger, life, prosperity, knowledge and good deeds are burnt up; for those who provoke his anger, even their sacrifices are fruitless, ॥30॥
7.2.15.31: and so too their restraints and observances—there need be no doubt about this. A man should never utter any word contrary to the guru. ॥31॥
7.2.15.32: If out of great delusion he should speak so, he goes to the Raurava hell. Carefully, in mind, deed and speech with regard to the guru, ॥32॥
7.2.15.33: a wise man who seeks the highest good should not behave falsely. He should always do what is beneficial and pleasing to the guru, whether instructed or not. ॥33॥
7.2.15.34: Whether in his absence or in his presence, he should carry out the guru's work. A devotee of such conduct, with mind ever diligent, ॥34॥
7.2.15.35: a disciple who does what pleases the guru then becomes worthy of the Śaiva dharmas. If the guru is virtuous, wise, a revealer of supreme bliss, ॥35॥
7.2.15.36: a knower of reality and devoted to Śiva, then he is a giver of liberation—but not another. Reality is what produces awareness and gives rise to supreme bliss. ॥36॥
7.2.15.37: He by whom that reality is known is alone the revealer of bliss—not one who is a guru in name only and devoid of awareness. ॥37॥
7.2.15.38: Boats may carry one another across; can a stone carry a stone across? Through one who is a guru in name only, liberation too is in name only. ॥38॥
7.2.15.39: But those by whom reality is known are themselves liberated and also liberate others. In one devoid of reality, how can there be awakening? How indeed can there be grasp of the Self? ॥39॥
7.2.15.40: One devoid of such grasp is called a paśu (bound soul); and one directed by paśus does not pass beyond the state of being a paśu. ॥40॥
7.2.15.41: Therefore only one who knows the reality (tattva), being himself liberated, is accepted here as a liberator. Even if this teacher is endowed with all the auspicious marks and knows all the scriptures, ॥41॥
7.2.15.42: and even if he knows the procedures of all the means, yet if he lacks realisation of the reality, he is fruitless. He whose intellect engages in the reality right up to direct experience— ॥42॥
7.2.15.43: from his glance and the like supreme bliss arises. Therefore, the one through whose very contact awakening and bliss arise— ॥43॥
7.2.15.44: a wise man should choose him alone as guru, not another. That guru, approved by disciples skilled in humility and good conduct, ॥44॥
7.2.15.45: should be served by seekers of liberation until he is fully known. When he is known, there should be steady devotion until one has taken refuge in the reality. ॥45॥
7.2.15.46: But one should never abandon the reality nor neglect it in any way. A guru in whom not even a little bliss or awakening is found— ॥46॥
7.2.15.47: even after a year, the disciple should leave him and resort to another guru. Even having taken refuge in another guru, he should not disrespect the former one, nor the guru's brothers, sons, instructors and inspirers. ॥47॥
7.2.15.48: In that matter, first approaching a brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas, one should worship the guru who is wise, auspicious and pleasing to behold, ॥48॥
7.2.15.49: the giver of all fearlessness, whose mind is filled with compassion. One should please him with effort, by mind, deed and speech. ॥49॥
7.2.15.50: The disciple should worship him until he becomes pleased. When he is pleased, the disciple's sins are destroyed at once. ॥50॥
7.2.15.51: Therefore wealth, gems, fields and houses, ornaments and garments, vehicles, beds and seats— ॥51॥
7.2.15.52: these one should give to the guru with devotion, according to one's means. One should not be deceitful about wealth if one desires the supreme goal. ॥52॥
7.2.15.53: Since he alone is father, mother, husband, kinsman, wealth, happiness, companion and friend, therefore one should offer everything to him. ॥53॥
7.2.15.54: Having offered these, afterwards, dedicating to him one's own self together with one's lineage and possessions, with a libation of water, one should always remain under his control. ॥54॥
7.2.15.55: When an embodied being has given his own self to Śiva in the form of the preceptor, then he becomes a Śaiva; for him there is no rebirth thereafter. ॥55॥
7.2.15.56: The guru should test a disciple who has resorted to him for one year if a brāhmaṇa, two years if a kṣatriya, and three years if a vaiśya, ॥56॥
7.2.15.57: by commands, fitting and unfitting, such as demanding the giving of life and wealth, putting superior ones to low work and low ones to superior work. ॥57॥
7.2.15.58: Those who, even when reviled or beaten, do not fall into dejection—they are fit, self-controlled and pure for the rite of Śaiva consecration. ॥58॥
7.2.15.59: Non-violent, compassionate, always of diligent mind, free of pride, intelligent, having given up rivalry, sweet-spoken, ॥59॥
7.2.15.60: upright, gentle, pure, humble, steady-minded, endowed with purity and good conduct, devotees of Śiva, twice-born— ॥60॥
7.2.15.61: those thus endowed with good conduct in speech, mind, body and action are to be purified and instructed according to rule—this is the settled view in the scriptures. ॥61॥
7.2.15.62: A woman has no eligibility of her own for the rite of Śaiva consecration; but by her husband's authorization she certainly has it, if she is endowed with devotion to the Lord. ॥62॥
7.2.15.63: Likewise a widow certainly has eligibility with the permission of her son or others, and a maiden by her father's command. For śūdras, low-born castes, and especially the fallen, ॥63॥
7.2.15.64: and likewise for mixed castes, the purification of the paths (adhvan) is not prescribed. If they too have unfeigned devotion to Śiva, the supreme cause, ॥64॥
7.2.15.65: they should effect the purification of their sins by the giving of the guru's foot-water and the like. Here, those born in anuloma order are indeed counted among the twice-born; ॥65॥
7.2.15.66: for them one should perform the purification of the paths and the rest as befits their mother's lineage. But a maiden who has been appointed to Śiva's dharma by her father and others— ॥66॥
7.2.15.67: she should be given in marriage to a devotee, not to another who is hostile. If through negligence she has been given to an adverse man, she should enlighten her husband. ॥67॥
7.2.15.68: If unable, abandoning him in mind, she should practise dharma—just as the devoted wife Anasūyā, leaving her husband Atri, the best of sages, ॥68॥
7.2.15.69: long ago attained fulfilment by worshipping Śaṅkara with austerity; and just as Draupadī, having worshipped the god Nārāyaṇa with austerity, the Pāṇḍavas ॥69॥
7.2.15.70: obtained as husbands, though not appointed to that dharma by her elders. In truth, the fault arising from lack of independence does not apply here ॥70॥
7.2.15.71: for a woman engaged in Śiva's dharma, because of the weight of Śiva's command. What use is saying much here? Whoever it may be that takes refuge in Śiva— ॥71॥
7.2.15.72: he is fit to be consecrated if he is subject to the guru; the rite does not differ for him. Merely by the guru's glance, by touch, or by conversation, ॥72॥
7.2.15.73: for one in whom wisdom arises there is no defeat. The consecration that is performed mentally by the path of yoga— ॥73॥
7.2.15.74: that secret one, accessible only through the guru's mouth, is not described here. But the ritual consecration preceded by the fire-pit and pavilion will be told in brief; its full extent cannot be told. ॥74॥
7.2.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the guru in the rite of initiation, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
7.2.16.1: Upamanyu said: On an auspicious day, in a pure place free from many defects, the preceptor should first perform the rite called Samaya. ॥1॥
7.2.16.2: Having examined the ground according to rule by its smell, colour, taste and so on, he should construct a pavilion there in the manner taught in the treatises of the builders. ॥2॥
7.2.16.3: Having made an altar in its middle, he should arrange fire-pits in the eight directions, or likewise in the four directions; then, in due order, in the northeast... ॥3॥
7.2.16.4: ...he should make the principal pit, or else on the western side. Or, having made only the one principal pit, he should arrange the decoration, ॥4॥
7.2.16.5: with canopies, banners and garlands of many kinds in abundance. Then in the middle of the altar he should make a maṇḍala with auspicious marks, ॥5॥
7.2.16.6: with red, golden and other powders, fit for invoking the Lord; but a poor man should make it with powders of vermilion, rice and wild rice only. ॥6॥
7.2.16.7: It may be one cubit or two cubits wide, white or red. For a lotus of one cubit the pericarp is held to be eight finger-breadths. ॥7॥
7.2.16.8: The filaments are half of that, and the remainder is the eight petals and so on. For a lotus of two cubits, the pericarp and the rest are double. ॥8॥
7.2.16.9: Having made it rich in ornaments and secondary ornaments, he should again prepare, on the altar to its northeast, a maṇḍala of one cubit or half of that, ॥9॥
7.2.16.10: spread with paddy, husked rice, white mustard, sesame, flowers and kuśa grass. There he should set up the Śiva-pot endowed with the proper marks, ॥10॥
7.2.16.11: made of gold, silver, copper or clay, strewn with sandal, flowers and unbroken rice, covered with kuśa and sprouts of dūrvā grass, ॥11॥
7.2.16.12: its neck wound with white thread, wrapped in a pair of new cloths, filled with pure water, with a tuft of kuśa on top, containing precious substances and having a lid. ॥12॥
7.2.16.13: He should also prepare a spouted pitcher and a vardhanī vessel, a conch or a discus, all without the thread and so on, or even a lotus leaf. ॥13॥
7.2.16.14: He should place the pot on the northern petal of its seat-lotus, and in front, with sandal-water, the vardhanī of the king of weapons (the Astra). ॥14॥
7.2.16.15: Then, to the east of the maṇḍala, having likewise prepared the mantra-pot as before, he should perform the great worship of the Lord according to rule. ॥15॥
7.2.16.16: Or else on the shore of the ocean, by a river, in a cowpen or on a mountain, in a temple or a house, or in any other charming place, ॥16॥
7.2.16.17: having done all that was described before, or doing it without the pavilion and the rest, having made the maṇḍala as before and the fire-ground (sthaṇḍila) for the fire, ॥17॥
7.2.16.18: the guru, with a joyful face, endowed with all auspicious things and having completed his daily rites, enters the hall of worship. ॥18॥
7.2.16.19: Having performed the great worship of Maheśa in the centre of the maṇḍala, he should again invoke Śiva in the Śiva-pot and worship him. ॥19॥
7.2.16.20: Having meditated on the Lord, protector of the sacrifice, as facing west, he should worship the Lord's Astra in the Astra-vardhanī on the south. ॥20॥
7.2.16.21: Having installed the mantra in the mantra-pot, the one skilled in mantras, having performed the mudrās and everything else, should carry out the mantra-worship. ॥21॥
7.2.16.22: Then the best of preceptors should perform the fire-offering in the Śiva-fire in the principal pit, and other brahmins should make offerings in the pits all around. ॥22॥
7.2.16.23: Their offering is prescribed as a quarter or a half of the ācārya's. Or else the best of preceptors alone may offer in the principal pit. ॥23॥
7.2.16.24: Others should recite the Veda, hymns and auspicious benedictions, and others, devoted to Śiva, should perform japa according to rule. ॥24॥
7.2.16.25: Having had dance, song, instrumental music and other auspicious things performed, and having properly honoured the assembled members according to rule, ॥25॥
7.2.16.26: and then having had the puṇyāha declaration recited and again worshipped Śaṅkara, the preceptor should pray to the god, desiring grace for the disciple: ॥26॥
7.2.16.27: Be gracious, O Lord of the gods of gods. Entering my body, O Lord of the universe, release this one out of compassion, O treasure of compassion. ॥27॥
7.2.16.28: Then, having received permission, as if the Lord said, I will do so, the preceptor should bring the disciple, who has fasted or has eaten only sacrificial food, ॥28॥
7.2.16.29: or who has eaten once a day, self-restrained, bathed, having done his morning rites, repeating the praṇava, meditating on the god, and having performed auspicious acts, ॥29॥
7.2.16.30: and, in the area in front of the western door or of the southern door, having seated the young disciple on a seat of darbha grass facing north, ॥30॥
7.2.16.31: the guru, himself standing and facing east, having sprinkled the disciple, who holds his body erect with joined palms, with water from the sprinkling vessel, on the head with the Astra mantra and mudrā, ॥31॥
7.2.16.32: and having struck him by tossing a flower, the guru should bind his eyes with a new, consecrated cloth, half of a fine silk garment. ॥32॥
7.2.16.33: Then the guru should lead the disciple into the maṇḍala through the door; and he, directed by him, should circumambulate Śambhu three times. ॥33॥
7.2.16.34: Then, having offered to the Lord a handful of flowers mixed with gold, facing east or north, he should prostrate on the ground like a staff. ॥34॥
7.2.16.35: Then the preceptor, having sprinkled him with the root mantra and struck him on the head with the Astra as before, should remove his blindfold. ॥35॥
7.2.16.36: Having seen the maṇḍala, he should again bow with joined palms to the Lord. Then the Śaiva preceptor, seated on the south of the maṇḍala, ॥36॥
7.2.16.37: the guru, having seated the disciple on a darbha seat on his own left, and having worshipped Mahādeva, should place the Śiva-hand, ॥37॥
7.2.16.38: Regarding his hand as full of Śiva's radiance, he should utter the Śiva-mantra and, filled with the conviction of being Śiva, place it on the disciple's head. ॥38॥
7.2.16.39: With that same hand the preceptor should touch all the limbs; and the disciple too should bow on the ground to the Lord in the form of the preceptor. ॥39॥
7.2.16.40: Then, having duly worshipped the god in the Śiva-fire and offered three oblations, and having seated the disciple as before, ॥40॥
7.2.16.41: Touching him with the tips of darbha grass, he should enter him with his own self by means of the vidyā mantra. Having bowed to Mahādeva, he should perform the joining of the channels (nāḍī). ॥41॥
7.2.16.42: By the method stated in the Śiva scriptures, having effected the going-out of the vital breath and contemplating its entry into the disciple's body, he should then satiate the mantras with oblations. ॥42॥
7.2.16.43: For satiating the root mantra, ten oblations are to be offered with that very mantra; likewise three for the limbs, with the limb-mantras themselves, in due order. ॥43॥
7.2.16.44: Then, having offered the full oblation, the preceptor who knows the mantras should, for expiation, again make ten oblations with the root mantra. ॥44॥
7.2.16.45: Again worshipping the Lord of gods and sipping water properly, and having offered oblations as prescribed, the preceptor should raise the disciple from his own birth-class to vaiśya status. ॥45॥
7.2.16.46: In the same way he should produce kṣatriya status for him; and then, again making the elevation in the same manner, the preceptor should produce brāhmaṇa-hood for him. ॥46॥
7.2.16.47: Having thus raised the kṣatriya and made him a brāhmaṇa, he should then produce Rudra-hood for both; for a born brāhmaṇa he should accomplish just the name Rudra. ॥47॥
7.2.16.48: Having performed sprinkling and striking (tāḍana) of the disciple, the guru, contemplating his own self within himself as of the nature of Śiva, flashing like a spark— ॥48॥
7.2.16.49: —the guru should expel the breath with the mantra through the channel as described; having gone out, he should likewise enter through the channel into the disciple's heart. ॥49॥
7.2.16.50: Having entered, recalling his consciousness as resembling a blue dot, he should contemplate it as blazing, its impurity dispelled by his own radiance. ॥50॥
7.2.16.51: Taking it through that channel with the withdrawal gesture (saṃhāra-mudrā), the mantra-adept, placing it within by inhalation (pūraka) for the sake of oneness with himself— ॥51॥
7.2.16.52: —holding it with retention (kumbhaka), and then with exhalation (recaka) through the channel as before, should take it from there and place it in the disciple's heart. ॥52॥
7.2.16.53: Touching him and giving him the sacred thread received from Śiva, he should offer three oblations and afterwards give the full oblation. ॥53॥
7.2.16.54: Seating the disciple to the right of the deity on an excellent seat strewn with kuśa grass and flowers, with joined palms, facing north, ॥54॥
7.2.16.55: making him sit in the svastika posture, the preceptor himself, facing east and seated on an excellent seat, with mantras and sounds of great auspiciousness, ॥55॥
7.2.16.56: taking up the full pot, fully prepared, the preceptor, meditating on Śiva, should consecrate the disciple by sprinkling (abhiṣeka). ॥56॥
7.2.16.57: Then, wiping off the bath water and putting on a white garment, the disciple, having sipped water and being adorned, should go to the pavilion with joined palms. ॥57॥
7.2.16.58: Seating him as before on a seat of darbha grass, the guru, having worshipped the deity in the maṇḍala, should perform hand-placement (karanyāsa). ॥58॥
7.2.16.59: Then the preceptor should meditate on the Lord in his mind and, with ash, touch the disciple with both hands, uttering Śiva. ॥59॥
7.2.16.60: Then the Śiva-preceptor, having performed for him the burning, flooding and so on, and the sakalīkaraṇa by way of the placement of the mātṛkā letters, ॥60॥
7.2.16.61: then the preceptor, contemplating Śiva's seat on the disciple's head, should invoke Śiva there as prescribed and worship him mentally. ॥61॥
7.2.16.62: With joined palms he should entreat the Lord: Remain here always. Having thus made the request, he should contemplate the disciple as shining with Śambhu's radiance. ॥62॥
7.2.16.63: Then, having worshipped Śiva and obtained Śiva's command, which is of Śiva's very nature, he should softly utter the Śiva mantra into the disciple's ear. ॥63॥
7.2.16.64: The disciple, with joined palms, having heard the mantra with his mind absorbed in it, should slowly repeat it at the Śiva-preceptor's instruction. ॥64॥
7.2.16.65: Then the one skilled in mantras, having imparted the Śakti mantra too and having had it pronounced comfortably, should pronounce a blessing upon him. ॥65॥
7.2.16.66: Then he should briefly explain the meaning of the mantra through the relation of the signified and the signifier, teach the form of the Lord, and instruct in yoga and posture. ॥66॥
7.2.16.67: Then, by the guru's command, in the presence of Śiva, the fire and the guru, the disciple, resolving thus with devotion, should utter the initiation vow: ॥67॥
7.2.16.68: Better the giving up of life, or even the cutting off of the head, than that I should eat without having worshipped the blessed three-eyed Lord. ॥68॥
7.2.16.69: He himself, self-restrained, should offer worship until delusion is overturned; until then he should propitiate the Lord, devoted to him and having him as his highest refuge. ॥69॥
7.2.16.70: Then he will be called a samaya initiate in the Śaiva order; having gained eligibility, he should keep the guru's command and remain under his control. ॥70॥
7.2.16.71: After this, the guru, having performed placement on his hands, should take ash with his own hand and give it to the disciple with the root mantra, and also a rudrākṣa consecrated by mantra, ॥71॥
7.2.16.72: or an image of the Lord, or else a concealed form of him, and, where possible, the means for worship, fire-offering, recitation and meditation. ॥72॥
7.2.16.73: The disciple, too, should accept with great reverence what he receives from the Śiva-preceptor, by that preceptor's command and not otherwise. ॥73॥
7.2.16.74: Placing on his head with devotion all that he received from the teacher, he should guard it and worship Śambhu, whether in a monastery or at home. ॥74॥
7.2.16.75: After this the preceptor should teach him the Śaiva code of conduct, in accordance with his devotion and faith and in accordance with his understanding. ॥75॥
7.2.16.76: Whatever is spoken, whatever is commanded, and whatever else is declared by the Śiva-preceptor at the samaya rite—all that he should bear on his head. ॥76॥
7.2.16.77: Taking up, reading aloud and hearing the Śaiva scriptures he should do at the preceptor's direction, not by his own wish nor from anyone else. ॥77॥
7.2.16.78: Thus has been briefly described the sacrament called samaya, the supreme means for men to attain Śiva's city directly. ॥78॥
7.2.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The consecration of the disciple, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
7.2.17.1: Upamanyu said: After this, the guru, having carefully examined the disciple's fitness, should perform the purification of the six paths (ṣaḍ-adhva) so that the disciple is released from all bonds. ॥1॥
7.2.17.2: Kalā, tattva, bhuvana, varṇa, then pada, and mantra — thus, in brief, the sixfold path is enumerated. ॥2॥
7.2.17.3: The five kalās beginning with Nivṛtti are called by the wise the path of kalā; the other five paths are pervaded by the five kalās. ॥3॥
7.2.17.4: From the Śiva-tattva down to earth is declared the path of tattvas; it comprises twenty-six in number and is of pure, impure and mixed nature. ॥4॥
7.2.17.5: The path of worlds is proclaimed as extending from Ādhāra up to Unmanā; without counting their divisions and subdivisions, it comprises sixty in number. ॥5॥
7.2.17.6: The fifty letters, which are forms of Rudra, are called the path of letters; the path of words is declared to have many varieties. ॥6॥
7.2.17.7: The path of mantras, together with all the subsidiary mantras, is pervaded by the supreme Vidyā. Just as Śiva, the lord of the tattvas, is not counted among the tattvas, ॥7॥
7.2.17.8: so he, the lord of mantras, is not to be counted in the path of mantras. The pervasiveness of the kalā-path and the pervadedness of the other paths — ॥8॥
7.2.17.9: he who does not truly know this is not at all fit for the purification of the paths. He by whom the form of the sixfold path is not known — ॥9॥
7.2.17.10: by him the relation of pervaded and pervader cannot even be understood. Therefore the nature of the paths, and likewise the relation of pervaded and pervader, ॥10॥
7.2.17.11: only after understanding them properly should one perform the purification of the paths. Having done everything there as before, up to preparing the fire-pit and the maṇḍala, ॥11॥
7.2.17.12: he should make in the east a maṇḍala for the pitchers, two cubits in measure. Then the Śaiva preceptor, having bathed and performed his daily rites, together with the disciple, ॥12॥
7.2.17.13: entering the maṇḍala, should perform the worship of Śambhu as before. There, milk-rice for the Lord, cooked from rice not less than an āḍhaka in measure, ॥13॥
7.2.17.14: having offered half of it, he should set aside the rest for the homa. Then, in a maṇḍala prepared in front, adorned with coloured powders, ॥14॥
7.2.17.15: the preceptor should place five pitchers, in the four directions and in the middle. In them he should install the five Brahma-mantras, with their root syllables joined with bindu and nāda, ॥15॥
7.2.17.16: beginning with namaḥ and ending with the syllable ya, the foremost knower of ritual should install them: Īśāna in the middle pitcher, Tatpuruṣa in the one placed in front, ॥16॥
7.2.17.17: Aghora in the southern one, Vāmadeva in the northern (left) one, and Sadyojāta in the western one. Having made the protection and formed the mudrā, the consecration of the pitchers ॥17॥
7.2.17.18: having done, he should begin the homa in the Śiva-fire as before. That half of the milk-rice which was earlier set aside for the homa, ॥18॥
7.2.17.19: having offered it, he should keep its remainder for the disciple to eat. Having performed the rite up to the tarpaṇa of the mantras as before, ॥19॥
7.2.17.20: and having offered the full oblation for them, he should then perform the kindling (dīpana). After oṃ, huṃ, then the root mantra ending in phaṭ, ॥20॥
7.2.17.21: and finally ending with svāhā — this they declare to be the formula for kindling, and likewise the aṅga mantras in due order. Three oblations of these are to be given in the kindling rite. ॥21॥
7.2.17.22: With those mantras, one by one, their blazing forms are to be contemplated. A white thread, spun by a brāhmaṇa maiden, made threefold and then threefold again, ॥22॥
7.2.17.23: that thread, having consecrated it with the root mantra, he should tie to the tip of the disciple's tuft, letting it reach to the big toe of the disciple standing with body erect. ॥23॥
7.2.17.24: Having let that thread hang down, he should join the suṣumṇā to it there. Taking it up with the Śānta mudrā, the knower of mantras, with the root mantra, ॥24॥
7.2.17.25: having offered three oblations, should establish its (the suṣumṇā's) presence in the thread. Striking the disciple on the heart by casting a flower, as before, ॥25॥
7.2.17.26: taking up his consciousness and placing it in the dvādaśānta, joining the thread with the suṣumṇā thread, protecting it with the astra mantra and the armour (varma) mantra, ॥26॥
7.2.17.27: and then having veiled that thread, he should regard it as the disciple's body. The bond made of the three root impurities, characterized by enjoyership and enjoyability, ॥27॥
7.2.17.28: which produces the sense-objects, senses, body and the rest — this he should imagine as his. The kalās beginning with Śāntyatīta, which have the forms of the elements beginning with ether, ॥28॥
7.2.17.29: are to be joined to the thread by their own names and worshipped with those names joined with namaḥ, or else with their seed-syllables. Having done in order what was stated before, ॥29॥
7.2.17.30: he should then observe the pervasion of mala and the rest in the tattvas and the rest, and the pervasion of the kalās in mala and the rest; and having offered oblations, he should kindle the kalās. ॥30॥
7.2.17.31: Striking the disciple on the head, and placing the thread on the body in due order, he should mark the thread at the position of Śāntyatīta while uttering the mantra. ॥31॥
7.2.17.32: Having done thus in sequence from Śāntyatīta down to Nivṛtti, and having offered three oblations, he should afterwards worship Śiva in the maṇḍala. ॥32॥
7.2.17.33: Seating the disciple to the south of the deity, facing north, in a maṇḍala strewn with darbha grass, the guru should give him the caru left over from the homa. ॥33॥
7.2.17.34: The disciple, honouring what was given by the guru and uttering Śiva's name first, having eaten it, should afterwards sip water twice and recite the Śiva-mantra. ॥34॥
7.2.17.35: Likewise, in another maṇḍala the guru should give him pañcagavya; he too, drinking it according to his capacity and sipping water twice, should remember Śiva. ॥35॥
7.2.17.36: Seating the disciple in a third maṇḍala as before, he should give him a tooth-stick having the characteristics stated in the scriptures. ॥36॥
7.2.17.37: With its soft tip, facing east or north, seated and restraining his speech, the disciple should clean his teeth. ॥37॥
7.2.17.38: Having washed the tooth-stick and thrown it away, and having sipped water, he should remember Śiva; then, instructed by the preceptor, with joined palms he should enter the Śiva-maṇḍala. ॥38॥
7.2.17.39: If the discarded tooth-stick is seen by the guru lying with its tip toward the east, north or west, it is auspicious; otherwise it is inauspicious. ॥39॥
7.2.17.40: If it points toward an unfavourable direction, the guru, to pacify that fault, should offer a hundred oblations with the root mantra, or half of that, or half of that again. ॥40॥
7.2.17.41: Then, having touched the disciple and having whispered the mantra of Śiva into his ears, the guru should have that disciple stay for the preparatory rite (adhivāsana) on the right side of the deity. ॥41॥
7.2.17.42: Pure, on a bed of darbha grass spread with an unworn (new) covering and consecrated with mantras, he should lie down at night with his head to the east, meditating inwardly on Śiva. ॥42॥
7.2.17.43: The guru, having bound with the śikhā-mantra the tuft of the disciple, to whose tuft a thread is tied, and having covered him with an unworn cloth with the armour-mantra (varman), ॥43॥
7.2.17.44: and having drawn three lines all around with ash, and with sesame and mustard seeds empowered by the astra-mantra, he should offer an oblation (bali) to the lords of the directions outside that boundary. ॥44॥
7.2.17.45: The disciple too, having thus undergone the adhivāsana and fasting thereafter, on waking and rising should report to the guru the dream he has seen. ॥45॥
7.2.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The rite of Śiva initiation, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
7.2.18.1: Upamanyu said: Then, having completed everything, such as bathing, and being urged by the preceptor, the disciple should go to the side of Śiva's maṇḍala with joined palms, meditating. ॥1॥
7.2.18.2: Then, having done everything as on the previous day, except the worship, up to the binding of the eyes, the guru should show him the maṇḍala. ॥2॥
7.2.18.3: When the scattering of flowers has been done by the blindfolded disciple, he should assign to him the name of that deity where the flowers fall. ॥3॥
7.2.18.4: And having brought him near, in this maṇḍala bearing the offered remains, as before, he should worship the god Īśāna and offer oblations into the Śiva-fire. ॥4॥
7.2.18.5: If a bad dream has been seen by the disciple, to pacify that fault he should offer a hundred oblations, or half that, or half of that, with the root mantra. ॥5॥
7.2.18.6: Then, having let the thread tied to the topknot hang down as before, whatever rite concerns the Nivṛtti kalā, beginning with the worship of the support (ādhāra)... ॥6॥
7.2.18.7: ...ending with the worship of Vāgīśvarī, he should perform, preceded by homa. Then, having bowed to Vāgīśā, the virtuous one who pervades Nivṛtti, ॥7॥
7.2.18.8: and having worshipped the god in the maṇḍala and offered three oblations, he should bring about the child's (disciple's) entry into all the wombs simultaneously. ॥8॥
7.2.18.9: Then, having performed striking, sprinkling and the rest on the disciple's thread-body, having taken up his self and placed it in the dvādaśānta, ॥9॥
7.2.18.10: then, taking it from there too with the root mantra and the mudrā seen in the scriptures, the preceptor should mentally join it simultaneously to all the wombs. ॥10॥
7.2.18.11: There are eight classes of gods and five classes of animals; with the single human class, the wombs are fourteen. ॥11॥
7.2.18.12: For the disciple's simultaneous entry into all of them, he should mentally place the disciple's self in Vāgīśānī, as is proper. ॥12॥
7.2.18.13: For the formation of the embryo, having worshipped the god, bowed down, and offered oblations as prescribed, he should contemplate it as formed. ॥13॥
7.2.18.14: Thus, through ritual action, he should bring about the birth and continued life of the one formed, his uprightness, the fulfilment of enjoyments, and likewise supreme delight. ॥14॥
7.2.18.15: For expiation, and for the perfection of class, life-span, enjoyment and saṃskāras, the best of preceptors, having offered three oblations, should pray to the god. ॥15॥
7.2.18.16: Having in just this way removed the impurity of being an enjoyer and of attachment to objects, that is, the purification of that body, he should then cut the disciple's three bonds. ॥16॥
7.2.18.17: By cutting, through the complete severance of the bond that bound him, having made the disciple's consciousness pure, he should regard it as alone (free). ॥17॥
7.2.18.18: Having offered the full oblation into the fire, he should then worship Brahmā; having offered him three oblations, he should convey Śiva's command to him: ॥18॥
7.2.18.19: O Grandsire, no obstruction is to be made by you for this one who is going to the supreme Śaiva abode; this command of Śiva is most weighty. ॥19॥
7.2.18.20: Having commanded thus, worshipped him and dismissed him according to rule, he should worship Mahādeva and offer three oblations. ॥20॥
7.2.18.21: Having drawn up the disciple's self, purified by Nivṛtti, as before, and placed it in his own self and in the thread, he should then worship Vāgīśa. ॥21॥
7.2.18.22: Having offered three oblations to her, bowed and dismissed her, he should make the joining of Nivṛtti with the Pratiṣṭhā kalā. ॥22॥
7.2.18.23: At the joining, having performed worship of both together and offered three oblations, he should then visualise the entry of the disciple's self into Pratiṣṭhā. ॥23॥
7.2.18.24: Then, having invoked Pratiṣṭhā and done all that was stated before, he should contemplate its pervasion and Vāgīśānī as its pervader, ॥24॥
7.2.18.25: her resembling the disc of the full moon; and having done the rest as before, he should convey to Viṣṇu the command of Śiva, the Supreme Self. ॥25॥
7.2.18.26: And having performed the dismissal of Viṣṇu and the rest, having joined Pratiṣṭhā with Vidyā, and in her too, as before, ॥26॥
7.2.18.27: having done the rites, having contemplated its pervasion and Vāgīśā in due order, having done all up to the full oblation in the blazing fire, and the rest as before, ॥27॥
7.2.18.28: having invoked Nīlarudra and likewise performed worship and the rest for him, he should give him Śiva's command in the manner stated before. ॥28॥
7.2.18.29: Then, having dismissed him as well, and having joined the Vidyā kalā to Śānti, he should observe its pervasion. ॥29॥
7.2.18.30: Likewise he should contemplate Vāgīśī, the pervader of his own self, whose form resembles the rising sun, illuminating the ten directions. ॥30॥
7.2.18.31: Then, having done the rest as before, having invoked and worshipped the god Maheśvara and offered oblations to him, he should mentally convey Śiva's command. ॥31॥
7.2.18.32: Having likewise dismissed Maheśvara and performed the rite for this other kalā, having led it to the Śāntyatītā kalā, he should observe its pervasion. ॥32॥
7.2.18.33: Likewise he should contemplate Vāgīśī, the pervader of his own self, resembling the expanse of the sky; and do everything up to the full oblation as before. ॥33॥
7.2.18.34: Having done this by the remaining procedure and worshipped Sadāśiva, he should impart to him the command of Śambhu of immeasurable deeds. ॥34॥
7.2.18.35: There too, as before, placing Śiva on the head as before, and having worshipped Vāgīśa and bowed, he should dismiss her. ॥35॥
7.2.18.36: Then, having sprinkled the disciple on the head with the Śiva mantra as before, he should contemplate the dissolution of Śāntyatītā into the Śakti-tattva. ॥36॥
7.2.18.37: On the far shore beyond the six paths, he should contemplate the supreme Śaiva Śakti, pervading all paths, shining like ten million suns. ॥37॥
7.2.18.38: Having brought the disciple, stainless as pure crystal, before her, and afterwards having washed the scissors according to the method stated in the Śiva scriptures, ॥38॥
7.2.18.39: the preceptor should cut his topknot together with the thread. Then, having placed it on cow-dung, he should offer the topknot into the Śiva-fire, ॥39॥
7.2.18.40: with the root mantra ending in vauṣaṭ. Having washed the scissors again and placed them in the disciple's hand, he should return the disciple's consciousness into his body. ॥40॥
7.2.18.41: Then, having led the disciple (śiśu), who has bathed, sipped water ritually and had the auspicious rites (svastyayana) performed for him, into the vicinity of the maṇḍala, and having made him prostrate like a staff, ॥41॥
7.2.18.42: and having performed worship according to rule, the guru should offer three oblations with the audible (vācaka) mantra itself, to purify any deficiency in the ritual acts. ॥42॥
7.2.18.43: He should offer three oblations by way of whispered (upāṃśu) utterance. Again, having worshipped the Lord of gods, to purify any deficiency in the mantras, ॥43॥
7.2.18.44: he should offer three oblations by way of mental utterance. Then, having worshipped Śambhu present in the maṇḍala together with Ambā, and having offered three oblations, the guru should afterwards pray with folded hands: ॥44॥
7.2.18.45: O Lord, by your grace the purification of his six paths (ṣaḍadhvan) has been accomplished; therefore lead him to your supreme, imperishable abode. ॥45॥
7.2.18.46: Having thus informed the god, and having performed, preceded by the joining of the nāḍīs, the rite ending with the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti) as before, he should then purify the elements. ॥46॥
7.2.18.47: Then, for purification, in the rite of purifying the elements, he should meditate on the stable and unstable, then on the cold and hot, and then on the corresponding stations, as having the form of oneness through pervasion. ॥47॥
7.2.18.48: Having severed the knots of the elements and having abandoned the elements together with their presiding deities, he who by the method of steadiness repeats the mantra in the supreme Śiva — ॥48॥
7.2.18.49: having purified him, burnt his body, and flooded it with drops of nectar, and having installed the self, he should then make his body consist of the purified paths. ॥49॥
7.2.18.50: There, first, he should place the all-pervading kalā Śāntyatītā of his own path, wholly pure, on the disciple's head, and likewise Śānti on the face; ॥50॥
7.2.18.51: Vidyā from the throat down to the navel, Pratiṣṭhā below that in order down to the knees, and below that he should place Nivṛtti, and contemplate them. ॥51॥
7.2.18.52: Having placed the root mantra with its own seed-syllables and with the limbs, and knowing him the disciple to be of the nature of Śiva, he should invoke the god in the lotus of his heart and worship him. ॥52॥
7.2.18.53: Having invoked the eternal presence and identity with Śiva in the disciple, the guru should bring about the qualities in this disciple who is full of Śiva's radiance: ॥53॥
7.2.18.54: the powers beginning with aṇimā; saying, be gracious, he should offer three oblations. In the same way he should again confer on him the qualities: ॥54॥
7.2.18.55: omniscience, likewise contentment, knowledge without beginning or end, undiminished power, independence, and infinite power. ॥55॥
7.2.18.56: Then, having taken leave of the god, he should consecrate him with the jars of Sadyojāta and the rest, meditating in his heart on the Lord of gods in due order. ॥56॥
7.2.18.57: Then, having seated that disciple and worshipped Śiva as before, having obtained permission from Śiva, he should impart to him the Śaiva vidyā. ॥57॥
7.2.18.58: There he should impart it preceded by Oṃkāra, enclosed (sampuṭa), ending with namaḥ, joined with Śiva and Śakti; and the Śakti-vidyā of the same kind. ॥58॥
7.2.18.59: He should teach the seer, metre and deity, likewise the Śiva-nature of Śiva and Śivā, the worship of Śambhu with its surrounding deities (āvaraṇa), and the seats. ॥59॥
7.2.18.60: Having worshipped the Lord of gods again, he should inform Śiva: Whatever has been performed by me, make all of it well-done. ॥60॥
7.2.18.61: The guru, together with the disciple, having bowed to the god, stretched like a staff on the ground, should then dismiss him from the maṇḍala and also from the fire. ॥61॥
7.2.18.62: Then all those in the assembly who are worthy of honour should be honoured in order. ॥62॥
7.2.18.63: The assembly members together with the officiating priests should be served according to one's means. One should not be miserly with wealth if one desires one's own welfare. ॥63॥
7.2.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The purification of the six paths and the rest, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
7.2.19.1: Upamanyu said: Next I shall explain the rite known by name as sādhaka initiation, and the greatness of the mantra of this sacrament, which I indicated earlier in my account. ॥1॥
7.2.19.2: Having worshipped the god in the maṇḍala and installed him in the jar as before, and having offered oblations, the preceptor should lead the disciple, without a turban, to the maṇḍala on the ground. ॥2॥
7.2.19.3: Having performed the rite up to the full oblation as before, and likewise having offered a hundred oblations, the best of preceptors, having gratified the deity with the root mantra by means of the jars, ॥3॥
7.2.19.4: and having kindled the fire as before, and done in order what was stated earlier, having consecrated the disciple by sprinkling as before, he should impart the supreme mantra. ॥4॥
7.2.19.5: There, having performed in detail and in order the rite up to the instruction of the vidyā, he should hand over the Śaiva vidyā into the disciple's hand with flower-water, saying: ॥5॥
7.2.19.6: By the grace of the Supreme Lord, this great mantra will surely be for you the bestower of the fruit of all attainments in this world and the next. ॥6॥
7.2.19.7: Having said this and worshipped the god, the guru, having obtained permission from Śiva, should teach the sādhaka the mantra practice and Śiva-yoga. ॥7॥
7.2.19.8: Having heard the guru's instruction, the practitioner of the mantra should, step by step, perform the mantra-practice prior to its application. ॥8॥
7.2.19.9: The practice of the root mantra is called puraścaraṇa, because it is to be performed before (puraḥ) the act called application (viniyoga). ॥9॥
7.2.19.10: Mantra-practice is not absolutely obligatory for one seeking liberation; but if performed, it would be beneficial for him too, here and hereafter. ॥10॥
7.2.19.11: On an auspicious day, in an auspicious place, or at a time free from defects, with teeth and nails clean, bathed, having performed the morning rites, ॥11॥
