7.2.19.12: having adorned himself with such perfumes, garlands and ornaments as are available, wearing a turban and an upper garment, entirely in white, and composed, ॥12॥
7.2.19.13: in a temple, a house, or some other very charming place, seated on a comfortable posture practised beforehand, ॥13॥
7.2.19.14: having made his own body Śaiva by the method taught in the Śiva scriptures, having worshipped the Lord of the lord of gods, Īśvara Nakulīśvara, ॥14॥
7.2.19.15: having offered him milk-rice, having completed the worship in order, having bowed down to that god and having received permission from his mouth, ॥15॥
7.2.19.16: he should repeat the Śiva mantra ten million times, or half of that, or half of that again; or two million times, or else one million. ॥16॥
7.2.19.17: And then, eating only milk-rice free of salt and alkalis, in measured quantity, he should always be non-violent, forbearing, calm and self-controlled. ॥17॥
7.2.19.18: If milk-rice is not available, he may live eating fruits, roots and the like, which are prescribed by Śiva himself, each successive one being distinguished in order: ॥18॥
7.2.19.19: cooked oblation-rice (caru), alms-food, then grains of barley-meal, barley gruel, vegetables, milk, curd, ghee, roots, fruits, and then water. ॥19॥
7.2.19.20: And having consecrated with the mantra the foods to be chewed, eaten and so on, he should, especially during this practice, always eat in silence. ॥20॥
7.2.19.21: The observer of the vow should bathe in pure water from a river or stream, purified by a hundred and eight repetitions of the mantra, or else sprinkle himself, according to his ability. ॥21॥
7.2.19.22: Likewise he should daily offer libations and make oblations into the Śiva-fire with seven, five or three substances, or else with ghee alone. ॥22॥
7.2.19.23: For the Śaiva practitioner who thus propitiates Śiva with devotion, nothing whatever is hard to obtain here or in the hereafter. ॥23॥
7.2.19.24: Or else, even without the formal practice of the mantra, he should repeat the mantra a thousand times every day with one-pointed mind, while fasting. ॥24॥
7.2.19.25: Nothing is difficult for him to attain, nor is there anything inauspicious for him anywhere; having gained knowledge, prosperity and happiness here, he also attains liberation. ॥25॥
7.2.19.26: In the practice, in the application, and likewise in daily and occasional rites, he should do japa after bathing in order with water, with ash, and with mantra. ॥26॥
7.2.19.27: Pure, with tied tuft of hair, wearing the sacred thread, with a pavitra ring on the hand, bearing the tripuṇḍra and rudrākṣa, he should repeat the five-syllabled vidyā. ॥27॥
7.2.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The consecration of the sādhaka and the greatness of the mantra, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
7.2.20.1: Upamanyu said: Then the guru should consecrate as ācārya the disciple who has been thus purified and has performed the Pāśupata vow, because he is fit for it; and otherwise he should not. ॥1॥
7.2.20.2: Having made the maṇḍala as before and having worshipped the Supreme Lord, he should place five pitchers in the directions and in the centre, as before. ॥2॥
7.2.20.3: Having installed Nivṛtti in front (east), Pratiṣṭhā in the western pitcher, Vidyā in the south, Śānti in the north, and the supreme Śāntyatītā in the centre— ॥3॥
7.2.20.4: having performed the protective rites and so on there, having formed the cow-gesture (dhenu-mudrā), having consecrated the pots with mantras, and having made oblations up to the final full oblation as before— ॥4॥
7.2.20.5: the preceptor, having led the disciple into the maṇḍala without a turban, should perform the satiation (tarpaṇa) and other rites of the mantras, ending as before. ॥5॥
7.2.20.6: Then, having worshipped the Lord of gods and taken his leave as before, he should make that disciple mount the seat for the consecration. ॥6॥
7.2.20.7: Afterwards, having performed the sakalīkaraṇa on him—who embodies the five kalās and whose body has been invested with mantras—and having bound him, he should offer the disciple to Śiva. ॥7॥
7.2.20.8: Then, lifting the pots in order, beginning with the Nivṛtti pitcher and ending with the central one, he should bathe that disciple with the Śiva mantra alone. ॥8॥
7.2.20.9: Then the preceptor, having attained the state of Śiva, should place the Śiva-hand on the head of the novice and proclaim him a Śivācārya. ॥9॥
7.2.20.10: Then, having adorned him and worshipped the god in the Śiva-maṇḍala, having offered one hundred and eight oblations, he should then give the full oblation. ॥10॥
7.2.20.11: Again having worshipped the Lord of gods and prostrated on the ground like a staff, placing joined palms on his head, the guru should address Śiva: ॥11॥
7.2.20.12: O Lord, by your grace this man has been made a preceptor by me. O God, showing him favour, may your divine command be granted to him. ॥12॥
7.2.20.13: Having thus petitioned and again bowed together with the disciple, the guru should worship Śiva and the divine Śiva-scripture (Śivāgama) as he would Śiva. ॥13॥
7.2.20.14: Again taking Śiva's leave, the preceptor should then give the book of Śiva-knowledge to the disciple with both hands. ॥14॥
7.2.20.15: He (the disciple), placing that knowledge (the scripture) on his head, should set it upon the seat of knowledge, and, having saluted it properly, worship it. ॥15॥
7.2.20.16: Then the guru should also give him royal insignia, since one who has attained the rank of ācārya deserves even a kingdom. ॥16॥
7.2.20.17: Then he should give instruction, as practised by the ancients, as taught in the Śiva-scriptures, and as honoured among people. ॥17॥
7.2.20.18: Saying: Having carefully examined disciples by the marks stated in the Śiva-scriptures and having initiated them, the preceptor should impart Śiva-knowledge to them. ॥18॥
7.2.20.19: Likewise he should earnestly cultivate all this: freedom from strain, purity, forbearance, compassion, and also freedom from craving and from envy. ॥19॥
7.2.20.20: Having thus instructed that disciple and dismissed Śiva from the maṇḍala, he should worship the Śiva-pitcher, the fire and the rest, and also the assembly members. ॥20॥
7.2.20.21: Or else the guru together with his group may perform the saṃskāras simultaneously; in that case three or two stages of the procedure are taught to be combined. ॥21॥
7.2.20.22: At the very beginning he should arrange the pitchers as in the purification of the paths, having performed the whole samaya-saṃskāra except the consecration. ॥22॥
7.2.20.23: Having worshipped Śiva again and performed the purification of the paths, when that is completed he should worship the god once more. ॥23॥
7.2.20.24: Having offered oblations to the mantra, satiated it, kindled it, and invoked the blessing of the Lord, he should place the mantra in the disciple's hand and complete the rest. ॥24॥
7.2.20.25: Or else, having mentally gone through the entire mantra-saṃskāra in order, the guru should perform the purification of the paths ending with the consecration. ॥25॥
7.2.20.26: There, whatever procedure is prescribed for the kalās beginning with Śāntyatītā, all of it is to be performed in the purification of the three tattvas. ॥26॥
7.2.20.27: The triad of tattvas is declared to be named Śiva, Vidyā and Ātman. In Śakti arose Śiva, from him Vidyā, and from her the Ātman arose. ॥27॥
7.2.20.28: The path of Śāntyatītā is pervaded by Śiva; the higher one next to it by Vidyā; and the remaining path, in its entirety, by the Ātman, in order. ॥28॥
7.2.20.29: Considering the Śāmbhava initiation hard to attain, the wise who have mastered the meaning of the Śiva-scriptures should commend the Śākta saṃskāra, which has mantra as its root. ॥29॥
7.2.20.30: Thus I have told you everything—this fourfold nature of the rite called saṃskāra. O Kṛṣṇa, what more do you wish to hear? ॥30॥
7.2.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The special and other consecrations, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
7.2.21.1: Kṛṣṇa said: O Lord, I wish to hear about the daily and occasional rites taught in the Śaiva scriptures for those who follow the Śaiva way of life. ॥1॥
7.2.21.2: Upamanyu said: Rising from bed at dawn, he should meditate on the God together with Ambā. After thinking over his duties for the day, he should leave the house when the dawn has risen. ॥2॥
7.2.21.3: Then he should relieve himself in an unobstructed, solitary place. After cleansing himself according to the rules, he should clean his teeth. ॥3॥
7.2.21.4: If tooth-sticks are not available, and on the eighth lunar day and similar days, he should cleanse his mouth with twelve mouthfuls of water. ॥4॥
7.2.21.5: Afterwards, having sipped water according to the rule, he should take the water bath (vāruṇa), in a river, in a temple tank, in a lake, or even at home. ॥5॥
7.2.21.6: Placing the bathing materials on its bank, he should remove the outer dirt, smear himself with earth and bathe, and then smear himself with cow-dung. ॥6॥
7.2.21.7: Having bathed again and again, and either discarding the cloth or washing it, well bathed, he should then put on a clean garment like a king. ॥7॥
7.2.21.8: A celibate student, an ascetic, and a widow should not take the cleansing bath, a bath with perfumes and the like, or cleaning of the teeth. ॥8॥
7.2.21.9: Wearing the sacred thread, tying his topknot and entering the water, he should immerse himself, sip water properly, and draw a triple circle in the water. ॥9॥
7.2.21.10: Submerged in the water, he should again repeat the mantra as far as he can and remember Śiva. Rising and sipping water, he should sprinkle himself with that same mantra. ॥10॥
7.2.21.11: He should do so with a cow's horn together with darbha grass, or with a palāśa leaf, or a lotus leaf, or with his two hands, five times or just three times. ॥11॥
7.2.21.12: In a garden and the like, or at home, he should bathe with a vardhanī vessel or a pitcher; at the time of immersion he should sprinkle himself with waters consecrated by mantras. ॥12॥
7.2.21.13: But if he is unable to take the water bath, he should cleanse his body from the soles of the feet to the head with a clean wet cloth. ॥13॥
7.2.21.14: Or he may take the fire bath (āgneya, with ash), or the mantra bath, or a bath with the Śiva mantra. A bath consisting of intent contemplation of Śiva is called the inner (ātmīya) bath of the yogin. ॥14॥
7.2.21.15: According to the procedure prescribed in his own sūtra, beginning with mantra-accompanied sipping of water, he should perform the rites ending with the brahmayajña, after offering libations to the gods and others. ॥15॥
7.2.21.16: Having meditated on Mahādeva residing in the solar disc and worshipped him according to rule, he should then offer the arghya to that Śiva in the form of the Sun. ॥16॥
7.2.21.17: Or else, having done this as stated in his own sūtra, he should cleanse his hands; then, performing the hand-placement (karanyāsa), he makes his body complete with the mantras. ॥17॥
7.2.21.18: Having sprinkled himself, with a bunch of kuśa grass, with water held in the left hand mixed with fragrance and white mustard seeds and accompanied by the root mantra, ॥18॥
7.2.21.19: with the mantras beginning āpo hi ṣṭhā, and having smelled the remaining water through the left nostril only, he should visualise the God within as white. ॥19॥
7.2.21.20: And taking up the sin residing in the body, expelling it through the other (savya) nostril, he should visualize it, black in colour, as lying outside, cast upon a stone. ॥20॥
7.2.21.21: Then he should offer libations to the gods and especially to the sages, and to the beings and the ancestors, and give the arghya according to rule. ॥21॥
7.2.21.22: With water mixed with red sandal he should make on the ground a well-rounded circle a hand's breadth in size, adorned with red powder and the like. ॥22॥
7.2.21.23: There he should worship the Sun together with his surrounding retinue, with the mantra khakholkāya along with its limbs, for the attainment of happiness. ॥23॥
7.2.21.24: Making a circle again and worshipping it with its limbs, he should place there a golden vessel measuring a Magadha prastha, ॥24॥
7.2.21.25: and fill it with fragrant water mixed with red sandal, with red flowers and sesame seeds, together with kuśa grass and unbroken rice, ॥25॥
7.2.21.26: with dūrvā grass, apāmārga and cow products, or with plain water alone. Kneeling on the ground and bowing to the God in the circle, ॥26॥
7.2.21.27: and placing that vessel on his head, he should offer that arghya to Śiva. Or else, with cupped hands, taking water with darbha grass, with the root mantra, ॥27॥
7.2.21.28: he should throw it up to Śiva, who dwells in the sky in the form of the Sun. Then, after cleansing his hands, he should again perform the hand-placement. ॥28॥
7.2.21.29: Understanding Śiva as consisting of the five Brahman mantras, from Īśāna to Sadyojāta, he should take the ash, rub it with the mantras, and touch his limbs, ॥29॥
7.2.21.30: with those mantras, down to the feet: head, face, heart, private parts and feet, in order. Then, rubbing the whole body with the root mantra, he should put on another garment, ॥30॥
7.2.21.31: Having put it on and sipped water twice, sprinkling himself with water consecrated by the eleven mantras, and covering himself with another upper cloth, he should sip water twice and remember Śiva. ॥31॥
7.2.21.32: Again having placed the mantras on his hands, the mantra-practitioner should draw the tripuṇḍra with ash, straight, oblong and distinct, on the forehead, with fragrant water. ॥32॥
7.2.21.33: Whatever mark has been drawn with ash on the forehead—round, square, a dot, or a half-moon— ॥33॥
7.2.21.34: he should draw the same on the arms, on the head, and between the breasts. Smearing the whole body with ash is not equal to these tripuṇḍra marks. ॥34॥
7.2.21.35: Therefore he should draw the tripuṇḍra alone, without smearing. He should wear rudrākṣa beads on the head, the neck, the ears and the hand. ॥35॥
7.2.21.36: A gold-coloured, unbroken, fine bead, not worn by others, is auspicious. For brāhmaṇas and the others in order, the best are white, yellow, red and then black. ॥36॥
7.2.21.37: If that is not available, whatever is available may be worn, provided it is undefiled. Even then, a bead proper to the higher should not be worn by the lower, nor the lower by the higher. ॥37॥
7.2.21.38: One who is impure should not wear the bead; he should wear it at all times. In this way, at the three junctures of the day, or at two, or just once, ॥38॥
7.2.21.39: having performed the bath and the rest according to his ability, he should worship the Supreme Lord. Going to the place of worship, he should settle into a pleasing seat, ॥39॥
7.2.21.40: and, facing east or north, meditate on the God and the Goddess. He should bow to the teachers from Śveta to Nakulīśa, to their disciples, and to his own guru. ॥40॥
7.2.21.41: Then, having again bowed to the god Śiva, one should recite the group of eight names: Śiva, Maheśvara, Rudra, Viṣṇu, Pitāmaha, ॥41॥
7.2.21.42: Saṃsāravaidya, Sarvajña and Paramātman — this is the group of eight. Or else, having recited the single name Śiva more than eleven times, ॥42॥
7.2.21.43: and having meditated on a mass of radiance at the tip of the tongue for the allaying of illnesses and the like, having washed the feet and made the hands anointed with sandal paste, one should perform the placing of mantras on the hands (karanyāsa), preceded by the purification of the hands. ॥43॥
7.2.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The daily and occasional rites, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
7.2.22.1: Upamanyu said: Nyāsa is said to be of three kinds, following the order of sustenance (sthiti), origination (utpatti) and dissolution (laya). The sthiti-nyāsa is for householders, and the utpatti nyāsa for celibate students (brahmacārins). ॥1॥
7.2.22.2: For renunciants (yatis) the dissolution-nyāsa, and likewise for forest-dwellers. That same dissolution-nyāsa is for a woman without a husband; for a married woman of the household it should be sthiti. ॥2॥
7.2.22.3: For a maiden, again, utpatti. I shall now state the defining feature of the nyāsa: placement from the thumb to the little finger is called the sthiti-nyāsa. ॥3॥
7.2.22.4: Beginning from the right thumb and ending at the left thumb is declared the utpatti-nyāsa; the reverse is the dissolution (saṃhṛti). ॥4॥
7.2.22.5: One should place in due order the syllables beginning with na, each with the bindu; one should place Śiva on the fingers, and also on the two palms and the two ring fingers. ॥5॥
7.2.22.6: Then, having performed the astra-nyāsa in the ten directions with the astra-mantra, one should contemplate the five kalās beginning with Nivṛtti, which embody the five elements, ॥6॥
7.2.22.7: together with the lords of the five elements, endowed with their respective emblems, residing in the heart, throat, palate, the middle of the brows, and the brahmarandhra; ॥7॥
7.2.22.8: one should contemplate them, with their knots, by their respective seed-syllables, within those respective seeds. For their purification one should recite the five-syllabled vidyā. ॥8॥
7.2.22.9: Having restrained the vital breath according to the number of the guṇas, one should then cut the knot of the elements with the astra mantra itself, by means of the astra-mudrā. ॥9॥
7.2.22.10: One should unite the self—driven by the vital breath through the suṣumṇā channel and issuing out through the brahmarandhra—with the radiance of Śiva. ॥10॥
7.2.22.11: Afterwards, having dried up the body with the wind, one should burn it with the fire of Time (kālāgni). Then, by the upward process, having withdrawn the kalās by means of the wind, ॥11॥
7.2.22.12: and having withdrawn the burnt body, touching the kalās together with their lord, one should flood the body with nectar and set each in its proper place. ॥12॥
7.2.22.13: Or else, the body having been withdrawn and burnt, without the re-creation of the kalās, one should then perform the flooding with nectar of what has become ashes. ॥13॥
7.2.22.14: Then, into that body made of the vidyā (mantra), one should join through the brahmarandhra the self, shaped like a lamp-flame, issuing forth from Śiva. ॥14॥
7.2.22.15: Having meditated on it as having entered within the body into the heart-lotus, one should again sprinkle the body made of vidyā with a shower of nectar. ॥15॥
7.2.22.16: Then one should perform the hand-nyāsa, preceded by purification of the hands; and after that perform the body-nyāsa with the great mudrā. ॥16॥
7.2.22.17: Then, having done the limb-nyāsa by the method taught by Śiva, one should perform the syllable-nyāsa on the joints of the hands, feet and so on. ॥17॥
7.2.22.18: Then, having placed the six limbs together with the six jātis, one should afterwards perform the binding of the directions in due order, beginning with the south-east (Āgneya). ॥18॥
7.2.22.19: Or else one may perform only the five-limbed nyāsa beginning with the head, and likewise the six-limbed nyāsa, without the purification of the elements and the rest. ॥19॥
7.2.22.20: Having thus, in abbreviated form, purified body and self, and having attained the state of Śiva, one should worship the Supreme Lord. ॥20॥
7.2.22.21: But one who has the time and no confusion of mind should perform the nyāsa rite according to the extended procedure. ॥21॥
7.2.22.22: Among these, the first is the mātṛkā-nyāsa, next after it the brahma-nyāsa, third the praṇava-nyāsa, and after that the haṃsa-nyāsa. ॥22॥
7.2.22.23: The fifth nyāsa is said by the wise to consist of the five syllables. Of these one may perform one or several in rites such as worship. ॥23॥
7.2.22.24: Having placed a on the head and ā on the forehead, likewise i and ī on the two eyes, and u and ū on the two ears, ॥24॥
7.2.22.25: ṛ and ṝ on the two cheeks, ḷ and ḹ on the two nostrils, e and ai on the two lips, o and au on the two rows of teeth, in order, ॥25॥
7.2.22.26: aṃ on the tongue, and then aḥ is to be applied on the palate, in due order. One should place the ka-group on the right hand, on its five joints. ॥26॥
7.2.22.27: And likewise one should place the ca-group on the joints of the left hand; and the ṭa-group and ta-group on both feet. ॥27॥
7.2.22.28: pa and pha on the two sides, then ba and bha on the back and the navel; one should place ma on the heart. Then in due order on the skin and the rest, ॥28॥
7.2.22.29: one should place the letters from ya to sa on the seven bodily constituents (dhātus); ha within the heart, and kṣa between the two brows. ॥29॥
7.2.22.30: Having thus placed the fifty letters by the method of Rudra, one should place the five Brahmans (brahma-mantras), according to the divisions of limbs, faces and kalās. ॥30॥
7.2.22.31: Having performed the hand-nyāsa and the rest with them, or not, in order, one should assign these to the head, face, heart, private parts and feet. ॥31॥
7.2.22.32: Then one should assign the faces, beginning with the upper and ending with the western; and the five kalās of Īśāna on these five, in order. ॥32॥
7.2.22.33: Then the four kalās of Puruṣa are to be placed on the four faces, following the order beginning with the east. ॥33॥
7.2.22.34: On the heart, throat, shoulders, navel, belly, back and chest—the eight kalās of Aghora; also on the feet and the hands. ॥34॥
7.2.22.35: Afterwards one should contemplate the thirteen kalās of Vāmadeva on the anus, penis, thighs, knees, shanks, buttocks, hips and sides. ॥35॥
7.2.22.36: The eight kalās of Sadyojāta too the best knower of ritual should assign to the feet, the hands, the nose, the head and the arms. Having thus performed in due sequence the nyāsa of the thirty-eight kalās, ॥36॥
7.2.22.37: afterwards the wise knower of the praṇava should perform the praṇava-nyāsa: on both arms, on the elbows and on the wrists, ॥37॥
7.2.22.38: on the sides, belly, thighs and shanks, on the feet and likewise on the back. Having thus performed the praṇava-placement, the one skilled in nyāsa ॥38॥
7.2.22.39: should perform the haṃsa-nyāsa as taught in the Śaiva scripture: dividing the seed-syllable of haṃsa, placing it on the eyes and on the nostrils, ॥39॥
7.2.22.40: dividing it, on the arms, eyes, mouth, forehead, and on the ears, on the armpits, the shoulders, the sides and likewise the breasts. ॥40॥
7.2.22.41: On the waist, the two hands and the two ankles, or else by the method of the five limbs (pañcāṅga) — having performed this haṃsa-nyāsa, one should then place the five-syllabled mantra (pañcākṣarī), ॥41॥
7.2.22.42: according to the method stated before, by which Śiva-hood arises. One who is not Śiva should not practise the worship of Śiva; one who is not Śiva should not worship Śiva; one who is not Śiva should not meditate on Śiva; one who is not Śiva cannot attain Śiva. ॥42॥
7.2.22.43: Therefore, having made the body Śaiva and having abandoned the notion of being a bound soul (paśu), and contemplating, I am Śiva, one should perform the Śaiva rite. ॥43॥
7.2.22.44: The sacrifice of ritual action, the sacrifice of austerity, the sacrifice of japa which is higher than that, the sacrifice of meditation and the sacrifice of knowledge — these are proclaimed as the five sacrifices. ॥44॥
7.2.22.45: Some are devoted to the sacrifice of action, others to the sacrifice of austerity, still others to the sacrifice of japa, and likewise some to the sacrifice of meditation, ॥45॥
7.2.22.46: and others are devoted to the sacrifice of knowledge; each successive one is superior. The sacrifice of action is said to be twofold, by the distinction of being done with desire and without desire. ॥46॥
7.2.22.47: The one with desire, having enjoyed the objects of desire, being attached to desires, is born again. The desireless one, having enjoyed pleasures in Rudra's abode, then falling from there, ॥47॥
7.2.22.48: is born as one devoted to the sacrifice of austerity — there is no doubt about this. And the ascetic, again having enjoyed pleasures there and then falling from there, ॥48॥
7.2.22.49: is born on earth as a man devoted to japa and meditation. The mortal devoted to japa and meditation, here, by virtue of the excellence of that, ॥49॥
7.2.22.50: having obtained knowledge, very soon attains union with Śiva (śiva-sāyujya). Therefore even the sacrifice of action of embodied beings, enjoined by Śiva, leads to liberation; ॥50॥
7.2.22.51: when desireless; joined with desire, it will lead only to bondage. Therefore, among the five sacrifices, one should be intent on meditation and knowledge. ॥51॥
7.2.22.52: He who has meditation and knowledge has crossed the ocean of worldly existence. Free from faults such as violence, pure, a means of purifying the mind, ॥52॥
7.2.22.53: the sacrifice of meditation is therefore supreme, granting the fruit of final liberation. Just as servants working outside are not great sharers in the reward, ॥53॥
7.2.22.54: as is seen in a king's palace, so too here are the ritualists. For to meditators the subtle form of the Lord becomes directly perceptible, ॥54॥
7.2.22.55: just as here, for ritualists, the gross form is fashioned from clay, wood and the like. Therefore those devoted to the sacrifice of meditation, regarding gods made of stone and clay, ॥55॥
7.2.22.56: do not wholly resort to them, because they know the true nature of Śiva. The man who, abandoning Śiva abiding in the self, worships him outside, ॥56॥
7.2.22.57: is like one who throws away the fruit in his hand and licks his own elbow. From knowledge comes meditation, and from meditation knowledge again arises; ॥57॥
7.2.22.58: through both of these comes liberation; therefore one should be devoted to meditation. At the dvādaśānta, likewise on the crown of the head, on the forehead, between the eyebrows, ॥58॥
7.2.22.59: or at the tip of the nose, or likewise in the mouth, at the neck, and in the heart, or at the navel — the eternal seat — with a mind pierced by faith, ॥59॥
7.2.22.60: one should worship the God and the Goddess with the offerings of external worship. Or else one should worship daily in a liṅga, or even in a man-made image, ॥60॥
7.2.22.61: or in the fire, or on a sacrificial ground, with devotion and according to one's means. Or else one should worship the Supreme Lord both inwardly and outwardly. One devoted to inner worship may or may not perform external worship. ॥61॥
7.2.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named The daily and occasional rites taught in the Śaiva scriptures, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥22॥
7.2.23.1: Upamanyu said: I shall now briefly set out the explanation of the procedure of worship that was taught in the Śiva-scripture by Śiva himself to Śivā. ॥1॥
7.2.23.2: Whether or not one has first performed the inner worship as an auxiliary rite, ending with the fire-offering, one should afterwards perform the outer worship. ॥2॥
7.2.23.3: There, having mentally prepared the materials and purified them, having meditated on the god Vināyaka and worshipped him according to rule, ॥3॥
7.2.23.4: and having duly worshipped in the mind Nandīśa on the south and likewise Suyaśā on the north, the wise one should conceive a seat for the deity: ॥4॥
7.2.23.5: a seat furnished with the parts beginning with the ārādhana-seat — a lion-seat, a yoga-seat and the like, or a spotless lotus-seat endowed with the three tattvas. ॥5॥
7.2.23.6: Upon it one should meditate on Śiva together with Ambā, captivating to all, endowed with all auspicious marks, beautiful in every limb, ॥6॥
7.2.23.7: possessed of every excellence, adorned with all ornaments, with red lips, hands and feet, his face smiling white like jasmine and the moon, ॥7॥
7.2.23.8: resembling pure crystal, with three eyes like full-blown lotuses, four-armed, of noble limbs, bearing the lovely crescent of the moon, ॥8॥
7.2.23.9: with hands in the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, Hara holding the deer and the axe, with serpents as necklace and bracelets, with a lovely blue region of the throat, ॥9॥
7.2.23.10: beyond all comparison, with his attendants and retinue. Then one should contemplate Maheśvarī on his left side, ॥10॥
7.2.23.11: lustrous like the petals of a full-blown lotus, with wide and long eyes, a face like the full moon, and dark curling hair, ॥11॥
7.2.23.12: resembling the petals of a blue lotus, wearing the half-moon as her crest, with breasts very round, firm, high, smooth and full, ॥12॥
7.2.23.13: slender-waisted, broad-hipped, clad in a fine, delicate yellow garment, furnished with all ornaments, radiant with the mark on her forehead, ॥13॥
7.2.23.14: graced by tresses strewn with varied flowers, fitting in form in every respect, her face slightly bowed with modesty, ॥14॥
7.2.23.15: holding a shining golden lotus in her right hand, placing the other hand straight like a staff, seated on the great seat, ॥15॥
7.2.23.16: the severer of bonds, manifestly of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss. Having thus meditated on the god and the goddess upon the auspicious excellent seat, ॥16॥
7.2.23.17: one should worship them with devotion, with flowers of the heart, as with all the offerings. Or else, having thus conceived any one of the forms of the Lord — ॥17॥
7.2.23.18: the Śaiva form called Sadāśiva, or likewise the supreme Māheśvarī form, or the one named Ṣaḍviṃśaka, or else the one called Śrīkaṇṭha — ॥18॥
7.2.23.19: and having also performed the placing of mantras (nyāsa) and the rest on it just as on one's own body, and in this form meditating on Śiva as embodied, beyond the existent and the non-existent, ॥19॥
7.2.23.20: having meditated thus, one should complete the worship mentally following the very order of the outer rite. Afterwards one should mentally perform the fire-offering in the navel with fuel-sticks, ghee and the rest. ॥20॥
7.2.23.21: And between the eyebrows one should meditate on Śiva in the form of a pure lamp-flame. Thus, whether the inner worship is done as an auxiliary or independently, in the auspicious meditative yoga, ॥21॥
7.2.23.22: ending with the fire-rite, the procedure is the same in every case. Then, having completed the entire mental sequence of worship, ॥22॥
7.2.23.23: one should worship the god in the liṅga, or on the sthaṇḍila (prepared ground), or even in the fire. ॥23॥
7.2.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The explanation of the rite of worship, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥23॥
7.2.24.1: Upamanyu said: For purification, one should sprinkle the place of worship with water using the root mantra, and with water scented with fragrance and sandal one should place a flower there. ॥1॥
7.2.24.2: Having driven away the obstacles with the astra mantra, and having enclosed the place with the varma (armour) mantra, and having placed the astra in the directions, one should prepare the ground for worship. ॥2॥
7.2.24.3: Spreading darbha grass there, one should wash the vessels with sprinkling and so on; having purified all the vessels, one should perform the purification of the materials. ॥3॥
7.2.24.4: The sprinkling vessel (prokṣaṇī), the arghya vessel, after that the pādya vessel, and likewise the vessel for ācamana water — this is the set of four. ॥4॥
7.2.24.5: Having washed, sprinkled and looked upon them, one should then pour pure water into them, and put in all the auspicious substances as available. ॥5॥
7.2.24.6: Gems, silver, gold, fragrances, flowers, unbroken rice and the like, fruits, sprouts and darbha grass — these are auspicious substances of many kinds. ॥6॥
7.2.24.7: Into the bathing water one should put fragrances and the like, and especially into the drinking water one should put cool and pleasing flowers and so forth. ॥7॥
7.2.24.8: One should put uśīra (vetiver) and sandal into the pādya water; and nutmeg, kaṅkola, camphor, bahumūla and tamāla — ॥8॥
7.2.24.9: — these, having been powdered, one should especially put into the ācamana water; and cardamom, camphor and sandal into all the vessels. ॥9॥
7.2.24.10: Into the arghya vessel one should put tips of kuśa grass, unbroken rice, barley, paddy and sesame too, ghee, white mustard, flowers and sacred ash. ॥10॥
7.2.24.11: Into the sprinkling vessel one should put kuśa, flowers, barley, paddy, bahumūla, tamāla and sacred ash, in due order. ॥11॥
7.2.24.12: Having placed the mantra in all the vessels, having enclosed them on the outside with the varma mantra, and afterwards protecting them with the astra, one should display the dhenu-mudrā (cow gesture). ॥12॥
7.2.24.13: Then, having sprinkled all the articles of worship with water from the sprinkling vessel, one should purify them duly with the root mantra. ॥13॥
7.2.24.14: If all the vessels are not available, the best of practitioners should prepare a single sprinkling vessel for all rites, and with water prepare that common arghya. ॥14॥
7.2.24.15: Then, having duly worshipped Lord Vināyaka in order with foods to be chewed and eaten and so on, then on the right side of the door — ॥15॥
7.2.24.16: — one should properly worship Nandin himself, lord of the inner apartments, resembling a mountain of gold, adorned with all ornaments, ॥16॥
7.2.24.17: wearing the crescent moon as a crown, gentle, three-eyed and four-armed, the lord bearing a blazing trident, a deer, an axe and a sharp cane, ॥17॥
7.2.24.18: with a face like the orb of the moon, or else lion-faced. And on the north side of the door, one should worship his wife, daughter of the Maruts, ॥18॥
7.2.24.19: Suyaśā, of good vows, the mother, intent on adorning the feet of the Goddess. Having worshipped her, and having entered the inner shrine of the Supreme Lord, ॥19॥
7.2.24.20: having worshipped the liṅga with those materials, one should remove the remnants of the previous offering (nirmālya); having washed it, one should place a flower on its top for its purification. ॥20॥
7.2.24.21: Holding a flower in hand, one should repeat the mantra according to one's capacity for the purification of the mantra. Having worshipped Caṇḍa in the north-east, one should have the nirmālya given to him. ॥21॥
7.2.24.22: Afterwards one should construct the seat, beginning with the support (ādhāra), in due order. Then one should meditate on the auspicious, dark Ādhāraśakti upon the ground. ॥22॥
7.2.24.23: In front of her, one should visualise Ananta with raised neck, coiled in form, white, five-hooded, as if licking the sky. ॥23॥
7.2.24.24: Above him is the auspicious seat with four lion feet; dharma, knowledge, detachment and sovereignty are indeed its feet. ॥24॥
7.2.24.25: Placed at the south-east and the other intermediate quarters, they are white, red, yellow and dark in colour; adharma and the rest are placed at the east and the other quarters, ending with the north, in order. ॥25॥
7.2.24.26: Having placed them, one should visualise the limbs of the seat as resembling lapis lazuli. Its upper covering is a lotus seat, spotless and white. ॥26॥
7.2.24.27: They declare its eight petals to be the eightfold powers beginning with aṇimā; and its filaments the Rudras beginning with Vāma, together with the śaktis beginning with Vāmā. ॥27॥
7.2.24.28: The seeds also are those very śaktis, within, up to Manonmanī; the pericarp is supreme detachment, and the stalk is knowledge of the nature of Śiva. ॥28॥
7.2.24.29: The bulb is the essence of Śiva-dharma. At the end of the pericarp are the three discs; above the three discs is the seat consisting of the triad of principles beginning with ātman. ॥29॥
7.2.24.30: Above all the seats one should imagine a divine seat, comfortable, spread with variegated coverings, shining with pure knowledge (śuddhavidyā). ॥30॥
7.2.24.31: One should perform invocation, installation, confinement, gazing and obeisance, forming the mudrās for each separately. ॥31॥
7.2.24.32: Having offered water for the feet, water for sipping, arghya, fragrance, and after that flowers, incense, a lamp and betel, one should then bathe Śiva and Śivā. ॥32॥
7.2.24.33: Or else, having thus arranged the seat and the image, and having made it complete with limbs (sakalīkṛtya) by the root mantra, by the Brahma-mantras and likewise by others, ॥33॥
7.2.24.34: one should then invoke, together with the Goddess, Śiva, the supreme cause, the god resembling pure crystal, unmoving and imperishable, ॥34॥
7.2.24.35: the cause of all worlds, supreme, consisting of all worlds, standing within and without, pervading all, subtler than the subtle and greater than the great, ॥35॥
7.2.24.36: the imperishable Lord, seen without effort by devotees, yet beyond the reach even of gods such as Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu and Rudra, ॥36॥
7.2.24.37: the essence of the Vedas, heard in scripture to be beyond the reach even of the learned, without beginning, middle or end, the medicine for those afflicted with the disease of worldly existence, ॥37॥
7.2.24.38: renowned as the Śiva-principle, established in the world for its welfare. With devotion one should worship the excellent liṅga with the five services. ॥38॥
7.2.24.39: The liṅga is the form of Maheśa, Śiva, the Supreme Self. At the time of bathing one should perform auspicious acts such as shouts of victory. ॥39॥
7.2.24.40: He should be bathed with the five cow-products, ghee, milk, curd, honey and the like first, with roots, with the juices of fruits, and with sesame, mustard and barley-meal, ॥40॥
7.2.24.41: Having bathed the deity with approved grains such as barley and with powders made from black gram and the like, and having smeared it with flour-pastes and so on, one should bathe it with warm water. ॥41॥
7.2.24.42: One should rub it with bilva leaves and the like to remove the smell of the paste. Then, having bathed it again with waters, in the manner of service befitting an emperor, ॥42॥
7.2.24.43: one should offer fragrant āmalaka and turmeric in due order. Then, having cleansed the liṅga, or else the image, with waters, ॥43॥
7.2.24.44: one should bathe it with scented water, with water containing kuśa and flowers, and with waters containing gold and gems, consecrated by mantras, in due order. ॥44॥
7.2.24.45: But if the materials are unavailable, one should bathe Śiva with faith using whatever could be gathered, or with waters consecrated by mantras alone. ॥45॥
7.2.24.46: One should bathe him, preceded by mantras, with a pitcher, or with a conch, or with a vardhanī vessel, or with the hand, together with kuśa and flowers. ॥46॥
7.2.24.47: With the Pavamāna hymns, the Rudra hymn, the Nīla Rudra and the Tvarita Rudra, with hymns such as the Liṅga-sūkta, and with the Atharvaśiras, ॥47॥
7.2.24.48: with Ṛg verses, with Śaiva Sāman chants, and with the five Brahma-mantras, with the Śiva mantra and with the praṇava, one should bathe the Lord of the god of gods. ॥48॥
7.2.24.49: As one performs the bath and other rites for the God, so should one do for the Goddess; there is no difference whatsoever in that, since the two are equal. ॥49॥
7.2.24.50: Having first performed the bath and other rites for the God, one should afterwards perform them for the Goddess, by the command of the god of gods. ॥50॥
7.2.24.51: When Ardhanārīśvara is the object of worship, there is no order of before and after among the various services, whether in the liṅga or anywhere else. ॥51॥
7.2.24.52: Having performed the ablution of the liṅga and wiped it with a clean, fragrant cloth, one should offer a garment and a sacred thread. ॥52॥
7.2.24.53: Water for the feet, water for sipping, arghya, sandal paste, flowers, ornaments, incense, lamp, food offering, drinking water, and material for cleansing the mouth, ॥53॥
7.2.24.54: and again water for sipping, then after that mouth-perfume, and an auspicious, beautiful crown adorned with all kinds of gems, ॥54॥
7.2.24.55: pure ornaments and various garlands, two fans and two chowries, a parasol, a palm-leaf fan and a mirror, ॥55॥
7.2.24.56: Having offered these, one should perform the waving of lights (nīrājana), accompanied by the sounds of all auspicious instruments, by song, dance and the like, and with shouts of victory. ॥56॥
7.2.24.57: In a vessel of gold, silver or copper, or an auspicious earthen one, adorned with lotus designs, flowers, seeds, curd, unbroken rice and the like, ॥57॥
7.2.24.58: and marked with figures made of cow-dung—trident, a pair of conches, lotus, nandyāvarta, śrīvatsa, svastika, mirror, thunderbolt, fire and the like— ॥58॥
7.2.24.59: having placed eight lamps all around and one in the middle, one should meditate upon and worship in them the nine Śaktis beginning with Vāmā. ॥59॥
7.2.24.60: Having covered it with the Kavaca mantra and protected it on all sides with the Astra mantra, and having shown the cow-gesture (dhenumudrā), one should lift the vessel with both hands. ॥60॥
7.2.24.61: Or one may place five lamps on the vessel in order—in the intermediate directions and in the middle—or else just a single lamp. ॥61॥
7.2.24.62: Then, lifting that vessel, one should wave it in order above the liṅga and so on, circling three times clockwise, with the root mantra. ॥62॥
7.2.24.63: Then one should offer arghya and apply fragrant sacred ash on the head; having made an offering of a handful of flowers, one should afterwards present the food offerings. ॥63॥
7.2.24.64: Then one should give drinking water, and having again given water for sipping, one should present betel furnished with the five fragrant substances. ॥64॥
7.2.24.65: One should sprinkle what is to be sprinkled and have songs and dramatic performances conducted. Having meditated on Śiva and Śivā in the liṅga and so on, one should repeat the Śiva mantra according to one's capacity. ॥65॥
7.2.24.66: With humility one should perform circumambulation, prostration, praise, self-offering, and the submission of one's requests. ॥66॥
7.2.24.67: Having offered arghya and a handful of flowers and formed the mudrā according to rule, one should then beg the God's forgiveness and, having dismissed him from the external seat, meditate on him within oneself. ॥67॥
7.2.24.68: In great difficulty one may perform the services from pādya up to mouth-perfume, or just arghya and so on, or merely the scattering of flowers, with devotion foremost. ॥68॥
7.2.24.69: By that much alone, when done with devotion, supreme dharma is well accomplished. Without having worshipped Śiva, one should not eat as long as breath moves in the body. ॥69॥
7.2.24.70: If a sinful person eats willfully without worship, there is no expiation for him. But if one eats through negligence, one should vomit it out with effort, ॥70॥
7.2.24.71: bathe, worship the God and the Goddess twofold, fast, and practise ten thousand repetitions of Śiva's mantra, observing celibacy. ॥71॥
7.2.24.72: On the next day, having given gold and the like according to his means to Śiva or to a devotee of Śiva, and having performed a great worship, he becomes pure. ॥72॥
7.2.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The worship of Śiva taught in the scriptures, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥24॥
7.2.25.1: Upamanyu said: What was left unsaid here about worship, as if from fear of disrupting the sequence, that other matter I shall now explain, briefly and not at length. ॥1॥
7.2.25.2: Before the offering of the food oblation and after the offering of the lamp, one should perform the worship of the enclosures, or else when the waving of lights (nīrājana) has arrived. ॥2॥
7.2.25.3: There, in the first enclosure of Śiva or of Śivā, one should worship the mantras from Īśāna down to Sadyojāta, and also those from Rudra down to Astra. ॥3॥
7.2.25.4: They are placed in the northeast, in the eastern part, in the south, likewise in the north, and in the west; then in the southeast, in the northeast, likewise in the southwest, ॥4॥
7.2.25.5: in the northwest, again in the northeast, and after that in the four directions. This is called the inner enclosure (garbhāvaraṇa), or else the assemblage of mantras. ॥5॥
7.2.25.6: Or else one may worship the limbs from Hṛdaya up to Astra. Outside that, one should worship Śakra in the east and Yama in the south, ॥6॥
7.2.25.7: the wise one should worship Varuṇa in Varuṇa's quarter (west) and Dhanada in the north, Īśa in the northeast, Fire in his own quarter, and Nirṛti in the southwest; ॥7॥
7.2.25.8: Māruta in the northwest, Viṣṇu in the southwest, Vidhi (Brahmā) in the northeast. Outside the lotus one should worship also the weapons, beginning with the thunderbolt and ending with the lotus, ॥8॥
7.2.25.9: of well-known forms, belonging to the world-guardians, in their directions, in due order. All the deities of the enclosures, looking towards the god and goddess, ॥9॥
7.2.25.10: are to be meditated upon with palms joined in reverence, seated at ease. To all the enclosure deities, with their own names joined with namaḥ, ॥10॥
7.2.25.11: one should offer worship with flowers, having bowed to all of them in due order. Or one may worship only the inner enclosure, or with its own enclosure. ॥11॥
7.2.25.12: This holds in yoga, meditation, japa and homa, whether external or internal. The food offering to be given is of six kinds: plain rice, rice with mung beans, ॥12॥
7.2.25.13: milk-rice, rice mixed with curd, rice with jaggery, and rice steeped in honey. Of these, one or several, accompanied by various side dishes, ॥13॥
7.2.25.14: together with jaggery and sugar, one should offer; also excellent churned curd, eatables chiefly cakes, and sweet fruits; ॥14॥
7.2.25.15: and very cool drinking water, rich with red sandal and flowers; and soft pieces of areca nut steeped in cardamom juice; ॥15॥
7.2.25.16: and betel leaves combined with catechu and the like, pale, golden-coloured, properly prepared and auspicious; and white lime powder made from stone, not too dry and not spoiled; ॥16॥
7.2.25.17: and camphor, then cubeb, nutmeg and the like, fresh and fine. The unguent should be sandal, powdered from the root-wood; ॥17॥
7.2.25.18: musk, saffron, and a liquid made of musk. The flowers should be fragrant, pure and lovely. ॥18॥
7.2.25.19: Flowers that are scentless, strong-smelling, spoiled, stale, or fallen apart of themselves should not be offered in the worship of Śiva. ॥19॥
7.2.25.20: Garments should be soft, and ornaments especially made of gold, resembling rings of lightning. ॥20॥
7.2.25.21: All these should be fumigated with camphor, resin, aguru and sandal, and perfumed all around with masses of flowers. ॥21॥
7.2.25.22: Incense prepared with powders of sandal, aguru, camphor wood and guggulu, along with ghee and honey, is praised. ॥22॥
7.2.25.23: Lamps kept constantly burning with very fragrant ghee from a tawny (kapilā) cow, mixed with camphor, are commended. ॥23॥
7.2.25.24: The five cow-products, and sweet milk, curd and ghee likewise, from a tawny cow, are dear to Śambhu for bathing and for drinking. ॥24॥
7.2.25.25: And fine seats made of ivory, set with gold and gems, and colourful coverings; ॥25॥
7.2.25.26: and beds, high and low, lovely and comfortable, furnished with soft pillows and made of fine cotton. ॥26॥
7.2.25.27: Water brought from a river flowing to the ocean, or from a great stream, cool and strained through cloth, is especially good for bathing and drinking. ॥27॥
7.2.25.28: A parasol, moon-like and lovely, gleaming with strings of pearls, studded with the nine gems, divine, charming with its golden staff; ॥28॥
7.2.25.29: and two chowries, white and fine, adorned with gold, shaped like a pair of royal swans, beautified with jewelled handles; ॥29॥
7.2.25.30: and a mirror, very smooth, anointed with divine fragrance, covered all around with gems and adorned with fine garlands; ॥30॥
7.2.25.31: a conch of deep sound, resembling a swan, jasmine or the moon, inlaid with gems and gold at the mouth, the back and other parts; ॥31॥
7.2.25.32: and lovely trumpets (kāhala) producing various sounds, made of gold and adorned with pearls; ॥32॥
7.2.25.33: kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas, murajas, timicchas, paṭahas and the like, with a sound like the ocean, should be carefully provided. ॥33॥
7.2.25.34: Lovely utensils and vessels of every kind, and all their stands, one should have made of gold alone. ॥34॥
7.2.25.35: And the temple of Maheśa, Śiva, the Supreme Self, should be designed like a royal palace, with the features prescribed in the science of architecture (śilpaśāstra): ॥35॥
7.2.25.36: enclosed by high ramparts, with gateway towers shaped like mountains, covered with many gems, with golden doors and door-panels, ॥36॥
7.2.25.37: made of refined gold, surrounded by hundreds of jewelled pillars, rich with canopies of pearl strings, with arched gateways of coral, ॥37॥
7.2.25.38: its top adorned with divine golden crowning finials shaped like pots, and marked with the king of weapons (the trident), ॥38॥
7.2.25.39: and surrounded on all sides by residences fit for princes, beautified with royal roads and the like, and by mansions with lofty, towering spires, ॥39॥
7.2.25.40: and with excellent assembly halls standing in the directions and intermediate directions, its precincts exceedingly adorned, as though with inner enclosures. ॥40॥
7.2.25.41: The place should be attended by thousands of excellent women skilled in dance and song, and by many men accomplished in playing the flute and the vīṇā; ॥41॥
7.2.25.42: guarded by heroic guards equipped with elephants, horses and chariots; adorned with many flower gardens and many lakes, ॥42॥
7.2.25.43: and resplendent in the cardinal and intermediate directions with many long ponds; served by those who know the essence of the Vedas and Vedānta, devoted to the Śaiva scriptures, ॥43॥
7.2.25.44: by devotees delighting in the Śaiva way of life, bearing the marks taught in the Śaiva scriptures, tranquil, smiling-faced, prosperous, and devoted to right conduct, ॥44॥
7.2.25.45: served by illustrious twice-born Śaivas and Māheśvaras. Thus, whether inside or outside, in structures built according to one's means — ॥45॥
7.2.25.46: in a place made of stone, of ivory, of wood or of brick, or even simply of clay; or in a holy forest or on a mountain, ॥46॥
7.2.25.47: at a river, in a temple, in some other region, or in an auspicious house — whether rich or poor, without holding back his own capacity, one should worship the Lord with devotion using only wealth acquired by just means. ॥47॥
7.2.25.48: But even if one worships Śiva with devotion using wealth acquired by unjust means, there is no sin for him, since the Lord is subject to the devotee's feeling. ॥48॥
7.2.25.49: If one worships without devotion, even with wealth acquired by just means, he does not obtain its fruit; devotion alone is the cause here. ॥49॥
7.2.25.50: Whatever is done with devotion, according to one's wealth, with Śiva as its object — whether small or great — the fruit is equal for the rich and the poor. ॥50॥
7.2.25.51: A man, even of little wealth, should perform worship impelled by devotion; even one whose essence is great riches should not do it if devoid of devotion. ॥51॥
7.2.25.52: Even one who gives his entire possessions to Śiva, if devoid of devotion, does not by that become a partaker of the fruit; devotion alone is the cause here. ॥52॥
7.2.25.53: Not by extremely fierce austerities, nor by all the great sacrifices, can one reach the divine city of Śiva, leaving aside devotion directed to Śiva. ॥53॥
7.2.25.54: O Kṛṣṇa, more secret than the secret is devotion to Śiva, the Supreme Lord present everywhere; there is no doubt — one endowed with it is liberated. ॥54॥
7.2.25.55: Repetition of Śiva's mantra, meditation, fire-offering, sacrifice, austerity, scriptural learning, charity and study — all are for the sake of inner feeling; there is no doubt about this. ॥55॥
7.2.25.56: A man lacking devotional feeling is not liberated even after doing everything; but one possessed of feeling is liberated even without doing anything. ॥56॥
7.2.25.57: With thousands of Cāndrāyaṇa vows, likewise hundreds of Prājāpatya penances, month-long fasts and others — what more need has a devotee of Śiva of these? ॥57॥
7.2.25.58: Men without devotion perform austerities in this world and in mountain caves for the sake of meagre enjoyments; the devotee is liberated through his feeling. ॥58॥
7.2.25.59: Sāttvika action grants liberation; yogins are established in sattva. Ritualists enveloped by rajas would perform rājasa action, which grants powers (siddhi). ॥59॥
7.2.25.60: Asuras and rākṣasas, endowed with the quality of tamas, worship the Lord for worldly ends, and so do other men of that kind. ॥60॥
7.2.25.61: Whether resorting to a tāmasa, a rājasa or a sāttvika disposition, one who performs worship and the like with devotion attains welfare. ॥61॥
7.2.25.62: Since devotion has been fashioned like a boat to rescue one from the ocean of sin, what harm can rajas and tamas do to one endowed with devotion? ॥62॥
7.2.25.63: Whether an outcaste, a lowly person, a fool or one fallen, if he has taken refuge in Śiva, O Kṛṣṇa, he is worthy of worship by all gods and asuras. ॥63॥
7.2.25.64: Therefore, with every effort, one should worship Śiva with devotion alone, since for those without devotion there is no fruit anywhere. ॥64॥
7.2.25.65: I shall tell you a great secret; listen to my words, O Kṛṣṇa — a truth well established after deliberation by the Vedas, the śāstras and the knowers of the Veda. ॥65॥
7.2.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The worship taught in the Śaiva scriptures, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥25॥
7.2.26.1: Upamanyu said: Whether one is a slayer of a brāhmaṇa, a drinker of liquor, a thief, or one who has defiled his teacher's bed; or even a slayer of his mother, a slayer of his father, a slayer of a hero, or a slayer of an embryo — ॥1॥
7.2.26.2: — having worshipped with devotion Śiva, the supreme cause, even without mantras, he would be released from those various sins gradually, within twelve years. ॥2॥
7.2.26.3: Therefore even a fallen man should worship Śiva with every effort, if he is a devotee devoted to no other, living on alms, with senses subdued. ॥3॥
7.2.26.4: Even having committed a very great sin, if one worships the Lord of the gods with devotion using the five-syllabled mantra, he is freed from that sin. ॥4॥
7.2.26.5: Those who subsist on water, those who subsist on air, and others emaciated by vows — for them there is no reaching Śiva's world through these vows alone. ॥5॥
7.2.26.6: Whoever worships Śiva even once with devotion, using the five-syllabled mantra alone, he too goes to Śiva's abode, owing to the greatness of Śiva's mantra. ॥6॥
7.2.26.7: Therefore austerities and all sacrifices with one's entire property as fee — these are not equal even to a ten-millionth part of the worship of Śiva's image. ॥7॥
7.2.26.8: Whether bound or freed from the fetter, if the devotee worships with the five-syllabled mantra, he is released; there need be no deliberation about this. ॥8॥
7.2.26.9: Whether without the Rudra hymn or with the Rudra, one should worship Śiva with the Sūkta; the man who does so even once — though fallen or deluded — is liberated. ॥9॥
7.2.26.10: Or one should worship the god with the six-syllabled mantra or with the Sūkta-mantra — a devotee of Śiva who has conquered anger, whether he has not obtained or has obtained initiation. ॥10॥
7.2.26.11: Here the one who has obtained is superior to one who has not; of this there is no doubt. Or with that mantra together with the Brahma and Aṅga mantras and with the Haṃsa, one is liberated. ॥11॥
7.2.26.12: Therefore one should always worship Śiva with devotion using the Sūkta-mantra — once a day, twice, or three times, or constantly. ॥12॥
7.2.26.13: Those who worship Mahādeva are to be known as Maheśvaras themselves. But he by whom the blessed Śiva has not been worshipped with knowledge as his own helper — ॥13॥
7.2.26.14: — he wanders long in this saṃsāra, the ocean of sorrow. The fool who, having obtained the rare human birth, does not worship Śiva — ॥14॥
7.2.26.15: — fruitless is that birth of his, since it does not lead to liberation. Those who, having obtained the rare human birth, worship the Pināka-bearer — ॥15॥
7.2.26.16: — their birth is indeed fruitful; those best of men have attained their goal. And those who are intent on devotion to Bhava, whose minds are bowed to Bhava, ॥16॥
7.2.26.17: and engaged in constant remembrance of Bhava — they do not partake of sorrow. Charming mansions, women whose ornament is graceful charm, ॥17॥
7.2.26.18: and wealth beyond the point of satiety — these are the fruit of the rite of Śiva's worship. Those who desire great enjoyments and kingship in the abode of the gods, ॥18॥
7.2.26.19: they should long at all times for Hara's lotus feet. Good fortune, a lustrous form, strength, a disposition softened by generosity, ॥19॥
7.2.26.20: valour, and fame in the world come to one who worships Śiva. Therefore, abandoning everything, with mind fixed on Śiva alone, ॥20॥
7.2.26.21: one should perform the rite of Śiva-worship, if he desires his own welfare. Swiftly life departs, swiftly youth departs, ॥21॥
7.2.26.22: swiftly disease approaches; therefore the bearer of Pināka is to be worshipped. As long as death does not come, as long as old age does not overtake, ॥22॥
7.2.26.23: as long as the senses are not impaired, so long worship Śaṅkara. There is no other dharma in the three worlds equal to the worship of Śiva. ॥23॥
7.2.26.24: Knowing this, Sadāśiva should be worshipped with effort. The worship at the door, the curtain rite, the rite of bali to the retinue deities, ॥24॥
7.2.26.25: and the daily festival one should perform, if he worships in a temple. After the offering of the oblation-food, either he himself or an attendant ॥25॥
7.2.26.26: should give bali in due order to the retinue deities of the temple, going out with musical instruments and standing facing their respective directions. ॥26॥
7.2.26.27: He should offer flowers, incense, a lamp, and food along with water. Then, standing facing north, he should offer bali on the great pedestal. ॥27॥
7.2.26.28: Then whatever food and other things were offered earlier to the god — all of it, or what remains, he should offer to Caṇḍa. ॥28॥
7.2.26.29: Having then offered oblations into the fire duly, he should complete the rest of the worship. Having duly performed the application of the mantra, then the japa as prescribed for the mantra, ॥29॥
7.2.26.30: he should perform the daily festival as stated in Śiva's teaching. In a large vessel of metal, adorned with red lotuses, ॥30॥
7.2.26.31: having invoked there the divine Pāśupata weapon, he should worship it; and placing that vessel on the head of an adorned twice-born, ॥31॥
7.2.26.32: a twice-born whose body has the weapon placed on it by nyāsa and who holds a blazing staff — outside the temple's retinue deities, with auspicious sounds, ॥32॥
7.2.26.33: and with dancing, singing and the like, together with lamps, banners and so on, having made three circumambulations, neither hurried nor slow, ॥33॥
7.2.26.34: encircling the great pedestal by way of three circumambulations, the sacrificer, having entered again and standing at the door with joined palms, should take the vessel, bring it inside, and then dismiss the weapon. ॥34॥
7.2.26.35: Having performed the circumambulation and the rest in order, as stated before, and taking eight flowers, he should then conclude the worship. ॥35॥
7.2.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The rite of worship with all its parts and subsidiary parts, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥26॥
7.2.27.1: Upamanyu said: Now I shall describe the fire-rite, performed in a fire-pit, or on a prepared ground-altar, or on a vedi, or in an iron vessel, or in a new, auspicious earthen one. ॥1॥
7.2.27.2: Having installed the fire according to the rule and then having consecrated it, and having worshipped Mahādeva there, one should perform the homa rite. ॥2॥
7.2.27.3: One should make the fire-pit two hastas in measure, or only one hasta, either round or square; and likewise the vedi and the maṇḍala. ॥3॥
7.2.27.4: The pit should be as deep as it is wide; in its middle there should be an eight-petalled lotus, whose height is four aṅgulas, or just two aṅgulas. ॥4॥
7.2.27.5: They describe the navel (nābhi) within the pit with an elevation of twice a vitasti; and the aṅgula is reckoned as the space in the middle of the middle finger, between its middle and upper joints. ॥5॥
7.2.27.6: A hand (kara) is said by the wise to consist of twenty-four aṅgulas. Three girdles (mekhalā), or two, or else one — ॥6॥
7.2.27.7: one should make, as looks beautiful, smooth, pleasing and firm, with clay. The yoni should be made like an aśvattha leaf, or like an elephant's lip. ॥7॥
7.2.27.8: One should make it from the middle of the girdle, on the west or on the south, beautiful, slightly lowered towards the front, gradually opening out, ॥8॥
7.2.27.9: with its tip facing the pit, slightly leaving the girdle. For the vedi there is no rule of height; it may be of clay or of sand. ॥9॥
7.2.27.10: The maṇḍala is made with cow-dung water; the size of the vessel is not prescribed. One should smear the pit, the earthen vessel and the vedi with cow-dung water. ॥10॥
7.2.27.11: Having washed the metal vessel one should heat it; the others one should sprinkle with water. Then one should draw lines on the pit and the rest in the manner stated in one's own sūtra. ॥11॥
7.2.27.12: Having sprinkled it, one should prepare the seat for the fire with darbha grass or flowers, and should get ready all the materials for worship and for the oblation. ॥12॥
7.2.27.13: Having washed what is to be washed, one should purify it by sprinkling with the prokṣaṇī water. Fire produced from a gem, or produced from wood, or coming from a śrotriya's house, ॥13॥
7.2.27.14: or another honoured fire, one should then bring along with its container. Having circled it clockwise three times over the pit and the rest in due order, ॥14॥
7.2.27.15: and having uttered the fire-seed syllable, one should place the fire on its seat, either by way of the yoni, or likewise facing oneself. ॥15॥
7.2.27.16: The wise one, standing at the yoni area, should do this for the whole pit. The fire residing within his own navel, issuing like a spark from its aperture, ॥16॥
7.2.27.17: having come out, one should visualize it as merged into the outer fire, in the form of an orb. Everything up to the consecration of the ghee, beginning with the anvādhāna (adding fuel), ॥17॥
7.2.27.18: the knower of mantras should perform in the sequence stated in his own sūtra, with the root mantra. Having worshipped Śiva's form, then on the right side, ॥18॥
7.2.27.19: having placed the mantra in the ghee, one should show the mudrā called dhenu. The sruk and sruva to be used should be of bright metal, not of bell-metal, iron or lead, ॥19॥
7.2.27.20: or made of sacrificial wood, or as prescribed in smṛti and approved by craftsmanship; or a leaf of the palāśa (brahma-tree) and the like, without holes and raised in the middle. ॥20॥
7.2.27.21: Having wiped those two with darbha and heated them in the fire, one should sprinkle them again. Having sprinkled around in the order stated in one's own sūtra, with mantras preceded by Śiva, ॥21॥
7.2.27.22: one should offer with eight seed-syllables for the accomplishment of the fire's consecration: bhruṃ, stuṃ, bruṃ, śruṃ in order, and after that puṃ, ḍruṃ, druṃ. ॥22॥
7.2.27.23: These are the seven seed-syllables of the seven tongues in due order. The middle tongue, three-crested, is named Bahurūpā. ॥23॥
7.2.27.24: Of it, the flame on the south is Jvalantī, another on the left; the north-eastern tongue is Hiraṇyā; Kanakā stands in the east. ॥24॥
7.2.27.25: Raktā is in the south-east, Kṛṣṇā in the south-west; another is held to be Suprabhā; the tongue of the wind-quarter (north-west) is Atiriktā — each with a radiance matching its name. ॥25॥
7.2.27.26: Each is to be uttered after its own seed-syllable, ending with svāhā, in due order. Having offered ghee with the tongue-mantras into the tongues one by one in order, ॥26॥
7.2.27.27: and having offered three oblations in the middle with raṃ vahnaye svāhā, one should perform the sprinkling around, with ghee or with fuel sticks. ॥27॥
7.2.27.28: When this is done it becomes Śiva's fire; one should visualize Śiva's seat there. Having invoked the god Śiva, the Ardhanārīśvara, there, one should worship him, offering up to the lamp; then, having sprinkled around, one should perform the oblation of fuel sticks. ॥28॥
7.2.27.29: Those sticks should be of palāśa, or of other sacrificial trees, twelve aṅgulas long, not crooked, not dried of themselves, with bark, without blemish, and even. ॥29॥
7.2.27.30: Or ten aṅgulas long are prescribed, as thick as the little finger; or, if those are unavailable, a span (prādeśa) long; and all of them should be offered whole. ॥30॥
7.2.27.31: One should offer the ghee oblation shaped like a dūrvā leaf, four aṅgulas long; afterwards food in portions the size of an akṣa nut, ॥31॥
7.2.27.32: likewise parched grain, mustard seeds, barley and sesame, and, where possible, foods to be eaten, licked and sucked, smeared with ghee. ॥32॥
7.2.27.33: Ten oblations are to be offered there, or five, or three, according to one's capacity; or one may offer just a single oblation. ॥33॥
7.2.27.34: Ghee is offered with the sruva, fuel sticks and the like with the sruk, the rest with the hand; there one should offer by the divine tīrtha, or likewise by the sages' tīrtha of the hand. ॥34॥
7.2.27.35: If the others are unavailable, one may offer with a single substance, with faith. Again, for expiation one should offer three oblations after consecrating them with mantras. ॥35॥
7.2.27.36: Then, having filled the sruk with the ghee left over from the homa, and placed a flower at its tip, covering it with the sruva turned face down, ॥36॥
7.2.27.37: having covered it together with darbha, rising up with joined hands, one should offer with the root mantra ending in vauṣaṭ a stream of ghee as thin as a barley grain. ॥37॥
7.2.27.38: Having thus made the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti), one should sprinkle around as before. Then, having bidden farewell to the Lord of the gods, one should preserve the fire. ॥38॥
7.2.27.39: Or, having bidden farewell to that fire too, having united it in the navel, one should worship daily. Or else, having brought the fire by the method stated in the Śaiva scriptures, ॥39॥
7.2.27.40: one should duly consecrate and worship the fire born from the womb of Vāgīśī; having again done the anvādhāna and laid the enclosing sticks, ॥40॥
7.2.27.41: Having placed the vessels in pairs, and then having worshipped Śiva, having cleansed the sprinkling-vessel (prokṣaṇī) and sprinkled them with its water, ॥41॥
7.2.27.42: having set the praṇītā vessel, filled with water, in the north-east, having performed the rites up to the consecration of the ghee, and having cleansed the ladle (sruk) and spoon (sruva), ॥42॥
7.2.27.43: and then having performed the garbhādhāna, puṃsavana and sīmantonnayana rites, offering oblations separately for each, he should contemplate the fire as born. ॥43॥
7.2.27.44: He should contemplate him as three-footed, seven-handed, four-horned, two-headed, honey-tawny, three-eyed, crowned with matted locks and the moon, ॥44॥
7.2.27.45: red, with red garments and unguents, adorned with garlands and ornaments, endowed with all auspicious marks, wearing the sacred thread, with a triple girdle, ॥45॥
7.2.27.46: holding a spear (śakti) and the ladle and spoon in the right hands, and likewise with the others a javelin, a palm-leaf fan and a ghee vessel. ॥46॥
7.2.27.47: Having thus meditated on the born fire of this form, he should perform the birth-rite (jātakarma). Having done the removal of the navel cord, and then having cleared the birth-impurity, ॥47॥
7.2.27.48: having given it the name Śivāgniruci, preceded by an oblation, and having dismissed the parents, he should perform tonsure, initiation (upanayana) and the rest, ॥48॥
7.2.27.49: having performed its saṃskāras up to the conclusion of the Āptoryāma, and having done the homa beginning with the stream of ghee, then the sviṣṭakṛt oblation, ॥49॥
7.2.27.50: after that he should sprinkle around the fire with the seed-syllable raṃ. Of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and Īśāna, and likewise of the guardians of the worlds, ॥50॥
7.2.27.51: and of their weapons, having performed worship all around in due order, the one who knows the rite, taking out fire for the purpose of incense, lamps and the like, ॥51॥
7.2.27.52: and having again prepared the materials beginning with ghee, having arranged a seat in the fire and invoked there as before, ॥52॥
7.2.27.53: and having worshipped the God and the Goddess, he should then perform the rite ending with the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti). Or else the fire-rite prescribed for one's own āśrama, as an offering to Śiva, ॥53॥
7.2.27.54: understanding it thus, the follower of the Śiva-āśrama should perform; there is no other rule there. Ash is to be collected from the Śiva-fire, or that arising from the agnihotra, ॥54॥
7.2.27.55: or even that produced from the wedding-fire, well-burnt, pure and fragrant. Dung of a tawny cow, caught in the air while falling, is recommended, ॥55॥
7.2.27.56: neither wet nor too hard, not foul-smelling nor dried out. If it has fallen to the ground, he should take it after discarding the top and bottom. ॥56॥
7.2.27.57: Having made it into balls, he should throw it into the Śiva-fire etc. with the root mantra. Rejecting the under-burnt and over-burnt, taking the white ash, ॥57॥
7.2.27.58: having taken it, or having stirred it well, he should deposit it in an ash-receptacle — of metal, wood, clay or stone, ॥58॥
7.2.27.59: or he should provide some other beautiful, clean ash-receptacle. He should deposit the ash, like wealth, in a level, auspicious, clean place. ॥59॥
7.2.27.60: When setting out, he should take the ash himself, or an attendant may. He should not give it into an unfit hand, nor drop it on an impure surface; he should not touch it with the lower limbs, nor neglect it, nor step over it. ॥60॥
7.2.27.61: Taking the ash from there, he should apply it with mantras at the prescribed times, not otherwise; nor should he have it given to the unworthy. ॥61॥
7.2.27.62: He should collect the ash while the deity has not yet been dismissed, because once the dismissal is done it becomes Caṇḍa's ash. ॥62॥
7.2.27.63: After the fire-rite is done, he should perform the bali offering according to the method taught in the Śiva scriptures, or in the manner prescribed in his own sūtra. ॥63॥
7.2.27.64: Then, placing the seat of knowledge on a well-smeared maṇḍala and installing the treasury of knowledge (the scripture), he should worship it in order with flowers and so on. ॥64॥
7.2.27.65: Making a maṇḍala for the guru too in front of the scripture, and setting an excellent seat there, he should worship the guru with flowers and so on. ॥65॥
7.2.27.66: Then he should honour those worthy of honour and feed the hungry; then he himself may eat pure food at ease. ॥66॥
7.2.27.67: Or he may eat what was offered to the God, its remainder, for self-purification, with faith and not from greed — but not what was offered to Caṇḍa. ॥67॥
7.2.27.68: For perfume, garlands and whatever else was offered, the same rule applies; but the discerning man should not there think, I am Śiva. ॥68॥
7.2.27.69: Having eaten and sipped water, meditating on Śiva in the heart, he should utter the root mantra, and spend the rest of the time in suitable pursuits such as discourses on the Śiva scriptures. ॥69॥
7.2.27.70: At night, when the first part has passed, having performed a charming worship, he should prepare a single, very beautiful bed for Śiva and Śivā, ॥70॥
7.2.27.71: and likewise food to chew and eat, garments, unguents, flowers, garlands and so on — making everything charming, either mentally or in actual deed. ॥71॥
7.2.27.72: Then, pure, he should sleep at the feet of the God and the Goddess — a householder together with his wife, and others alone. ॥72॥
7.2.27.73: Perceiving the time of dawn, he should utter the primal mantra, bowing mentally to the imperishable God with Ambā and with his gaṇas. ॥73॥
7.2.27.74: Having performed, as far as he is able, purification and the rest as befits place and time, he should awaken the God and the Goddess with divine sounds of conches and the like. ॥74॥
7.2.27.75: Then, having completed the worship of Śiva and Śivā with very fragrant flowers that have bloomed at that time, he should begin the rite described before. ॥75॥
7.2.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The fire rite, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥27॥
7.2.28.1: Upamanyu said: Hereafter I shall explain, according to the path taught in the Śaiva scriptures, the order of the occasional (naimittika) rites for those who follow the Śaiva way of life (śiva-āśrama). ॥1॥
7.2.28.2: In all the months, in both fortnights, on the eighth and the fourteenth lunar days, and likewise on the parvan days, in due order, ॥2॥
7.2.28.3: at the solstices and equinoxes, and especially at eclipses, a great worship should be performed, or even a greater one, according to one's ability. ॥3॥
7.2.28.4: Every month, having duly prepared the brahmakūrca, and having bathed Śiva with it, one who has fasted should drink the remainder. ॥4॥
7.2.28.5: For faults such as the slaying of a brahmin, however exceedingly great, no other expiation surpasses the drinking of the brahmakūrca. ॥5॥
7.2.28.6: In Pauṣa, under the asterism Puṣya, one should perform the waving of lights (nīrājana) for the Lord; in Māgha, under the asterism called Maghā, one should offer a ghee-blanket. ॥6॥
7.2.28.7: In Phālguna, at the end of Uttarā Phalgunī, one should begin the great festival; in Caitra, on the full moon of Citrā, one should perform the swing festival according to rule. ॥7॥
7.2.28.8: On the Vaiśākha full moon under Viśākhā one should make a great flower-pavilion; in Jyeṣṭha, under the asterism called Mūla, one should cause a cool water-pot to be offered. ॥8॥
7.2.28.9: In Āṣāḍha, under Uttarāṣāḍhā, likewise the placing of the pavitra threads; in Śrāvaṇa one should prepare other maṇḍalas made of natural materials. ॥9॥
7.2.28.10: Under the asterism called Śraviṣṭhā, and thereafter on the full moon of Prauṣṭhapada, one should perform the water-play with sprinkling, on the day connected with Pūrvāṣāḍhā. ॥10॥
7.2.28.11: Then on the Āśvayuja full moon one should offer milk-rice and newly cooked rice, and with that very food perform the fire-rite on the day of Śatabhiṣaj. ॥11॥
7.2.28.12: On the Kārttika full moon, in conjunction with Kṛttikā, one should offer a thousand lamps; likewise in Mārgaśīrṣa, under Ārdrā, one should bathe Śiva with ghee. ॥12॥
7.2.28.13: One who is unable to do these at those times may perform simply a festival, or an assembly (āsthāna), or a great worship, or an enhanced worship. ॥13॥
7.2.28.14: And when an auspicious event occurs, and in praiseworthy undertakings; in dejection, in misconduct, after a bad dream, or on seeing an evil sight, ॥14॥
7.2.28.15: in a portent or any other inauspicious thing, or in a severe illness, rites such as bathing, worship, japa, meditation, fire-offering and gifts ॥15॥
7.2.28.16: should be performed suited to the occasion, preceded by puraścaraṇa. And if the Śiva-fire is extinguished, one should kindle it again. ॥16॥
7.2.28.17: He who, firmly established in the dharma of Śarva, lives thus, ever diligent—to him Maheśvara grants liberation in a single birth. ॥17॥
7.2.28.18: Whoever performs this in ever-increasing measure in the daily and occasional rites goes to the divine, primal abode of Śrīkaṇṭhanātha. ॥18॥
7.2.28.19: There, having enjoyed great pleasures for a hundred crore kalpas, the man, falling from there in the course of time, reaches the world of Umā and that of Kumāra, ॥19॥
7.2.28.20: having attained the Vaiṣṇava and Brāhma worlds, and especially Rudraloka, and having dwelt there for a long time enjoying the pleasures described, ॥20॥
7.2.28.21: and again going upward from there, passing beyond the five abodes, he obtains knowledge from Śrīkaṇṭha and from there goes to the city of Śiva. ॥21॥
7.2.28.22: One devoted to half the practice likewise proceeds in the same way, but with two returns; afterwards, obtaining knowledge, he attains union (sāyujya) with Śiva. ॥22॥
7.2.28.23: But the embodied one who has practised a quarter (half of half), after the end of the body, passing beyond the two worlds—up to the end of the cosmic egg or upward to the Unmanifest— ॥23॥
7.2.28.24: having reached the Pauruṣa and Raudra abodes of the Lord of the mountain-king's daughter, and having enjoyed pleasures in many ways for many thousands of yugas, ॥24॥
7.2.28.25: when his merit is exhausted, reaches the earth and is born in a great family. There too, by the force of former impressions, he of great splendour ॥25॥
7.2.28.26: abandons the dharmas of the bound soul (paśu) and becomes devoted to Śiva's dharma; by the very weight of that dharma, meditating, he goes to the city of Śiva. ॥26॥
7.2.28.27: Having enjoyed various pleasures, he goes to the station of the Vidyeśvaras; there, having enjoyed many pleasures along with the Vidyeśvaras in succession, ॥27॥
7.2.28.28: he returns once more, whether within or outside the cosmic egg. Then, obtaining knowledge of Śiva and attaining supreme devotion, ॥28॥
7.2.28.29: and attaining likeness in nature to Śiva, he does not return again. And he who is intensely devoted to Śiva, as one whose mind is attached to sense-objects is attached to them, ॥29॥
7.2.28.30: he is liberated, whether he performs the Śiva-dharmas or not. The one who returns once, twice, or thrice is a returner; ॥30॥
7.2.28.31: one who has the qualification for Śiva-dharma would not again become merely a universal emperor. Therefore, taking refuge in Śiva for whatever reason, ॥31॥
7.2.28.32: one should set one's mind on Śiva-dharma, if one has made effort for the highest good. In this matter we shall not compel anyone by any means. ॥32॥
7.2.28.33: Through compulsion and excessive argument this does not, by their nature, appeal to some; but it does appeal to others through the weight of meritorious impressions— ॥33॥
7.2.28.34: to those in whom the cause of worldly existence is not able to sprout. Therefore, having fully considered this in accordance with one's nature, ॥34॥
7.2.28.35: one should take up Śiva-dharma, if one desires one's own welfare (śiva). ॥35॥
7.2.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The rules for daily and occasional rites, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥28॥
7.2.29.1: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Lord, from your own mouth I have heard, equal to the Veda, the daily and occasional rites taught by Śiva for those who have taken refuge in him. ॥1॥
7.2.29.2: Now I wish to hear: if there is also a desire-motivated (kāmya) rite for those qualified for Śiva's dharma, please describe it now. ॥2॥
7.2.29.3: Upamanyu said: There is rite whose fruit is in this world, some whose fruit is in the next, and some for both this world and the next; and that again is fivefold. ॥3॥
7.2.29.4: Some rite consists of ritual action; some rite consists of austerity; ॥4॥
7.2.29.5: some consists of japa and meditation, and some of all these. The one consisting of ritual action is further divided according to the sequence of fire-offering, gift, and worship. ॥5॥
