7.2.29.6: It becomes fruitful only for those endowed with full power, not for others; and that power is the command of Maheśa, Śiva, the supreme Self. ॥6॥
7.2.29.7: Therefore a twice-born who bears Śiva's command should perform the desire-motivated rites. Now I shall describe the kāmya rite that bestows fruit here and hereafter. ॥7॥
7.2.29.8: It is to be performed by Śaivas and Māheśvaras, internally and externally respectively. Śiva and Maheśvara are not absolutely different here. ॥8॥
7.2.29.9: Just so, Śaivas and Māheśvaras too are not different. Those men who depend on Śiva and delight in the sacrifice of knowledge are Śaivas; ॥9॥
7.2.29.10: those devoted to the sacrifice of action on earth are called Māheśvaras. Therefore Śaivas should perform the rite internally, Māheśvaras externally. ॥10॥
7.2.29.11: But the procedure of the rite about to be described does not differ. Having duly examined the ground by its smell, colour, taste and so on, ॥11॥
7.2.29.12: there, on a surface of the ground pleasing to the mind, with a canopy spread above, well smeared with cow-dung, resembling the inside of a mirror, ॥12॥
7.2.29.13: one should first determine the east by the method seen in the scriptures, and lay out a maṇḍala of one or two cubits. ॥13॥
7.2.29.14: One should draw a spotless eight-petalled lotus with its pericarp, with powders of gems, gold and the like, gathered as available, ॥14॥
7.2.29.15: furnished with five enclosures and full of great beauty. On the petals the siddhis are to be imagined; on the filaments, together with their śaktis, ॥15॥
7.2.29.16: the eight Rudras beginning with Vāma, in order from the eastern petal onward; in the pericarp, dispassion; in the seeds, the nine śaktis; ॥16॥
7.2.29.17: in the bulb, dharma of Śiva's nature; in the stalk, knowledge resting on Śiva; and above the pericarp, the circles of fire, sun and moon; ॥17॥
7.2.29.18: beyond that, the triad of principles called Śiva-, Vidyā- and Ātma-tattva; and above all the seats, a comfortable seat adorned with various flowers. ॥18॥
7.2.29.19: One should worship Śiva with the five enclosures, together with Ambā — him who resembles pure crystal, serene, of cool radiance, ॥19॥
7.2.29.20: adorned with a crown of matted locks like a ring of lightning, clad in tiger skin, his lotus-face slightly smiling, ॥20॥
7.2.29.21: whose soles, palms and lower lip are like red lotus petals, endowed with all auspicious marks, adorned with all ornaments, ॥21॥
7.2.29.22: bearing excellent divine weapons, anointed with divine fragrances, five-faced, ten-armed, with a crescent moon as crest-jewel. ॥22॥
7.2.29.23: His eastern face is gentle, with radiance like the rising sun, rich with three lotus-eyes, crested with the young moon. ॥23॥
7.2.29.24: The southern face has a lovely radiance like a dark rain-cloud, is crooked with frowning brows, fearsome, with three round red eyes, ॥24॥
7.2.29.25: dreadful with fangs, unassailable, with quivering bud-like lower lip. The northern face resembles coral, adorned with dark curls, ॥25॥
7.2.29.26: graceful, three-eyed, with the moon as ornament on its crest. The western face shines like the full moon, brilliant with three eyes, ॥26॥
7.2.29.27: bearing the crescent, gentle, charming with a soft smile. The fifth face resembles crystal, radiant with the lunar crescent, ॥27॥
7.2.29.28: exceedingly gentle, shining with three wide-open eyes. He is resplendent on the right with trident, axe, thunderbolt, sword and fire, ॥28॥
7.2.29.29: and on the left resplendent with serpent, iron arrow, bell, noose and goad. His form is enclosed up to the knees by Nivṛtti, up to the navel by Pratiṣṭhā, ॥29॥
7.2.29.30: likewise up to the throat by Vidyā, up to the forehead by Śāntā, and above that by the supreme kalā called Śāntyatītā, ॥30॥
7.2.29.31: pervading the five paths, his body directly made of the five kalās; the god whose crown is Īśāna, the ancient one whose face is called Puruṣa, ॥31॥
7.2.29.32: whose heart is Aghora, likewise whose secret part is Vāma, Maheśvara, whose feet are Sadya; his form consisting of thirty-eight kalās, ॥32॥
7.2.29.33: the Lord consisting of the Mātṛkā letters, likewise consisting of the five Brahmas, consisting of what is called Oṃkāra, and endowed with the Haṃsa-śakti, ॥33॥
7.2.29.34: likewise whose lap is occupied by the śakti whose nature is Will, with the śakti called Knowledge on the right and the one called Action on the left, ॥34॥
7.2.29.35: Sadāśiva, consisting of the three tattvas, the very embodiment of Vidyā — having conceived this form with the root mantra and having performed sakalīkaraṇa in due order, ॥35॥
7.2.29.36: and having worshipped duly up to the arghya with the root mantra, then invoking Śiva himself in embodied form together with the supreme Śakti, ॥36॥
7.2.29.37: having invoked there Mahādeva, who is free from manifestation as being or non-being, and having performed the five preparatory acts, one should worship the supreme Lord ॥37॥
7.2.29.38: with the Brahma mantras and the six limbs, then with the Mātṛkā, with the praṇava, and with the Śiva mantra joined with Śakti, in order, ॥38॥
7.2.29.39: or with the Śānta mantra, and likewise with other Vedic mantras in full; or one may worship the supreme God with the Śiva mantra alone. ॥39॥
7.2.29.40: Having made the offerings from foot-water up to mouth-freshener, without the dismissal, one should then begin the worship of the five enclosures in due order. ॥40॥
7.2.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named Rites for desired ends, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥29॥
7.2.30.1: There, at the very beginning, one should first worship with fragrance and the rest the two gods Heramba and Ṣaṇmukha, beside Śiva and Śivā, on the right and on the left respectively. ॥1॥
7.2.30.2: Then, all around, in the first enclosure, one should worship the Brahmans, the five brahma-mantras, together with their Śaktis, in due order from Īśāna up to Sadyojāta. ॥2॥
7.2.30.3: There too one should worship, in sequence, the six limbs — the heart and the rest — of Śiva and of Śivā, beginning from the quarter of Agni. ॥3॥
7.2.30.4: There, afterwards, one may or may not worship the eight Rudras, Vāma and the rest, with the Śaktis Vāmā and the rest, all around in order beginning from the east. ॥4॥
7.2.30.5: I have told you the first enclosure, O delight of the Yadus; the second enclosure is now told out of affection — listen with faith. ॥5॥
7.2.30.6: One should worship Ananta on the eastern petal, with his Śakti to his left, and Sūkṣma on the southern petal together with his Śakti. ॥6॥
7.2.30.7: Then, on the western petal, one should worship Śivottama together with his Śakti; likewise, on the northern petal, one should worship Ekanetra. ॥7॥
7.2.30.8: Next one should worship Ekarudra and his Śakti on the north-eastern petal, and should worship Trimūrti and his Śakti on the petal of Agni's (south-east) quarter. ॥8॥
7.2.30.9: One should worship Śrīkaṇṭha on the south-western petal with his Śakti to his left; likewise one should worship Śikhaṇḍīśa on the north-western petal of the Wind. ॥9॥
7.2.30.10: In the second enclosure the sovereigns (cakravartins) are to be worshipped all around; in the third enclosure the eight Forms (aṣṭamūrtis) are to be worshipped along with their Śaktis. ॥10॥
7.2.30.11: In the eight directions in turn, all around in order beginning from the east: Bhava, Śarva, likewise Īśāna, Rudra, then Paśupati, ॥11॥
7.2.30.12: Ugra, Bhīma and Mahādeva — these are the eight Forms in order. Immediately after that, there the eleven Forms beginning with Mahādeva are to be worshipped in order together with their Śaktis. ॥12॥
7.2.30.13: Mahādeva, Śiva, Rudra, Śaṅkara, Nīlalohita, Īśāna, Vijaya, Bhīma, Devadeva, Bhavodbhava, ॥13॥
7.2.30.14: and Kapardīśa — these are named the eleven, and likewise the eleven Śaktis. Of them, eight are to be worshipped first, in due order beginning from Agni's quarter. ॥14॥
7.2.30.15: Devadeva on the eastern petal and Īśāna in Agni's region; Bhavodbhava between the two, and Kapālīśa beyond that. ॥15॥
7.2.30.16: In that enclosure, further, one should worship the lord of bulls in front, Nandin to his right, and likewise Mahākāla to his left (north). ॥16॥
7.2.30.17: Śāstṛ on the petal of Agni's quarter, the Mothers on the southern petal, the elephant-faced one on the south-western petal, and Ṣaṇmukha again on the western petal of Varuṇa; ॥17॥
7.2.30.18: Jyeṣṭhā on the Wind's petal, Gaurī in the north, Caṇḍa in the north-east of the Lord; between Śāstṛ and Nandīśa one should worship the chief of sages, Vṛṣabha. ॥18॥
7.2.30.19: To the north of Mahākāla one should worship Piṅgala; then, between Śāstṛ and the group of Mothers, Bhṛṅgīśvara. ॥19॥
7.2.30.20: Between the Mothers and Vighneśa one should worship Vīrabhadra; between Skanda and Vighneśa one should worship the goddess Sarasvatī. ॥20॥
7.2.30.21: Between Jyeṣṭhā and Kumāra, Śrī who worships Śiva's feet; between Jyeṣṭhā and Gaṇāmbā one should worship Mahāmoṭī. ॥21॥
7.2.30.22: Between Gaṇāmbā and Caṇḍa one should worship the goddess Durgā. In this same enclosure, further, the host of Śiva's attendants — ॥22॥
7.2.30.23: manifold, called Rudras, Pramathas and Bhūtas, together with their Śaktis — and the band of Śivā's female companions, one should worship with a composed mind, having meditated on them. ॥23॥
7.2.30.24: When the extensive third enclosure has thus been worshipped, one should meditate on the fourth enclosure outside it and worship it. ॥24॥
7.2.30.25: The Sun is to be worshipped on the eastern petal, the four-faced Brahmā in the south, Rudra on the petal of Varuṇa's quarter, and Viṣṇu on the petal of the northern quarter. ॥25॥
7.2.30.26: Now, each of these four gods has separate enclosures. For him the Sun, first come his six limbs alone, along with the Śaktis Dīptā and the rest: ॥26॥
7.2.30.27: Dīptā, Sūkṣmā, Jayā, Bhadrā, Vibhūti, Vimalā, Amoghā and Vidyutā, in order, stationed all around beginning from the east. ॥27॥
7.2.30.28: In the second enclosure the four Forms are to be worshipped in order, from the east up to the north, and after them the Śaktis. ॥28॥
7.2.30.29: Āditya, Bhāskara, Bhānu and Ravi, in sequence; or Arka, Brahmā, Rudra and Viṣṇu — these are the forms of Vivasvat. ॥29॥
7.2.30.30: Vistārā is in the eastern part, Sutārā stationed in the south, Bodhanī in the western part, and Āpyāyinī in the north. ॥30॥
7.2.30.31: Then, placing Uṣā, Prabhā, likewise Prājñā and also Sandhyā in the north-east and the other intermediate quarters, one should worship them in the second enclosure. ॥31॥
7.2.30.32: Soma, Aṅgāraka, Budha the best of the wise, Bṛhaspati of vast intellect, Bhārgava the treasure of splendour, ॥32॥
7.2.30.33: Śanaiścara, likewise Rāhu, and Ketu, smoky and fearsome — these one should worship all around in the third enclosure, in order. ॥33॥
7.2.30.34: Alternatively, one should worship the twelve Ādityas in the second enclosure, and in the third enclosure worship the twelve zodiac signs. ॥34॥
7.2.30.35: And outside that, all around, the seven groups of seven: sages, gods, Gandharvas, serpents, hosts of Apsarases, ॥35॥
7.2.30.36: Grāmaṇīs, likewise Yakṣas, Yātudhānas, and the horses made of the seven metres, and the Vālakhilyas — one should worship these. ॥36॥
7.2.30.37: Having thus worshipped the Sun in the third enclosure, one should next worship Brahmā together with three enclosures. ॥37॥
7.2.30.38: One should worship Hiraṇyagarbha in the east, then Virāj in the south, Kāla in the western part, and Puruṣa in the north. ॥38॥
7.2.30.39: Hiraṇyagarbha, the first Brahmā, resembles a lotus; Kāla looks like pure collyrium; Puruṣa is like crystal. ॥39॥
7.2.30.40: Triguṇa, Rājasa, Tāmasa and likewise Sāttvika — these four, in order, are stationed in the first enclosure. ॥40॥
7.2.30.41: In the second enclosure, Sanatkumāra, Sanaka, Sanandana and Sanātana are to be worshipped in order, all around, beginning from the east. ॥41॥
7.2.30.42: Then in the third enclosure one should worship the Prajāpatis: eight first, in the east and the other directions, and three in the east and west, in due sequence. ॥42॥
7.2.30.43: Dakṣa, Ruci, Bhṛgu, Marīci and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Atri and Kaśyapa, ॥43॥
7.2.30.44: and Vasiṣṭha — these are renowned as the lords of creatures. Their wives too are to be worshipped together with them, in due order: ॥44॥
7.2.30.45: Prasūti and Ākūti, Khyāti and Sambhūti, Dhṛti, Smṛti, Kṣamā, Sannati and Anasūyā, ॥45॥
7.2.30.46: the Mother of the gods Aditi and Arundhatī — all of them devoted wives, ever intent on the worship of Śiva, splendid and lovely to behold. ॥46॥
7.2.30.47: Or else, in the first enclosure one should worship the four Vedas, and in the second enclosure, in turn, the Itihāsas and Purāṇas. ॥47॥
7.2.30.48: Then in the third enclosure all the Vedic branches of knowledge, headed by the Dharmaśāstras, are to be worshipped all around. ॥48॥
7.2.30.49: The Vedas are placed in front, beginning from the east, and the others as one likes, performing the worship all around in eight or in four divisions. ॥49॥
7.2.30.50: Having thus worshipped Brahmā, together with his three enclosures, in the south, one should then worship Rudra with his enclosures in the west. ॥50॥
7.2.30.51: His first enclosure is declared to be the six limbs of Brahman, and the second enclosure likewise consists of the Vidyeśvaras. ॥51॥
7.2.30.52: In the third enclosure there is a difference; that is now told. His four forms are to be worshipped in order, beginning from the east. ॥52॥
7.2.30.53: In front, in the east, is the god in the Sakala form, possessed of the three guṇas, called Śiva; in the south is worshipped the rājasic Brahmā, the creator, as Bhava. ॥53॥
7.2.30.54: In the west is to be worshipped the tāmasic Agni, Hara the destroyer; in the north the sāttvic Viṣṇu, bestower of happiness, lord of the universe, Mṛḍa. ॥54॥
7.2.30.55: Having thus worshipped in the western quarter Śiva, the twenty-sixth principle of Śambhu, one should then worship Vaikuṇṭha on the northern side. ॥55॥
7.2.30.56: Placing Vāsudeva in front, one should worship in the first enclosure; Aniruddha on the south, then Pradyumna in the west, ॥56॥
7.2.30.57: and afterwards Saṅkarṣaṇa in the north; or one may worship these two interchanged. The first enclosure has been told; now the auspicious second enclosure: ॥57॥
7.2.30.58: Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, Narasiṃha, then Vāmana, Rāma and another Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and also the venerable horse-faced one. ॥58॥
7.2.30.59: In the third enclosure one should worship the discus in the eastern part; in the south one should worship the missile named Nārāyaṇa, called in some places the Unobstructed. ॥59॥
7.2.30.60: In the west the Pāñcajanya conch, and then in the north the Śārṅga bow. Thus, with three enclosures, Hari himself, the supreme, called Viśva, ॥60॥
7.2.30.61: Mahāviṣṇu, Sadāviṣṇu, one should worship, having given him embodied form. Having thus worshipped the four forms of Viṣṇu in the order of the four vyūhas, one should worship their four Śaktis in order: ॥61॥
7.2.30.62: One should worship Prabhā in the south-eastern quarter, Sarasvatī in the south-west, Gaṇāmbikā in the north-west, and Lakṣmī in the north-east. ॥62॥
7.2.30.63: Thus, having performed the worship of the forms beginning with the Sun and, after that, of their Śaktis, one should worship the guardians of the worlds in that same enclosure: ॥63॥
7.2.30.64: Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti and Varuṇa, Vāyu, Soma and Kubera, and then one should worship Īśāna. ॥64॥
7.2.30.65: Having thus worshipped the fourth enclosure according to rule, one should then worship the weapons of Maheśa in the outer enclosure: ॥65॥
7.2.30.66: The glorious trident in the north-east, the thunderbolt in Mahendra's quarter east, the axe in the quarter of Fire south-east; in the south one should worship the arrow. ॥66॥
7.2.30.67: In the south-west one should worship the sword, the noose in Varuṇa's region west, the goad in the Wind's quarter north-west, and the Pināka bow in the north. ॥67॥
7.2.30.68: One should worship Rudra's Kṣetrapāla facing west. Having worshipped the fifth enclosure, thereafter, outside — ॥68॥
7.2.30.69: outside the enclosures of all the enclosure-deities, or else in the fifth: in the fifth, together with the Mothers, one should worship the great Bull in front. ॥69॥
7.2.30.70: Then all the semi-divine beings are to be worshipped all around: sky-goers, sages, Siddhas, Daityas, Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, ॥70॥
7.2.30.71: the serpent-lords beginning with Ananta, together with the Nāgas born of their respective clans, the Ḍākinīs, and the chiefs of Bhūtas, Vetālas, Pretas and Bhairavas, ॥71॥
7.2.30.72: and others dwelling in the netherworld, born of various species; rivers, oceans, mountains, forests and lakes, ॥72॥
7.2.30.73: domestic animals, birds, trees, insects and other lowly creatures, humans of various forms, and wild beasts of lowly birth, ॥73॥
7.2.30.74: the worlds within the cosmic egg, then the millions of cosmic eggs, and the countless worlds outside the egg together with their rulers, ॥74॥
7.2.30.75: the Rudras who uphold the cosmic eggs, stationed in the ten directions; whatever belongs to the guṇas, whatever pertains to Māyā, or whatever is of Śakti, and what lies beyond that — ॥75॥
7.2.30.76: whatever exists that can be denoted by a word, whether sentient or insentient — understanding all that to be at the side of Śiva and Śivā, one should worship it collectively. ॥76॥
7.2.30.77: all of them with joined palms, inconceivable, with smiling faces, and ever gazing lovingly at the god and the goddess. ॥77॥
7.2.30.78: Having thus performed the worship of the enclosures, for the pacification of distraction one should again worship the lord of the gods and utter the five-syllable mantra. ॥78॥
7.2.30.79: Then, after that, one should offer to Śiva and Śivā a great caru, like nectar, accompanied by fine side dishes, pure and lovely. ॥79॥
7.2.30.80: The best is of thirty-two āḍhakas, and the lowest at least one āḍhaka; having prepared it according to one's means, one should offer it with faith. ॥80॥
7.2.30.81: Then, having offered drinking water and betel together with relishes, and having performed the waving of lamps (nīrājana) and the like, he should complete the rest of the worship. ॥81॥
7.2.30.82: He should procure only excellent articles suitable for the deity's enjoyment; a devotee should not be stingy with wealth when he has the means. ॥82॥
7.2.30.83: For one who is deceitful, or negligent, or who performs the rite defectively, desire-motivated rites do not bear fruit at all — such is the saying of the virtuous. ॥83॥
7.2.30.84: Therefore, completely abandoning negligence, he should perform desire-motivated rites with all their components, if he wishes for the attainment of the fruit. ॥84॥
7.2.30.85: Having thus completed the worship, and then having bowed to the God and the Goddess, and having concentrated the mind with devotion, he should afterwards recite the hymn. ॥85॥
7.2.30.86: Then, having worshipped with the hymn, at the end he should eagerly repeat the five-syllabled vidyā, at least one hundred and eight times, or over a thousand times. ॥86॥
7.2.30.87: Having performed worship of the vidyā and worship of the guru, afterwards, in due order, he should honour the members of the assembly too, according to his prosperity and his faith. ॥87॥
7.2.30.88: Then, having ritually dismissed the Lord of the gods together with all the enclosure deities, he should give the maṇḍala to the guru along with the implements of the sacrifice. ॥88॥
7.2.30.89: Or he should give everything, in due order, to those who have taken refuge in Śiva; or else he should offer it to Śiva alone in a shrine of Śiva. ॥89॥
7.2.30.90: Or he may worship the God in the Śiva-fire with the seven oblation substances, having duly worshipped all the deities of the enclosures. ॥90॥
7.2.30.91: This rite, named Yogeśvara, is renowned in the three worlds; there is no sacrifice anywhere in the world superior to it. ॥91॥
7.2.30.92: There is nothing in this world that cannot be accomplished by this, whether some fruit of this life or a fruit of the next world. ॥92॥
7.2.30.93: No restriction is laid down such as: this is its fruit, this is not; it is the supreme means to all that has the nature of the good. ॥93॥
7.2.30.94: It cannot be specified: whatever a person worships for, that fruit is obtained by him from this rite, as from the wish-fulfilling gem. ॥94॥
7.2.30.95: Even so, one should not employ this for the sake of a trivial fruit, because one who seeks a small thing from the Great becomes himself smaller. ॥95॥
7.2.30.96: Whether the fruit be great or small, a rite succeeds if it is done; so let the rite be performed directed toward Mahādeva. ॥96॥
7.2.30.97: Therefore the discerning one should perform this for fruits, visible and invisible, not obtainable by other means, such as victory over enemies and over death. ॥97॥
7.2.30.98: And in the case of great sins, fears of grave diseases and the like, famines and the like, one should perform the pacificatory rite by means of this, for the sake of appeasement. ॥98॥
7.2.30.99: What is the use of much talk? Maheśvara has declared this to be the Śaivas' own weapon, the averter of great calamities. ॥99॥
7.2.30.100: Therefore there is no greater protection for oneself here than this; thinking thus, one who employs this rite attains what is auspicious. ॥100॥
7.2.30.101: He who, having become pure and well-composed, recites merely the hymn, he too obtains one-eighth of the fruit of his most desired object. ॥101॥
7.2.30.102: One who, contemplating its meaning, recites it while fasting on a parvan day, or on the eighth or fourteenth lunar day, would obtain half the fruit. ॥102॥
7.2.30.103: But he who, contemplating the meaning and likewise observing a vow on parvan days and the like, recites the hymn for one month, obtains the complete fruit. ॥103॥
7.2.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The Śaivas' rites for desired ends, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥30॥
7.2.31.1: Upamanyu said: I shall tell you, O Kṛṣṇa, a hymn that follows the order of the five enclosures (pañcāvaraṇa). It is this holy hymn called Yogeśvara, by which the rite is brought to completion. ॥1॥
7.2.31.2: Victory, victory to you, O Śambhu, sole lord of the world, charming by nature, whose very nature is eternal consciousness, whose reality lies beyond the reach of speech and mind, even of those that have left behind the impure expanse of the world! ॥2॥
7.2.31.3: Victory to you, whose expanse is pure by nature, whose actions are beautiful! Victory to you, whose great power is equal to your own self, O ocean of pure qualities! ॥3॥
7.2.31.4: Victory to you, endowed with infinite radiance, whose form has no equal! Victory to you, support of an inconceivable greatness, whose auspiciousness is undisturbed! ॥4॥
7.2.31.5: O stainless one, O one without support, victory to you whose arising has no cause! O one of unbroken supreme bliss, victory to you, cause of liberation! ॥5॥
7.2.31.6: Victory to you of utterly supreme sovereignty! Victory to you, abode of boundless compassion! Victory to you, whose all is self-dependent! Victory to you of matchless glory! ॥6॥
7.2.31.7: Victory to you who envelop the great universe! Victory to you who are enveloped by nothing! Victory to you, higher than all! Victory to you, beyond whom there is absolutely nothing higher! ॥7॥
7.2.31.8: Victory, O wondrous one! Victory, O one not petty! Victory, O unimpaired one! Victory, O imperishable one! Victory, O immeasurable one! Victory, O one free of illusion! Victory, O one beyond mere being! Victory, O spotless one! ॥8॥
7.2.31.9: O mighty-armed one, O one of great essence, O one of great qualities, O one of great renown, O one of great strength, O great wielder of māyā, O one of great delight, O great warrior. ॥9॥
7.2.31.10: Salutation to the supreme god, salutation to the supreme cause. Salutation to Śiva, the tranquil one; salutation to you, the most auspicious. ॥10॥
7.2.31.11: For this entire world, together with gods and asuras, is dependent on you. ॥11॥
7.2.31.12: Therefore, who is able to transgress the command laid down by you? ॥12॥
7.2.31.13: Moreover, this person has you always as his sole refuge; therefore, having shown him grace, may you grant him what he prays for. ॥13॥
7.2.31.14: Victory to you, O Ambikā, O mother of the world! Victory to you who consist of all the worlds! Victory to you of limitless sovereignty! Victory to you of incomparable form! ॥14॥
7.2.31.15: Victory to you who are beyond speech and mind! Victory to you, destroyer of the darkness of unconsciousness! Victory to you, free from birth and old age! Victory to you, higher even than what is beyond time! ॥15॥
7.2.31.16: Victory to you who abide in manifold forms! Victory to you, beloved of the lord of the universe! Victory to you, to be worshipped by all the gods! Victory to you who unfold as the universe! ॥16॥
7.2.31.17: Victory to you of auspicious, divine limbs! Victory to you, lamp of auspiciousness! Victory to you of auspicious conduct! Victory to you, giver of auspiciousness! ॥17॥
7.2.31.18: Salutation to you, whose form is an assemblage of supremely auspicious qualities. From you indeed the world has arisen, and into you alone it dissolves. ॥18॥
7.2.31.19: Therefore, without you, even the Lord could not bestow the fruit. From birth onwards, O queen of the gods, this person has taken refuge in you. ॥19॥
7.2.31.20: Therefore fulfil the desire of this devotee of yours. Five-faced, ten-armed, resembling pure crystal— ॥20॥
7.2.31.21: the god whose body is made of the letters, the Brahma-mantras and the kalās, both with parts and without parts, mounted on the Śiva-form, transcending the Śānti kalā—may that Sadāśiva, worshipped by me with devotion, grant me the welfare I pray for. ॥21॥
7.2.31.22: May Śakti, the power of Will, called Śivā, seated on the lap of Sadāśiva, mother of all the worlds, grant my desire. ॥22॥
7.2.31.23: The two beloved sons of Śiva and Śivā, the gods Heramba and Ṣaṇmukha, possessed of Śiva's majesty, omniscient, feeding on the nectar of Śiva-knowledge, ॥23॥
7.2.31.24: contented, affectionate toward each other, ever honoured by Śiva and Śivā, and ever honoured too by the gods headed by Brahmā, ॥24॥
7.2.31.25: ever arisen to bring about the protection of all the worlds, taking incarnations at will in many ways through divisions of their own portions— ॥25॥
7.2.31.26: these two, thus worshipped by me constantly beside Śiva and Śivā—placing their parents' command foremost, may they grant me what I pray for. ॥26॥
7.2.31.27: He who is like pure crystal, named Īśāna, Sadāśiva, the form identified with the head of Śiva the supreme Self, ॥27॥
7.2.31.28: devoted to the worship of Śiva, tranquil, transcending Śānti, abiding in ether, the last seed-syllable of the five-syllable mantra, endowed with five kalās, ॥28॥
7.2.31.29: worshipped first in the first enclosure together with its Śakti—may that pure, supreme Brahman grant me what I pray for. ॥29॥
7.2.31.30: He who is like the rising sun, named Puruṣa, the ancient one, identified with the eastern face of Śiva the supreme, ॥30॥
7.2.31.31: of the nature of Śānti, abiding in wind, devoted to worship of Śambhu's feet, the first among Śiva's seed-syllables, and having four kalās among the kalās, ॥31॥
7.2.31.32: worshipped by me with devotion in the eastern part together with its Śakti—may that pure, supreme Brahman grant me what I pray for. ॥32॥
7.2.31.33: He who is like collyrium-mountain and the like, Aghora of fearsome form, the southern face of the god, worshipper of the feet of the god of gods, ॥33॥
7.2.31.34: mounted on the Vidyā level, situated in the middle of the fire-circle, the second among Śiva's seed-syllables, endowed with eight kalās among the kalās, ॥34॥
7.2.31.35: worshipped together with its Śakti in the southern region of Śambhu—may that pure, supreme Brahman grant me what I pray for. ॥35॥
7.2.31.36: He who is like saffron powder, named Vāma, wearing excellent attire, the northern face of the Lord, established in the Pratiṣṭhā level, ॥36॥
7.2.31.37: situated in the middle of the water-circle, devoted to the worship of Mahādeva, the fourth among Śiva's seed-syllables, endowed with thirteen kalās, ॥37॥
7.2.31.38: worshipped together with its Śakti in the northern region of the god—may that pure, supreme Brahman grant me what I pray for. ॥38॥
7.2.31.39: He who is white as conch, kunda-jasmine and the moon, named Sadya, of gentle features, the western face of Śiva, devoted to the worship of Śiva's feet, ॥39॥
7.2.31.40: established in the Nivṛtti level and situated in earth, the third among Śiva's seed-syllables, and endowed with eight kalās, ॥40॥
7.2.31.41: May the purifying supreme Brahman, worshipped together with Śakti on the western side of the deity, grant me what I pray for. ॥41॥
7.2.31.42: The two heart-forms of Śiva and of Śivā, filled with Śiva — placing the command of those two foremost, may they both grant me my desire. ॥42॥
7.2.31.43: The two auspicious forms of Śiva and of Śivā, resting in Śiva — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they both grant me my desire. ॥43॥
7.2.31.44: The two armours of Śiva and of Śivā, filled with Śiva — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they both grant me my desire. ॥44॥
7.2.31.45: The two eye-forms of Śiva and of Śivā, resting in Śiva — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they both grant me my desire. ॥45॥
7.2.31.46: And the two weapon-forms of the divine pair, ever intent on worship — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they both grant me my desire. ॥46॥
7.2.31.47: Vāma, Jyeṣṭha, and Rudra, Kāla and Vikaraṇa, Balavikaraṇa, and next Balapramathana, ॥47॥
7.2.31.48: and Sarvabhūtadamana, together with their eight Śaktis of like nature — may they grant me what I pray for, solely by the command of the divine pair. ॥48॥
7.2.31.49: Then Ananta and Sūkṣma, Śiva and also Ekanetra, Ekarudra and Trimūrti, Śrīkaṇṭha and Śikhaṇḍin, ॥49॥
7.2.31.50: and likewise their eight Śaktis, worshipped in the second enclosure — may they grant me my desire, solely by the command of the divine pair. ॥50॥
7.2.31.51: The eight forms beginning with Bhava and their Śaktis too, and likewise the other eleven forms beginning with Mahādeva — ॥51॥
7.2.31.52: all of them, together with their Śaktis, stationed in the third enclosure — honouring the command of the divine pair, may they bestow the desired fruit. ॥52॥
7.2.31.53: The king of bulls, of great splendour, with a voice like a great cloud, resembling the peaks of Meru, Mandara, Kailāsa and the Himālaya, ॥53॥
7.2.31.54: shaped like the crest of a white cloud, adorned with a hump, and resplendent with a tail resembling a great serpent-king, ॥54॥
7.2.31.55: with red mouth, horns and hooves, eyes mostly red, all limbs stout and tall, radiant with a most graceful gait, ॥55॥
7.2.31.56: bearing auspicious marks, glorious, with blazing jewelled ornaments, dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, the banner and the mount of the divine pair, ॥56॥
7.2.31.57: and whose other body is purified by the placing of their feet — the personified form of the king of bulls, glorious, bearing the splendid excellent trident as weapon — placing their command foremost, may he grant me my desire. ॥57॥
7.2.31.58: Nandīśvara, of great splendour, son of the daughter of the mountain-king, ever worshipped and saluted by the gods together with Nārāyaṇa, ॥58॥
7.2.31.59: stationed with his attendants at the door of Śarva's inner palace, equal in renown to the Lord of all, crusher of all asuras, ॥59॥
7.2.31.60: consecrated as overseer of all the Śiva-dharmas, dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, bearing the splendid excellent trident as weapon, ॥60॥
7.2.31.61: attached to those who take refuge in Śiva and loved by them in turn — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he grant me my desire. ॥61॥
7.2.31.62: Mahākāla, the mighty-armed, like a second Mahādeva — may he ever protect those who rely on Mahādeva. ॥62॥
7.2.31.63: Dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, ever the worshipper of the divine pair — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he bestow on me what I long for. ॥63॥
7.2.31.64: Śāstā, knower of the true meaning of all scriptures, the supreme body of Viṣṇu, son of Viṣṇu in the form of Mahāmoha, fond of honey, meat and liquor — placing their command foremost, may he grant me my desire. ॥64॥
7.2.31.65: Brahmāṇī and Māheśī, Kaumārī and Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī and Māhendrī, and Cāmuṇḍā of fierce valour — ॥65॥
7.2.31.66: these are the seven Mothers, mothers of the whole world; may they grant me what I pray for, by the command of the Supreme Lord. ॥66॥
7.2.31.67: He whose face is that of a rutting elephant, son of Gaṅgā, Umā and Śaṅkara, whose body is the sky, whose arms are the directions, whose eyes are the moon, sun and fire, ॥67॥
7.2.31.68: ever worshipped by the divine elephants of the quarters, Airāvata and the rest, bursting with the rut of Śiva-knowledge, the remover of obstacles for the gods, ॥68॥
7.2.31.69: and the creator of obstacles for the asuras and others — Vighneśa, devoted to Śiva — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he bestow on me what I long for. ॥69॥
7.2.31.70: The six-faced one, born of Śiva, the lord bearing the spear and the thunderbolt, the god who is son of Agni and again son of Aparṇā, ॥70॥
7.2.31.71: and son of Gaṅgā, of Gaṇāmbā, and likewise of the Kṛttikās, surrounded by Viśākha, Śākha and Naigameya, ॥71॥
7.2.31.72: conqueror of Indra, the moon-like commander, and likewise conqueror of the asura Tāraka, piercer by his own might of the mountains headed by Meru, ॥72॥
7.2.31.73: shining like molten gold, with eyes like lotus petals, Kumāra, the great model of beauty among the delicate, ॥73॥
7.2.31.74: dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, ever worshipping Śiva's feet — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he bestow on me what I long for. ॥74॥
7.2.31.75: Jyeṣṭhā, most excellent, the giver of boons, delighting in the worship of the divine pair — placing their command foremost, may she bestow on me what I long for. ॥75॥
7.2.31.76: Gaṇāmbikā, revered by the three worlds, manifest in the shape of a meteor, requested from Śiva by Brahmā for the creation and growth of the world, ॥76॥
7.2.31.77: the forms that issued from between the brows of Śivā when she divided herself: Dākṣāyaṇī Satī, Menā, and likewise Haimavatī Umā, ॥77॥
7.2.31.78: the mother of Kauśikī and likewise of Bhadrakālī, the mother of Aparṇā and likewise of Pāṭalā, ॥78॥
7.2.31.79: ever devoted to the worship of Śiva, Rudrāṇī, beloved of Rudra — honouring the command of the divine pair, may she bestow on me what I long for. ॥79॥
7.2.31.80: Caṇḍa, lord of all the Gaṇas, born from the mouth of Śambhu — honouring the command of the divine pair, may he bestow on me what I long for. ॥80॥
7.2.31.81: May Piṅgala, the glorious leader of the gaṇas, devoted to Śiva and dear to Śiva, grant me my desire, by the command of Śiva and Śivā alone. ॥81॥
7.2.31.82: May the leader of the gaṇas named Bhṛṅgīśa, intent on the worship of Śiva, grant me my desire, with the Lord's command going before. ॥82॥
7.2.31.83: Vīrabhadra, of great splendour, resembling snow, jasmine and the moon, ever dear to Bhadrakālī and protector of the Mothers, ॥83॥
7.2.31.84: remover of the head of the sacrifice and of the evil-minded Dakṣa, the hewer of the limbs of the gods beginning with Upendra, Indra and Yama, ॥84॥
7.2.31.85: the glorious attendant of Śiva, guardian of Śiva's command — may he bestow on me what I long for, by the command of Śiva and Śivā alone. ॥85॥
7.2.31.86: Sarasvatī, born from the lotus of Maheśa's speech, devoted to the worship of Śiva and Śivā — may she bestow on me what I long for. ॥86॥
7.2.31.87: Lakṣmī, abiding on Viṣṇu's chest, delighting in the worship of Śiva and Śivā — may she bestow on me what I long for, by the command of Śiva and Śivā alone. ॥87॥
7.2.31.88: Mahāmoṭī, wholly devoted to the worship of the Great Goddess's feet — may she, by that Goddess's own direction, bestow on me what I long for. ॥88॥
7.2.31.89: Kauśikī, mounted on a lion, the supreme daughter of Pārvatī, the sleep of Viṣṇu, the Great Illusion, slayer of the great buffalo demon, ॥89॥
7.2.31.90: destroyer of Niśumbha and Śumbha, fond of wine, meat and liquor — honouring her mother's command, may she bestow on me what I long for. ॥90॥
7.2.31.91: The Rudras, equal in renown to Rudra, the Pramathas of celebrated might, and those called Bhūtas, of great valour, equal in radiance to Mahādeva, ॥91॥
7.2.31.92: eternally liberated, incomparable, free from the pairs of opposites, free from calamity, accompanied by their Śaktis and attendants, saluted by all the worlds, ॥92॥
7.2.31.93: capable of creating and destroying all the worlds, devoted to one another and loyal to one another, ॥93॥
7.2.31.94: exceedingly affectionate toward one another, bowing to one another, ever most dear to Śiva, marked with the marks of Śiva, ॥94॥
7.2.31.95: gentle, terrible, and likewise mixed, having natures of the two intermediate kinds; ill-formed and well-formed, and bearing various forms likewise — ॥95॥
7.2.31.96: honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they indeed grant me my desire. The group of the Goddess's dear companions, marked with the marks of the Goddess, ॥96॥
7.2.31.97: together with the daughters of Rudra and with Śaktis in many ways, ever worshipped with devotion in the third enclosure of Śambhu — ॥97॥
7.2.31.98: honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may it bestow auspiciousness on me. Divākara, the Sun, a form of Maheśa, with a beautiful orb of radiance, ॥98॥
7.2.31.99: without qualities, mixed with qualities, and likewise pure quality alone; of changeless nature, primal, one, with common modifications, ॥99॥
7.2.31.100: and of uncommon actions in the sequence of creation, maintenance and dissolution; thus divided threefold, fourfold and again fivefold, ॥100॥
7.2.31.101: worshipped together with his followers in the fourth enclosure of Śambhu, dear to Śiva, attached to Śiva, delighting in the worship of Śiva's feet — ॥101॥
7.2.31.102: honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may he bestow auspiciousness on me. The six limbs of Divākara, and the eight Śaktis beginning with Dīptā, ॥102॥
7.2.31.103: Āditya, Bhāskara, Bhānu and Ravi in order, Arka, Brahmā, likewise Rudra and Viṣṇu — these are the forms of Āditya; ॥103॥
7.2.31.104: Vistarā, Sutarā, Bodhinī, Āpyāyinī, and further the others — Uṣā, Prabhā, likewise Prājñā and Sandhyā — these too are the Śaktis; ॥104॥
7.2.31.105: and the planets from Soma to Ketu, imbued with Śiva, impelled by the command of Śiva and Śivā — may they bestow auspiciousness on me. ॥105॥
7.2.31.106: Or else the twelve Ādityas and likewise the twelve Śaktis, the sages, the divine Gandharvas, the hosts of serpents and Apsarases, ॥106॥
7.2.31.107: the Grāmaṇīs, likewise the Yakṣas, the Rākṣasas and the gods — these seven groups of seven — and the horses made of the seven metres, ॥107॥
7.2.31.108: and the Vālakhilyas and others — all worshippers of Śiva's feet — honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they bestow auspiciousness on me. ॥108॥
7.2.31.109: Next Brahmā, a form of the God of gods, lord of the earth-sphere, possessing lordship of sixty-four qualities, established in the principle of intellect (buddhi-tattva), ॥109॥
7.2.31.110: without qualities, mixed with qualities, and likewise pure quality alone; the god of changeless nature, thereafter, first, common in action, ॥110॥
7.2.31.111: and of uncommon actions in the sequence of creation, maintenance and dissolution; thus divided threefold, fourfold and again fivefold, ॥111॥
7.2.31.112: worshipped together with his followers in the fourth enclosure of Śambhu, dear to Śiva, attached to Śiva, delighting in the worship of Śiva's feet — ॥112॥
7.2.31.113: honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may he bestow auspiciousness on me. Hiraṇyagarbha, the lord of the world, Virāṭ, Kāla and Puruṣa, ॥113॥
7.2.31.114: Sanatkumāra, Sanaka, Sananda and Sanātana, and the lords of creatures, Dakṣa and the others, sons of Brahmā, ॥114॥
7.2.31.115: the eleven with their wives, and Dharma and Saṅkalpa too — these, delighting in Śiva's worship, wholly devoted to Śiva, ॥115॥
7.2.31.116: all subject to Śiva's command — may they bestow auspiciousness on me. Likewise the four Vedas together with the Itihāsas and Purāṇas, ॥116॥
7.2.31.117: the Dharmaśāstras, accompanied by the Vedic sciences, mutually non-contradictory in meaning, expounding the nature of Śiva — ॥117॥
7.2.31.118: honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they bestow auspiciousness on me. Next Rudra, Mahādeva, the weightier form of Śambhu, ॥118॥
7.2.31.119: lord of the sphere of fire, the master possessing the sovereignty of Puruṣa, endowed with the self-identity of Śiva, without qualities yet of the nature of the three qualities, ॥119॥
7.2.31.120: purely sāttvika, and also rājasa and tāmasa; at first delighting in changelessness, but thereafter of uniform modification, ॥120॥
7.2.31.121: He is of unique deeds, distinct from the others in carrying out creation and the rest; the one who cut off even Brahmā's head, who is both his father and his son. ॥121॥
7.2.31.122: Father and also son, controller even of Viṣṇu, the constant enlightener of both of them, the gracious Lord. ॥122॥
7.2.31.123: Rudra, who abides within and outside the cosmic egg, lord of both worlds, dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, delighting in the worship of Śiva's feet — ॥123॥
7.2.31.124: — placing Śiva's command foremost, may he grant me auspiciousness. His Brahman mantras and six limbs, and likewise the group of eight Vidyeśas, ॥124॥
7.2.31.125: and the four distinct forms headed by Śiva, worshippers of Śiva — Śiva, Bhava, Hara, and also Mṛḍa as the other — placing Śiva's command foremost, may they grant me auspiciousness. ॥125॥
7.2.31.126: Next, Viṣṇu, the supreme body of Maheśa Śiva himself, directly the lord of the water principle, established in the state of the Unmanifest, ॥126॥
7.2.31.127: beyond the guṇas, yet abounding in sattva, and likewise consisting of guṇa alone; identifying himself with the unchanging, whose transformation is shared by the three, ॥127॥
7.2.31.128: of unique deeds, distinct in carrying out creation and the rest, vying even with Svayambhū Brahmā born from Śiva's right side, ॥128॥
7.2.31.129: directly created by the primal Brahmā and yet also his creator; abiding within and outside the cosmic egg, Viṣṇu, lord of the two worlds, ॥129॥
7.2.31.130: slayer of the asuras, bearer of the discus, and likewise the younger brother of Śakra, who appeared here in ten forms on the pretext of Bhṛgu's curse, ॥130॥
7.2.31.131: who of his own will descended upon the earth to check the burden of the earth; of immeasurable strength, master of māyā, deluding the world by māyā, ॥131॥
7.2.31.132: taking the form of Mahāviṣṇu or else of Sadāviṣṇu, ever worshipped by the Vaiṣṇavas on a seat made of the three forms, ॥132॥
7.2.31.133: dear to Śiva, devoted to Śiva, delighting in the worship of Śiva's feet — placing Śiva's command foremost, may he grant me auspiciousness. ॥133॥
7.2.31.134: Vāsudeva, Aniruddha, Pradyumna, and after them Saṅkarṣaṇa are declared to be the four forms of Hari. ॥134॥
7.2.31.135: Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, Nārasiṃha, then Vāmana, the three Rāmas, likewise Kṛṣṇa, and Viṣṇu with the horse's face, ॥135॥
7.2.31.136: the discus, weapon of Nārāyaṇa, the conch Pāñcajanya and the bow Śārṅga — honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they grant me auspiciousness. ॥136॥
7.2.31.137: Prabhā, Sarasvatī, Gaurī and Lakṣmī, imbued with devotion to Śiva — at the bidding of Śiva and Śivā, may these grant me auspiciousness. ॥137॥
7.2.31.138: Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Soma, Kubera, and likewise Īśāna bearing the trident — ॥138॥
7.2.31.139: all devoted to Śiva's worship, imbued with true devotion to Śiva — honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they grant me auspiciousness. ॥139॥
7.2.31.140: The trident, the thunderbolt, likewise the axe and the arrow, the sword, noose and goad, and the Pināka, the best of weapons — ॥140॥
7.2.31.141: these divine weapons of the God and the Goddess — honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they always protect me. ॥141॥
7.2.31.142: The god bearing the form of a bull, son of Surabhi, of great might, rivalling the fire called Vaḍavā, surrounded by the five mother-cows, ॥142॥
7.2.31.143: who through austerity attained the status of vehicle of the two supreme lords — placing their command foremost, may he grant my desire. ॥143॥
7.2.31.144: Nandā, Sunandā, Surabhi, Suśīlā and Sumanā — these five mother-cows dwell in Śiva's world, ॥144॥
7.2.31.145: ever intent on devotion to Śiva, wholly given to Śiva's worship — by the command of Śiva and Śivā alone, may they grant what I desire. ॥145॥
7.2.31.146: The Kṣetrapāla, of great splendour, resembling a dark rain-cloud, his face fearsome with fangs, radiant with quivering red lips, ॥146॥
7.2.31.147: with red, upstanding hair, glorious, eyes crooked with frowning brows, three round red eyes, adorned with the moon and serpents, ॥147॥
7.2.31.148: naked, his hands raised holding trident, noose, sword and skull; Bhairava, surrounded by Bhairavas, Siddhas and Yoginīs, ॥148॥
7.2.31.149: who, seated in every sacred field, stands as protector of the good, supremely intent on bowing to Śiva, imbued with true devotion to Śiva, ॥149॥
7.2.31.150: especially protecting those who take refuge in Śiva like his own sons — honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may he grant me auspiciousness. ॥150॥
7.2.31.151: Tālajaṅgha and the others, the four worshipped in his first enclosure — honouring the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they protect me. ॥151॥
7.2.31.152: And Bhairava and the others who surround him on all sides — may they too favour me, out of reverence for Śiva's command. ॥152॥
7.2.31.153: The sages headed by Nārada, divine and worshipped even by the gods; the Sādhyas, the Nāgas, and the gods who dwell in Janaloka; ॥153॥
7.2.31.154: those whose offices have ceased, dwelling in Maharloka; the seven sages, and others too, together with the hosts of the celestial-car dwellers — ॥154॥
7.2.31.155: all devoted to Śiva's worship, obedient to Śiva's command — by the command of Śiva and Śivā, may they grant me what I long for. ॥155॥
7.2.31.156: The four classes of divine beings from the Gandharvas down to the Piśācas; the Siddhas, Vidyādharas and the others, and whatever other sky-rangers there are; ॥156॥
7.2.31.157: the Asuras and Rākṣasas dwelling in the nether regions, the serpent-lords headed by Ananta, the birds headed by Vainateya (Garuḍa); ॥157॥
7.2.31.158: the Kūṣmāṇḍas, Pretas and Vetālas, the Grahas and other hosts of Bhūtas, the Ḍākinīs, Yoginīs, and Śākinīs of like kind; ॥158॥
7.2.31.159: sacred fields, gardens, houses and the like, holy fords and shrines, islands, oceans, rivers, other great streams, and lakes; ॥159॥
7.2.31.160: the mountains headed by Sumeru, the forests all around, animals, birds, trees, worms, insects and the like, and wild beasts — ॥160॥
7.2.31.161: All the worlds as well, the lords of the worlds, the cosmic eggs together with their coverings, the quarters, and the ten elephants of the directions, ॥161॥
7.2.31.162: the letters, the words, the mantras, and the tattvas together with their presiding lords, the Rudras who uphold the cosmic egg, and the other Rudras along with their Śaktis, ॥162॥
7.2.31.163: and whatever in this world is seen, inferred or heard — may all of them grant my desire, by the command of Śiva and Śivā alone. ॥163॥
7.2.31.164: Then the supreme Śaiva knowledge, which releases the bound souls from their fetters, divine, called Pañcārtha, which lies beyond the knowledge of the bound, ॥164॥
7.2.31.165: and the scripture called Śivadharma, and its sequel called Śivadharmottara, the Purāṇa known as Śaiva and as Śivadharma, equal in authority to the Veda, ॥165॥
7.2.31.166: and the Śaiva Āgamas, and the others of four kinds beginning with the Kāmika — honoured and worshipped here without distinction from Śiva and Śivā, ॥166॥
7.2.31.167: commanded by those two alone for the fulfilment of my intended aim — may they approve this rite as fruitful and well performed. ॥167॥
7.2.31.168: The teachers from Śveta down to Nakulīśa together with their disciples, the gurus of their lineage, and especially my own gurus, ॥168॥
7.2.31.169: the Śaivas and the Māheśvaras devoted to knowledge and ritual action — may they approve this rite as fruitful and well performed. ॥169॥
7.2.31.170: All the worldly Brāhmaṇas, the Kṣatriyas and the Vaiśyas in due order, knowers of the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, experts in all the śāstras, ॥170॥
7.2.31.171: the Sāṅkhyas, the Vaiśeṣikas, the Yogins and the Naiyāyika men, the Sauras, the Brāhmas, the Raudras, the Vaiṣṇavas and other men, ॥171॥
7.2.31.172: all the cultured and the distinguished, restrained by Śiva's command — may they approve this rite which accomplishes my intended aim. ॥172॥
7.2.31.173: The Śaivas who stand on the Siddhānta path, the Śaiva Pāśupatas likewise, the Śaivas who bear the Great Vow, and other Śaivas, the Kāpālikas — ॥173॥
7.2.31.174: keepers of Śiva's command, worthy of worship even by me by Śiva's ordinance — may they all favour me and proclaim the rite fruitful. ॥174॥
7.2.31.175: Those established in the Dakṣiṇa knowledge and those who follow the Dakṣiṇa and Uttara paths — may they act without opposition to the mantra of me who seek the highest good. ॥175॥
7.2.31.176: Unbelievers, the deceitful, the ungrateful, the tāmasic, heretics and the exceedingly sinful — may they keep far away from me. ॥176॥
7.2.31.177: What need is there here of praising many? Whoever at all are believers — may they all favour me, and may the good proclaim auspiciousness. ॥177॥
7.2.31.178: Salutation to you, Śiva, together with Ambā and with your sons, the primal cause, enveloped by the manifest universe in the form of the five coverings. ॥178॥
7.2.31.179: Having said this and prostrated on the ground like a staff before Śiva and Śivā, one should recite the five-syllabled mantra no fewer than one hundred and eight times. ॥179॥
7.2.31.180: Likewise, having recited the Śakti mantra and made the offering of it, and having begged pardon of the Lord, one should complete the remainder of the worship. ॥180॥
7.2.31.181: This most meritorious hymn is dear to the hearts of Śiva and Śivā; it grants all desires and is directly the sole means to enjoyment and liberation. ॥181॥
7.2.31.182: Whoever recites this daily, or listens to it with a concentrated mind, quickly shakes off his sins and attains union with Śiva. ॥182॥
7.2.31.183: The slayer of a cow, the ungrateful, the killer of a hero or of an embryo, one who kills a refugee, one who betrays a friend's trust, ॥183॥
7.2.31.184: one of wicked and sinful conduct, the slayer of a mother or of a father — by reciting this hymn he is freed from each such sin. ॥184॥
7.2.31.185: In fears that portend great calamity, such as bad dreams, if one recites this, one will not suffer calamity from them. ॥185॥
7.2.31.186: Long life, health, prosperity and whatever else is desired — a man who persists in reciting this hymn obtains all that. ॥186॥
7.2.31.187: The fruit described is that of reciting the Śiva hymn without worship; the fruit of reciting it after worship cannot be told. ॥187॥
7.2.31.188: Let this gaining of fruits be set aside: when this is recited, the God together with Ambikā, merely on hearing it, stands present in the sky. ॥188॥
7.2.31.189: Therefore, having worshipped the God of gods together with Umā in the sky, one should stand with joined palms and recite this hymn. ॥189॥
7.2.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named The great hymn to Śiva, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥31॥
7.2.32.1: Upamanyu said: O Kṛṣṇa, I have told you this supreme rite, which grants success here and in the next world and consists of a combination of ritual action, austerity, japa and meditation. ॥1॥
7.2.32.2: Now I shall describe the great rite for Śaiva men which yields fruit in this very world, consisting of worship, fire-oblation, japa, meditation, austerity and gifts. ॥2॥
7.2.32.3: In this, the best knower of the meaning of mantras should first perfect the mantra, because a rite producing visible success does not otherwise yield fruit. ॥3॥
7.2.32.4: Even one who has perfected the mantra, if he is wise, should not rashly perform a rite whose fruit is obstructed by some powerful unseen force. ॥4॥
7.2.32.5: For that obstruction, however, an expiation can be made here. Having examined it through omens and the like, he should first perform the expiation. ॥5॥
7.2.32.6: The man who, out of delusion, performs a rite meant for worldly fruit in any other way will not obtain its fruit by it, and will become an object of ridicule. ॥6॥
7.2.32.7: One lacking confidence should never perform a rite of visible fruit; such a person is indeed without faith, and one without faith does not attain the fruit. ॥7॥
7.2.32.8: Even if the rite is fruitless, the fault is not the god's, since for men who act as prescribed the fruit is seen in this very world. ॥8॥
7.2.32.9: The practitioner who has perfected the mantra, removed the obstruction, and is confident and faithful obtains that fruit by performing the rite. ॥9॥
7.2.32.10: Moreover, to obtain that fruit he should be devoted to celibacy, and at night he should eat sacrificial food, or milk-rice, or fruits. ॥10॥
7.2.32.11: Whatever is forbidden, such as violence, he should not do even in thought. He should always be pure, his limbs smeared with ash and well attired. ॥11॥
7.2.32.12: Having thus become observant of conduct, on an auspicious day favourable to himself, in a place with the characteristics described earlier, adorned with garlands of flowers and the like, ॥12॥
7.2.32.13: having duly smeared the ground with cow-dung over an area of at least one hasta, he should draw an auspicious lotus, shining with its own radiance, ॥13॥
7.2.32.14: made of refined gold, eight-petalled, with filaments, furnished with a pericarp in the middle, adorned with all gems, ॥14॥
7.2.32.15: and furnished with a stalk matching its own form. On a bulb likewise made of gold, properly according to rule, ॥15॥
7.2.32.16: and there again conceiving mentally all the powers beginning with aṇimā, having installed according to rule a liṅga with a pedestal, bearing the proper marks, made of gems, or of gold, or of crystal, ॥16॥
7.2.32.17: having invoked the imperishable god there, together with Ambā and his attendants, he should worship him. There the Maheśvara form of the Lord who possesses form is to be visualised: ॥17॥
7.2.32.18: four-armed, four-faced, decorated with all ornaments, clothed in a tiger skin, with a slightly smiling face, ॥18॥
7.2.32.19: with hands showing the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, and likewise holding a deer and an axe. Or else it may be visualised as eight-armed, according to the meditator's preference. ॥19॥
7.2.32.20: Then it holds the trident, battle-axe, sword and thunderbolt on the right, and likewise on the left the noose and goad, a shield and a serpent. ॥20॥
7.2.32.21: Its radiance resembles the rising sun, and each face has three eyes. Its eastern face is gentle, with a lustre matching its own form; ॥21॥
7.2.32.22: the southern resembles a dark rain-cloud and is terrible to behold; the northern is coral-coloured, adorned with dark locks; ॥22॥
7.2.32.23: the western shines like the full moon, gentle, bearing the crescent of the moon. Seated on its lap is the supreme Śakti of Maheśvara, ॥23॥
7.2.32.24: known as Mahālakṣmī, dark-complexioned and enchanting to all. Having made the image of such a form and having duly performed the sakalīkaraṇa in order, ॥24॥
7.2.32.25: then, having invoked the embodied supreme Cause, he should worship him. For his bath he should prepare there the pañcagavya of a tawny cow, ॥25॥
7.2.32.26: the pañcāmṛta, and especially whole seeds. Having made a maṇḍala in front, adorned with gem-powders and the like, ॥26॥
7.2.32.27: he should place the Īśāna pot on the pericarp, and afterwards arrange the Sadya and other pots around it. ॥27॥
7.2.32.28: Then he should place the eight pots of the Vidyeśas in order, beginning from the east; having filled them with water from sacred fords and wound thread round them as before, ॥28॥
7.2.32.29: having put in sacred substances with mantras and according to procedure, and having covered them all around with fine silk or other cloth, ॥29॥
7.2.32.30: and having placed the mantra on each, preceded by the respective mantras — when the time of bathing has come, amid the sounds of all auspicious instruments, ॥30॥
7.2.32.31: he should bathe the Supreme Lord with the pañcagavya and the rest. Then the kuśa-water and the others, and also the gold- and gem-waters, ॥31॥
7.2.32.32: prepared with fragrances, flowers and the like and consecrated with mantras — taking them up one after another with the mantra, he should bathe Maheśvara with each of them in order, ॥32॥
7.2.32.33: and he should perform the worship with fragrances, flowers and so on, and lamps. The unguent should be at least one pala and at most eleven palas. ॥33॥
7.2.32.34: One should offer flowers of gold and gems, auspicious and fragrant ones, blue lotuses and other water-lilies, and bilva leaves in great number, ॥34॥
7.2.32.35: and red and white lotuses for Śambhu. The incense is made from black aloe-wood, with camphor, ghee and guggulu; ॥35॥
7.2.32.36: the lamps are prepared with ghee from a tawny cow, with wicks of camphor. The five Brahma-mantras, the six limbs, and the enclosure deities are to be worshipped. ॥36॥
7.2.32.37: The food-offering is a great caru cooked in milk, with jaggery and ghee; and the drinking water is scented with pāṭala flowers, water-lilies, lotuses and the like; ॥37॥
7.2.32.38: well-prepared betel with the five fragrant spices; and especially ornaments made of gold and gems, ॥38॥
7.2.32.39: and garments that are colourful, fine, new and beautiful to look at are to be offered, together with singing, instrumental music and the like. ॥39॥
7.2.32.40: The japa of the root mantra is one lakh as the highest count; and the worship here is at least once and at most three times, according to the fruit desired. ॥40॥
7.2.32.41: The oblation should number at least ten, and at most a hundred, for each substance. In rites of killing, driving away and the like, Śiva is to be meditated upon in his terrible form. ॥41॥
7.2.32.42: In a rite for pacification or for prosperity, Śambhu is to be meditated upon in a gentle form, in the Śiva-liṅga, in the Śiva-fire, and in other images as well. ॥42॥
7.2.32.43: In rites of killing and the like, the ladle and spoon should be made of iron; elsewhere, in all rites of pacification and the rest, they should be of gold. ॥43॥
7.2.32.44: With dūrvā grass mixed with ghee and cow's milk, likewise with honey, with caru together with ghee, or with milk alone — ॥44॥
7.2.32.45: — one should offer oblations for conquering death; with sesame for the alleviation of disease; and with ghee and milk, or with lotuses alone, ॥45॥
7.2.32.46: one desiring prosperity should offer oblations for the removal of great poverty. One seeking to bring others under control should offer jāti flowers together with ghee. ॥46॥
7.2.32.47: With ghee and karavīra flowers a twice-born should perform the rite of attraction; with oil one should perform driving away, and again with honey, immobilisation. ॥47॥
7.2.32.48: Immobilization is done also with mustard, but felling with garlic; striking is done with the blood of both the donkey and the camel. ॥48॥
7.2.32.49: For killing and driving away one should use rohi seeds mixed with sesame; and one should perform the rite of causing enmity with the oil of the lāṅgalaka plant. ॥49॥
7.2.32.50: Binding, and also immobilizing an army, is done with rohi seed, and with oblation-substances mixed throughout with red mustard. ॥50॥
7.2.32.51: In a hostile (ābhicārika) rite one should offer oils pressed by a hand-mill, together with kaṭukī husks and cotton seeds. ॥51॥
7.2.32.52: In a hostile rite one should offer mustard seeds mixed with oil. Milk grants relief from fever and likewise yields the fruit of good fortune. ॥52॥
7.2.32.53: An oblation with honey, ghee and curd combined brings every accomplishment; so too with milk and rice grains, or with caru alone. ॥53॥
7.2.32.54: Pacification or prosperity is achieved, and especially subjugation and attraction, through an oblation with the seven substances beginning with the fuel-sticks. ॥54॥
7.2.32.55: Oblation with bilva leaves especially brings subjugation, attraction and prosperity, and likewise grants victory over an enemy. ॥55॥
7.2.32.56: In pacification rites the fuel-sticks are of palāśa, khadira and the like; in cruel rites, those from karavīra and arka; and thorny ones in rites of conflict. ॥56॥
7.2.32.57: One who is tranquil should perform the pacification rite, and especially the prosperity rite; but one who is pitiless and angry in mind would perform the hostile rite. ॥57॥
7.2.32.58: In an extremely dire situation, if there is no other remedy, one may perform the hostile rite directed at an assailant (ātatāyin). ॥58॥
7.2.32.59: One should not perform a hostile rite directed at the ruler of one's own realm, nor at anyone who is a believer, highly righteous, or worthy of honour, ॥59॥
7.2.32.60: — one should not perform it directed at him even if he is an assailant; nor at anyone at all who has taken refuge in Śiva in mind, deed or speech. ॥60॥
7.2.32.61: Having performed a hostile rite directed at the ruler of one's own realm, or at one who has taken refuge in Śiva, a man falls to ruin at once. ॥61॥
7.2.32.62: Therefore, if one desires one's own happiness, one should not harm the protector of one's own realm, or any devotee of Śiva, by hostile rites and the like. ॥62॥
7.2.32.63: And having performed killing and the like directed at anyone else, one should, filled with remorse, perform expiation. ॥63॥
7.2.32.64: Poor or rich, one may perform this even on a Bāṇa-liṅga, or on a self-manifested liṅga, or on one established by sages, or a Vedic one. ॥64॥
7.2.32.65: In the absence of gold and gems, and when unable to acquire them, one should perform this mentally, or with substitute substances. ॥65॥
7.2.32.66: One who is capable in some part but incapable in another part — he too, if he performs according to his capacity, attains the fruit. ॥66॥
7.2.32.67: Where, even when this rite has been performed, the fruit is not seen, one should repeat it twice or thrice; then the fruit is certainly seen. ॥67॥
7.2.32.68: Whatever excellent material was used in the worship — gold, gems and the like — all of it one should give to the guru, and the fee (dakṣiṇā) separately from that. ॥68॥
7.2.32.69: If he does not want it, one should offer all of it to Śiva, or to Śiva's devotees; it is not to be given to others. ॥69॥
7.2.32.70: One who accomplishes the rite himself by his own ability, without relying on a guru or others, should also act in this way here; he should not take the materials back for himself. ॥70॥
7.2.32.71: The fool who out of greed takes for himself the excellent materials that formed part of the worship will not obtain what he desires; there is no doubt about this. ॥71॥
7.2.32.72: As for the liṅga that was worshipped, one may take it oneself or not; if one takes it, then it should be worshipped daily, either by oneself or by another. ॥72॥
7.2.32.73: For one who performs this rite exactly as prescribed, without lapse, the fruit never fails; so what further inducement is needed? ॥73॥
7.2.32.74: Nevertheless I shall describe in brief the supreme accomplishment of the rite. Even one assailed by enemies or by diseases in many ways, ॥74॥
7.2.32.75: or even one gone into the mouth of death, is released without harm. The utterly wretched becomes honoured; the destitute becomes like Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera). ॥75॥
7.2.32.76: Even the ugly becomes like Kāma; even the old becomes youthful; an enemy at once becomes a friend; an opponent becomes a servant. ॥76॥
7.2.32.77: What was nectar becomes poison for his foes, and even poison becomes nectar; even the ocean becomes dry land, and dry land becomes the sea. ॥77॥
7.2.32.78: A chasm becomes a mountain, and that mountain becomes a chasm; fire becomes a lotus-pond, and a lake becomes fire. ॥78॥
7.2.32.79: What was a garden becomes a forest, and that forest becomes a garden; a petty deer becomes a lion, and a lion becomes a pet deer. ॥79॥
7.2.32.80: Women come to him like eager lovers; Lakṣmī (fortune) becomes faithful; speech becomes like a willing servant; and fame roams everywhere like a courtesan. ॥80॥
7.2.32.81: For the one who has accomplished this rite, the intellect becomes like one who moves at his own will; the mind becomes like a diamond needle; his power becomes like a mighty wind; his strength becomes like a rutting elephant. ॥81॥
7.2.32.82: Any undertaking set up on the enemies' side becomes paralysed despite their great efforts; all of the enemies' own friends turn into the enemy's camp against them. ॥82॥
7.2.32.83: The enemies, together with their kinsmen, become like corpses even while alive; and he himself, even if fallen into calamity, is freed from misfortune and indeed becomes like nectar (immortal). ॥83॥
7.2.32.84: Even unwholesome food constantly consumed becomes like an elixir; and love-delight, though enjoyed incessantly, ever feels new. ॥84॥
7.2.32.85: Everything, the future and so on, becomes as clear as an āmalaka fruit held in the hand; even the powers beginning with aṇimā (minuteness) come as spontaneous fruits. ॥85॥
7.2.32.86: What is the use of saying much here? When this rite has been accomplished, there is nothing unattainable in the fulfilment of all desires and aims. ॥86॥
7.2.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named Rites for attainments in this world, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥32॥
7.2.33.1: Upamanyu said: Next I shall explain the rite that is purely for the next world. There is no act equal to it in the three worlds. ॥1॥
7.2.33.2: It is endowed with surpassing merit and has been performed by all the gods—by Brahmā, by Viṣṇu, and especially by Rudra; ॥2॥
7.2.33.3: by Indra and the other guardians of the worlds, by the nine planets beginning with the Sun, by the great sages who know Brahman, such as Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha; ॥3॥
7.2.33.4: by Śveta, Agastya, Dadhīca and others, and by us who have taken refuge in Śiva; by the lords of the gaṇas such as Nandīśvara, Mahākāla and Bhṛṅgīśa; ॥4॥
7.2.33.5: by the Daityas dwelling in Pātāla, by the great serpents such as Śeṣa, by Siddhas, Yakṣas and Gandharvas, by Rākṣasas, Bhūtas and Piśācas— ॥5॥
7.2.33.6: this rite was performed by all of them, and each attained his own position. By this rite all the gods attained their divinity. ॥6॥
7.2.33.7: Brahmā attained his Brahmā-hood, Viṣṇu attained his Viṣṇu-hood, Rudra attained his Rudra-hood, and Indra attained his Indra-hood. ॥7॥
7.2.33.8: And Gaṇeśa attained his lordship of the gaṇas by this rite. Having bathed the liṅga—Śiva and Śivā—with water mixed with white sandal, having worshipped it with white, fully blossomed lotuses and bowed down, ॥8॥
7.2.33.9: one should there make a beautiful lotus-seat possessing the proper marks—if one has the wealth, of gold and the like, or of jewels and the like, according to one's means. ॥9॥
7.2.33.10: In the middle of its cluster of filaments one should place a small liṅga, the size of a thumb, beautiful, auspicious, made of all fragrant substances. ॥10॥
7.2.33.11: Having placed it on the right (south), one should worship it with bilva leaves. On the southern side one should offer aguru, and on the west red arsenic; ॥11॥
7.2.33.12: on the north one should offer sandal, and on the east yellow orpiment. One should also worship with fragrant, lovely and variegated flowers. ॥12॥
7.2.33.13: One should offer incense of black aguru mixed with guggulu all around, and present very fine, unfolded garments. ॥13॥
7.2.33.14: One should have milk-rice mixed with ghee and ghee lamps offered. Having offered everything with the mantra, one should then circumambulate. ॥14॥
7.2.33.15: Having bowed with devotion to the Lord of the gods and praised him, at the end one should ask forgiveness. Then one should offer the liṅga together with all the offerings, ॥15॥
7.2.33.16: to Śiva with the Śiva-mantra, resorting to the southern form (Dakṣiṇāmūrti). Whoever thus daily worships the auspicious liṅga made of the five fragrant substances, ॥16॥
7.2.33.17: freed from all sins, is honoured in Śiva's world. This is the supreme secret vow, the great vow of the Śiva-liṅga. ॥17॥
7.2.33.18: It has been told to you, a devotee; it should not be given to just anyone. It should be given to devotees of Śiva—so it was declared by Śiva of old. ॥18॥
7.2.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The rules of rites for the world beyond, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥33॥
7.2.34.1: Upamanyu said: Whatever attainment has been proclaimed here as arising from the obligatory, the occasional and the optional rites, all of it is obtained at once through the installation of a liṅga or an image. ॥1॥
7.2.34.2: The whole world consists of the liṅga; everything is established in the liṅga. Therefore, when the liṅga is installed, everything becomes established. ॥2॥
7.2.34.3: Whether by Brahmā, by Viṣṇu, by Rudra or by anyone else — none secures the stability of his own position by setting aside the installation of the liṅga. ॥3॥
7.2.34.4: What else need be said here as the reason for installation, since even Śiva himself installed the liṅga of Viśveśvara? ॥4॥
7.2.34.5: Therefore, with every effort, for well-being here and hereafter, one should install a liṅga of the Supreme Lord, or else an image. ॥5॥
7.2.34.6: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: What is this that is called the liṅga? How is Maheśvara the bearer of the liṅga? How does he have the nature of the liṅga, and why is Śiva worshipped in it? ॥6॥
7.2.34.7: Upamanyu said: The Unmanifest is called the liṅga — the origin and dissolution of the three guṇas, without beginning or end, which is the material cause of the universe. ॥7॥
7.2.34.8: That alone is primordial Nature (mūlaprakṛti) and Māyā, whose nature is like space. From that alone this world of moving and unmoving beings has arisen. ॥8॥
7.2.34.9: That world is threefold: impure, pure, and pure-impure. From it arise Śiva, Maheśa, Rudra, Viṣṇu and the Grandsire (Brahmā), ॥9॥
7.2.34.10: and the elements together with the senses, are born, and they dissolve into it by Śiva's command. For this very reason Śiva is called the liṅga-possessor, since he commands the liṅga. ॥10॥
7.2.34.11: For, unbidden by him, it cannot of itself become capable of any effect; and the universe born from it dissolves back into that very liṅga. ॥11॥
7.2.34.12: It is by this that it has the nature of the liṅga, and not by anything else. And the liṅga is the body of Śiva and Śivā, since it is presided over by the two of them. ॥12॥
7.2.34.13: Therefore one should always worship Śiva together with Ambā there. The pedestal of the liṅga is the Great Goddess; the liṅga is Maheśvara himself. ॥13॥
7.2.34.14: By worshipping these two alone, both he and she are worshipped. In ultimate truth, however, they do not have the liṅga as their body. ॥14॥
7.2.34.15: For those two are utterly pure; it is called their body only figuratively. That very liṅga is the supreme Śakti of Śiva, the Supreme Self. ॥15॥
7.2.34.16: When the Śakti receives his command, she brings forth the moving and unmoving world. His greatness cannot be told even in hundreds of years, ॥16॥
7.2.34.17: by which even Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa were bewildered in the beginning. Long ago, when the dissolution of these three worlds had come, ॥17॥
7.2.34.18: Viṣṇu, lying on his bed upon the waters, slept happily, undisturbed. By chance Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds, came there. ॥18॥
7.2.34.19: He saw the lotus-eyed one sleeping undisturbed. Deluded by Śambhu's Māyā, the Grandsire spoke to Viṣṇu. ॥19॥
7.2.34.20: Striking Mādhava in anger and rousing him, he said: Tell me, who are you? Struck by that sharp blow of the hand, he at once ॥20॥
7.2.34.21: awoke, rose from his bed and saw Parameṣṭhin (Brahmā). Inwardly enraged, yet outwardly as though unangered, Hari spoke to him: ॥21॥
7.2.34.22: Where have you come from, child? Why are you agitated? Tell me. Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, which suggested his own superiority, ॥22॥
7.2.34.23: Brahmā, bound in enmity by rajas, again spoke to him: Why do you call me child, as a teacher would his own pupil? ॥23॥
7.2.34.24: Do you not know me, the Lord, whose creation this manifold world is? Dividing myself threefold, I create this and then it is protected by me; ॥24॥
7.2.34.25: and I destroy it. No other creator than me exists in the world. When this was said, the imperishable Viṣṇu also spoke to Brahmā: ॥25॥
7.2.34.26: I alone am the first maker of this, its destroyer and its protector. You too descended long ago from my own imperishable body. ॥26॥
7.2.34.27: By my command you, making yourself threefold, create the three worlds, protect them, and at the end withdraw them and create them again. ॥27॥
7.2.34.28: You have forgotten Nārāyaṇa, the flawless Lord of the world; thus you disregard me, who am directly your own father. ॥28॥
7.2.34.29: There is no fault of yours in this; you are deluded by my Māyā. By my grace this delusion of yours will soon depart. ॥29॥
7.2.34.30: Hear the truth, O four-faced one: I indeed am the Lord of all gods — creator, sustainer and destroyer. There is no lord equal to me. ॥30॥
7.2.34.31: Thus a dispute arose between Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and there ensued a great, terrible, hair-raising battle, ॥31॥
7.2.34.32: as the two, bound in enmity by rajas, struck each other fiercely with their fists. To remove the pride of those two gods and to awaken them, ॥32॥
7.2.34.33: a wondrous liṅga of the Lord appeared between them, rich with thousands of garlands of flames, immeasurable and incomparable, ॥33॥
7.2.34.34: free from decrease and growth, devoid of beginning, middle and end. By its thousand flames Brahmā and Viṣṇu were bewildered. ॥34॥
7.2.34.35: Abandoning the fight, they then wondered, what is this? When its true nature did not become clear to them, ॥35॥
7.2.34.36: then they set out to examine its beginning and end. ॥36॥
7.2.34.37: There Brahmā, taking the form of a swan with wings on every side and becoming swift as mind and wind, went upward with great effort. ॥37॥
7.2.34.38: Nārāyaṇa too, the Self of the universe, assuming an immeasurable boar form like a mass of dark collyrium, went downward. ॥38॥
7.2.34.39: Thus for a thousand years Viṣṇu, the boar, hastened downward, yet did not see even a trace of the root of that liṅga. ॥39॥
7.2.34.40: For the same length of time the Grandsire went upward, wishing to know its end; utterly exhausted and not having seen the end, he fell down. ॥40॥
7.2.34.41: In the same way the blessed Viṣṇu, exhausted, his eyes full of agitation, quickly rose up from below with great hardship. ॥41॥
7.2.34.42: Then the two met each other, their glances wide with wonder; deluded by Śambhu's māyā, they did not know what was to be done and what was not. ॥42॥
7.2.34.43: Both, standing behind it, beside it and in front of it, bowed down and then pondered, what is the nature of this? ॥43॥
7.2.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The delusion of Hari and Vidhi, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥34॥
7.2.35.1: Upamanyu said: Then there appeared there, with resonance, Brahman marked by sound: the one-syllabled Brahman Om, which makes Brahman known. ॥1॥
7.2.35.2: Even that was at first not understood by Brahmā and likewise by Viṣṇu, because the minds of the two were obscured by rajas and tamas. ॥2॥
7.2.35.3: Then that single syllable became divided fourfold: into the three morae a, u, m, and beyond them the half-mora. ॥3॥
7.2.35.4: There the letter a rested on the southern side of the blazing liṅga, the letter u likewise on the northern, and the letter m in its middle. ॥4॥
7.2.35.5: The nāda consisting of the half-mora was heard at the top of the liṅga. Even when that praṇava, the supreme syllable, had then been divided, ॥5॥
7.2.35.6: those two gods understood nothing of the meaning of the division. Then the unmanifest praṇava underwent transformation in the form of the Vedas. ॥6॥
7.2.35.7: There the letter a became the Ṛk, the letter u the imperishable Yajus, the letter m became the Sāman, and the nāda the Atharvan śruti. ॥7॥
7.2.35.8: This Ṛk set forth its own meaning in brief: among the guṇas, rajas; among the forms, Brahmā, the first; and among the activities — ॥8॥
7.2.35.9: creation; among the worlds, the earth; among the tattvas, the imperishable Ātman; in the path of the kalās, Nivṛtti; and among the five Brahmans, Sadyojāta; ॥9॥
7.2.35.10: among the parts of the liṅga, the lower part; among the three causes, the one called bīja (seed); and among the powers beginning with aṇimā, the lordship of sixty-four qualities that pertains to buddhi. ॥10॥
7.2.35.11: Thus the whole world is pervaded by the Ṛk through these ten meanings. Then the Yajus set forth its own tenfold meaning: ॥11॥
7.2.35.12: among the guṇas, sattva; among the forms, Viṣṇu, the first; among the activities, preservation; among the worlds, the mid-space; and among the three tattvas, Vidyā; ॥12॥
7.2.35.13: among the kalā-paths, Pratiṣṭhā; among the five Brahmans, Vāmadeva; among the parts of the liṅga, the middle; and among the three causes, the yoni (womb); ॥13॥
7.2.35.14: and likewise the prākṛta lordship — hence the universe consists of the Yajus. Then the Sāman set forth its own meaning tenfold: ॥14॥
7.2.35.15: among the guṇas, tamas; among the forms, Rudra, the first; among the activities, dissolution in the three worlds; among the tattvas, Śiva, the highest; ॥15॥
7.2.35.16: among the kalās, Vidyā; and likewise among the five Brahmans, Aghora; among the parts of the liṅga, the part above the pedestal; among the three causes, the seed-bearer; ॥16॥
7.2.35.17: and likewise the pauruṣa lordship — thus the world is pervaded by the Sāman. Then the Atharvan declared its first meaning: being beyond the guṇas; ॥17॥
7.2.35.18: then, among the forms, Sadāśiva, Maheśvara himself; among the activities, of Śiva the supreme Self, though actionless, ॥18॥
7.2.35.19: the bestowal of grace on beings, by which creatures are liberated; among the worlds, that from which words turn back together with the mind — ॥19॥
7.2.35.20: above that, beyond the Unmanā world, the supramundane Soma-world, where the Lord Soma (he who is with Umā) ever dwells together with Umā; ॥20॥
7.2.35.21: above that, beyond the Unmanā world, reaching which one does not return; and among the kalās, Śānti, Śāntyatītā and Vyāpikā; ॥21॥
7.2.35.22: among the five Brahmans, Tatpuruṣa and likewise Īśāna; among the parts marked by nāda, the unsurpassed top of the liṅga, ॥22॥
7.2.35.23: where Śiva, alone and partless, is to be invoked and worshipped; then, among those tattvas, beyond bindu, beyond nāda, beyond śakti, and beyond the supreme beyond that, ॥23॥
7.2.35.24: the tattva beyond every tattva, in ultimate truth no tattva at all; among the causes, transcending the three — beyond the cause that agitates māyā, ॥24॥
7.2.35.25: beyond Ananta, beyond Śuddhavidyā, and beyond Maheśvara, the overlord of all the Vidyeśvaras, yet not beyond the supreme Sadāśiva, ॥25॥
