7.2.35.26: beyond the god whose body is all mantras, endowed with the three śaktis, five-faced, ten-armed, himself both with and without parts; ॥26॥
7.2.35.27: beyond even him, beyond the supreme bindu, beyond the half-moon and the supreme beyond that; beyond the supreme Lord of the Night beyond that, and beyond the one called nāda and what is beyond it; ॥27॥
7.2.35.28: beyond the still higher Lord of Suṣumnā, beyond even the Lord of the Brahmarandhra, beyond what is higher than that, beyond Śakti, and beyond the Śiva-tattva — ॥28॥
7.2.35.29: it declared Śiva, the supreme cause itself, himself without cause, the ordainer of causes, the meditator and the object of meditation, imperishable, ॥29॥
7.2.35.30: abiding in the midst of the supreme ether, situated above the supreme Self, endowed with all lordship, lord of all, having no lord over him; ॥30॥
7.2.35.31: and beyond the lordship born of māyā, impure, human and the like, both lower and higher, to be abandoned, lying within the range of the impure path; ॥31॥
7.2.35.32: beyond that, beyond the higher-than-high lordship beginning with Śuddhavidyā and ending with Unmanā — the supreme lordship, primal beyond Unmanā, and beginningless, ॥32॥
7.2.35.33: boundless, dependent on no other, unsurpassable, steady. Thus, with meanings of ten kinds, this Atharvan śruti — ॥33॥
7.2.35.34: since it is the weightiest, therefore the universe is pervaded by the Atharvan. The Ṛgveda then said: This waking state is expressed by me, ॥34॥
7.2.35.35: by which I am ever the expresser of the ātma-tattva. The Yajurveda likewise said: The dream state is expressed by me, ॥35॥
7.2.35.36: since in me Vidyā, the knowable, is transformed into the form of what is to be enjoyed. And the Sāman said: What is called deep sleep — thus everything is expressed by me; ॥36॥
7.2.35.37: this is denoted by Śiva, the tāmasa one, who is my meaning. The Atharvan said: What is called the fourth (turīya), and also what is beyond the fourth, ॥37॥
7.2.35.38: is expressed by me; therefore I belong to the state beyond the paths. The triad constituted by the paths is designated Śiva, Vidyā and Ātman. ॥38॥
7.2.35.39: That triad of the three guṇas, attainable through the three Vedas, is to be purified by one who seeks the highest state. What lies beyond the paths, called turīya, is nirvāṇa, the supreme state; ॥39॥
7.2.35.40: and what is beyond that, because it is free of the guṇas, is the purifier of this path. The nāda that makes both known, and the nādānta, are of my nature. ॥40॥
7.2.35.41: Therefore, because I am independent as its meaning, the Supreme Lord is its principal sense. Whatever object exists, all of that is also its meaning, in a secondary or a principal way. ॥41॥
7.2.35.42: They declare all things, taken together and also separately, to be the meaning of the praṇava. Therefore this one syllable, which is Brahman, denotes all meanings. ॥42॥
7.2.35.43: By it, uttering Om, Śiva first makes the entire world. For Śiva is this praṇava, and the praṇava is declared to be Śiva. ॥43॥
7.2.35.44: For there is no absolute difference between what is denoted and what denotes it. Rudra is beyond thought, since words, together with the mind, ॥44॥
7.2.35.45: turn back without reaching him. Yet he is denoted by the single syllable. From the single part of the syllable called A, Brahmā, called Ātman, is designated. ॥45॥
7.2.35.46: From the single letter called U, Viṣṇu, called Vidyā, is declared. From the single letter called M, Rudra, called Śiva, is spoken of. ॥46॥
7.2.35.47: From the right side of Maheśa was born Brahmā, known as Ātman; from the left side arose Viṣṇu, who is therefore called Vidyā. ॥47॥
7.2.35.48: From Śiva's heart arose Nīlarudra, known as Śiva. Brahmā is the initiator of creation; Viṣṇu, the deluder, of preservation; ॥48॥
7.2.35.49: and likewise Rudra is the initiator of dissolution, and always the controller of those two. ॥49॥
7.2.35.50: Therefore those three are called the causes of the world; and Śiva, the source of the three causes, is the supreme cause. ॥50॥
7.2.35.51: Because you two, bound in enmity by rajas, did not understand this meaning, the liṅga appeared between you to awaken you. ॥51॥
7.2.35.52: Thus they call me Om, as has been stated here by Atharvan, and by the Ṛk verses, the Yajus formulas, the Sāman chants, and other branches by the thousand. ॥52॥
7.2.35.53: Even though the Vedas themselves thus plainly declare it with their own mouths, the two could not grasp it, as if it were something experienced in a dream. ॥53॥
7.2.35.54: So, to awaken them there and to remove their darkness, everything was imprinted on the liṅga too, just as the Vedas had declared it. ॥54॥
7.2.35.55: Having seen that imprinted on the liṅga, then, by the grace of the Lord of the liṅga, the two gods became calm in mind and awakened. ॥55॥
7.2.35.56: Knowing the origin and dissolution and the true nature of the six paths, and the abode higher than them, and the Person who possesses that abode, ॥56॥
7.2.35.57: the Brahman beyond which there is nothing higher, partless, Śiva the Lord, eternally the master of this universe made of bound souls (paśu) and bonds (pāśa), ॥57॥
7.2.35.58: fearing nothing from any quarter, utterly beyond, without growth or decay, imperishable, pervading outside and inside, yet free of outside and inside, ॥58॥
7.2.35.59: unsurpassed, eternal, distinct from all the worlds, without marks, indescribable, beyond the range of speech and mind, ॥59॥
7.2.35.60: whose sole essence is light, peaceful, gracious, ever-risen, the abode of all auspiciousness, accompanied by a Śakti of the same nature — ॥60॥
7.2.35.61: having come to know the god Virūpākṣa, Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa then, frightened, joined their palms above their heads and spoke these words. ॥61॥
7.2.35.62: Brahmā said: Ignorant or knowing, I was created by you in the beginning, O God. If I have fallen into such delusion, who is at fault in this? ॥62॥
7.2.35.63: Let this ignorance of mine be set aside. When you are present, O Lord, who could fearlessly speak of what must be done, whether by himself or by another? ॥63॥
7.2.35.64: Even the quarrel between us two has indeed been auspicious, since it has yielded the fruit of bowing at the feet of you, the Lord, the God of gods. ॥64॥
7.2.35.65: Viṣṇu said: O God, there is no speech equal to your greatness with which to praise you; yet before the Lord, silence on the part of servants is a transgression. ॥65॥
7.2.35.66: What would be fitting to do here? Only this is suited to the occasion. Though not knowing, having babbled something or other, I bow to you. ॥66॥
7.2.35.67: The status of cause given by you was forgotten through your māyā; deluded and full of ego, I have been corrected once again. ॥67॥
7.2.35.68: What use are many entreaties? I am deeply afraid, O Lord, because I set out to measure you, the immeasurable. ॥68॥
7.2.35.69: They call you Mahādeva, the destroyer of the distress of the frightened; therefore, O Śaṅkara, please forgive my transgression today. ॥69॥
7.2.35.70: Thus entreated by those two lords, Maheśvara, pleased, showed favour to the two gods and spoke with a smile. ॥70॥
7.2.35.71: Īśvara said: Dear child, dear child, O Vidhi (Brahmā), O Viṣṇu, deluded by my māyā, you two, priding yourselves on lordship and with enmity roused against each other, ॥71॥
7.2.35.72: carried your quarrel as far as battle and did not stop, it is said. Then the creation of beings was interrupted, since you two are the causes of the world, ॥72॥
7.2.35.73: because of the disagreement between you two born of ignorance and pride. To put an end to that, your pride and delusion, by me alone, ॥73॥
7.2.35.74: have thus been removed today through the play of the liṅga's manifestation. Therefore, giving up quarrel and shame completely, ॥74॥
7.2.35.75: may you two perform your respective tasks, free of jealousy. Formerly, by my command, together with the mantra, all the knowledge-compendia (jñāna-saṃhitā) ॥75॥
7.2.35.76: were given by me to you two, so that your status as causes might be established; and the supreme jewel among mantras, called the sūtra, consisting of five syllables, ॥76॥
7.2.35.77: was taught by me; all that has been forgotten by you two today. And I give it all again, as before, by my command, ॥77॥
7.2.35.78: since without it you two are not capable of creation and protection. Having spoken thus, Mahādeva, to Nārāyaṇa and Pitāmaha (Brahmā), ॥78॥
7.2.35.79: gave to those two the king of mantras together with the knowledge-compendium. Having received the great, divine, supreme command of Maheśvara, ॥79॥
7.2.35.80: and the mantra-jewel of great meaning, and likewise all the kalās, the two prostrated themselves like a staff at the feet of the God of gods. ॥80॥
7.2.35.81: Then the two stood there, freed from fear and motionless with bliss. Meanwhile, wondrously, like a magic show, the divine liṅga of the Lord— ॥81॥
7.2.35.82: —the liṅga vanished somewhere and could no longer be perceived by the two. Then, lamenting, alas, alas, at the sudden breaking of their affection, ॥82॥
7.2.35.83: and saying to each other, what a marvel is this that has happened, and reflecting on the inconceivable glory of Śambhu, they became free of distress. ॥83॥
7.2.35.84: Having entered into supreme friendship and embraced each other, the two foremost of gods departed to attend to the business of the world. ॥84॥
7.2.35.85: From then on, all the gods and asuras beginning with Śakra, the sages, men, Nāgas and women too, install the liṅga according to the prescribed rites and worship him in the liṅga. ॥85॥
7.2.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The removal of the delusion of Hari and Vidhi, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥35॥
7.2.36.1: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Lord, I wish to hear the excellent rite of installation (pratiṣṭhā) of the liṅga and also of the image, as Śiva ordained it. ॥1॥
7.2.36.2: Upamanyu said: On a day not unfavourable to oneself, in the bright fortnight, one should make a liṅga of proper measurements, following the method taught in the Śaiva scriptures. ॥2॥
7.2.36.3: Then, having chosen an auspicious site and examined the ground, one should perform the ten preparatory rites, beginning with the marking out of the characteristic lines. ॥3॥
7.2.36.4: Before those ten rites, having worshipped Vināyaka and done the purification of the place and the rest, one should bring the liṅga to the bathing hall. ॥4॥
7.2.36.5: Then, with a golden stylus dipped in saffron and other liquids, one should inscribe the marked characteristic lines according to the Śilpa-śāstra. ॥5॥
7.2.36.6: With waters mixed with eight kinds of earth, or likewise with five kinds of earth, and with the five cow-products, one should purify the liṅga together with its pedestal. ॥6॥
7.2.36.7: Having worshipped it together with its pedestal and taken it to a body of water—a celestial one or another—one should there perform the adhivāsa of the liṅga together with its pedestal. ॥7॥
7.2.36.8: In a pure adhivāsa pavilion, endowed with every adornment, with arched gateways and an enclosure, encircled by garlands of darbha grass, ॥8॥
7.2.36.9: furnished with the eight elephants of the quarters, provided with eight pots for the guardians of the directions, equipped with the eight auspicious objects, and where worship of the directional guardians has been performed, ॥9॥
7.2.36.10: having made a broad seat-platform of metal or of wood, marked with a lotus seat, one should place it there in the middle. ॥10॥
7.2.36.11: Having worshipped the doorkeepers, the four beginning with Bhadra, in order—Subhadra, Vibhadra, Sunanda and Vinandaka— ॥11॥
7.2.36.12: having bathed and worshipped the liṅga together with its pedestal, and having wrapped it all round with two cloths along with kūrcas (bundles of darbha), ॥12॥
7.2.36.13: and having slowly brought it to the water, one should lay it upon the platform with its head to the east, the line (sūtra) below, and its pedestal to the west. ॥13॥
7.2.36.14: There one should keep the liṅga in adhivāsa, accompanied by all auspicious things, for five nights, three nights, or even one night. ॥14॥
7.2.36.15: Having dismissed what was worshipped there and purified it as before, having worshipped it in the manner of a festival procession, one should bring it to the hall of the couch. ॥15॥
7.2.36.16: There too one should make the place of the couch in the middle of a maṇḍala; having bathed the liṅga with pure waters, one should worship it in due order. ॥16॥
7.2.36.17: In the north-east, on ground that is clean and smeared, having drawn a lotus and purified the Śiva-pot, one should invoke Śiva there and worship him. ॥17॥
7.2.36.18: Having designed a white lotus in the middle of the altar according to rule, one should also draw the lotus of Caṇḍikā to its west. ॥18॥
7.2.36.19: Having prepared a couch with new cloths of linen and the like, or with flowers or darbha grass, one should place a golden flower upon it. ॥19॥
7.2.36.20: Having brought the liṅga there amid the sounds of every auspicious instrument, with a pair of red cloths together with a kūrca all round, ॥20॥
7.2.36.21: having wrapped it together with its pedestal, one should lay it down as before. Having drawn a lotus in front, on its petals in due order ॥21॥
7.2.36.22: one should set the pots of the Vidyeśas, and in the middle the Śaiva vardhanī pot. Around the three lotuses the best of the twice-born should offer oblations. ॥22॥
7.2.36.23: They are to be conceived as the eight forms of Śiva, stationed all round beginning from the east; or else four, in the cardinal directions, good Vedic reciters together with mantra-repeaters. ॥23॥
7.2.36.24: They should offer oblations; they are regarded as the four forms beginning with Viriñci. The preceptor, first among them, in the north-east or else in the west, ॥24॥
7.2.36.25: should perform the principal homa with the seven substances in due order; the other twice-born should offer a quarter or a half of what the ācārya offers. ॥25॥
7.2.36.26: Or the guru alone may offer the principal oblation here. First, having offered the full oblation, and a hundred and eight oblations with ghee, ॥26॥
7.2.36.27: one should place the Śiva-hand on the head of the liṅga with the root mantra. Offering a hundred, fifty, or half of that, in order, with the seven substances, ॥27॥
7.2.36.28: after each offering one should touch the liṅga and the pedestal again and again. Then, having offered the full oblation, one should give the fees in due order: ॥28॥
7.2.36.29: to the hotṛ priests and to the architect a quarter or a half of the ācārya's fee; half of that is to be given to the others and to the assembly members, according to one's means. ॥29॥
7.2.36.30: Then, having placed a golden bull or a kūrca in the pit, with earth-water, with the five cow-products, and again with pure water, ॥30॥
7.2.36.31: one should set in the pit the Brahma-stone, purified and smeared with sandal. Then, having performed kara-nyāsa with the nine names of the Śaktis, ॥31॥
7.2.36.32: one should deposit on the Brahma-stone orpiment and other minerals, together with seeds, fragrances and herbs, by the rule stated in the Śaiva scriptures. ॥32॥
7.2.36.33: Having set up a substitute liṅga made from a milky-sap tree, and having ascertained that it stands properly, removing it, one should set the liṅga upon the Brahma-stone, ॥33॥
7.2.36.34: one should install it slightly inclined toward the north-east with the root-vidyā; and then, joining the pedestal, recalling the Śākta root mantra, ॥34॥
7.2.36.35: having made the binding with binding substances and purified the place, and having offered arghya and flowers, they should again draw the curtain. ॥35॥
7.2.36.36: Then, for the sprinkling and other rites as appropriate, having brought the pots from the place of the couch, one should set them in order in front of the liṅga. ॥36॥
7.2.36.37: Then, beginning the great worship and having worshipped the ten pots, recalling the Śiva-mantra within the water of the Śiva-pot, ॥37॥
7.2.36.38: taking it up by joining thumb and ring finger, one should raise it; the knower of mantras should place it in the middle of the Īśāna portion of the liṅga. ॥38॥
7.2.36.39: Likewise one should place the Śakti, the Vidyā and the Vidyeśas in due order at the base of the liṅga; then one should sprinkle the liṅga with the Śiva-waters. ॥39॥
7.2.36.40: Having anointed the pedestal with the vardhanī and the liṅga again with the Vidyeśa pots, one should afterwards arrange the seat beginning with the ādhāra (support). ॥40॥
7.2.36.41: Having performed the placement (nyāsa) of the five kalās, one should contemplate the liṅga as blazing with radiance; then, with joined palms, facing north-east, one should invoke the two Śivas, Śiva and Śivā, as directly present, ॥41॥
7.2.36.42: contemplating the God coming down from the expanse of the sky together with the Goddess, mounted on the king of bulls or on a celestial car, adorned, rich in the splendour of every ornament, amid the sounds of all auspicious instruments, ॥42॥
7.2.36.43: surrounded by gods and dānavas headed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, the Sun and Indra, all their limbs moist with bliss, with joined palms placed upon their heads, ॥43॥
7.2.36.44: surrounded on all sides by them praising, dancing and bowing. Then, having performed worship with the five offerings (upacāras), one should conclude it. ॥44॥
7.2.36.45: There is no rite higher than this, namely than the fivefold offering. One should perform the installation for images too in every respect as for the liṅga. ॥45॥
7.2.36.46: At the time of carving out the features, the opening of the eyes should be done. During the water-residence and on the bed, one should lay them the images face downward. ॥46॥
7.2.36.47: With mantras one should join the deity in the heart of that image laid on the water of the pot. They declare installation in a place where a temple has been built to be superior to that without a temple. ॥47॥
7.2.36.48: One who is capable should first build the temple and afterwards perform the installation rite. If one is incapable, having installed a liṅga or else an image, ॥48॥
7.2.36.49: he should afterwards build a temple of Śiva in accordance with his means. And next I shall describe the excellent rite of installation for domestic worship. ॥49॥
7.2.36.50: Having made a small image or a liṅga endowed with the proper marks, when the northern course of the sun has arrived, in the bright fortnight, on an auspicious day, ॥50॥
7.2.36.51: having made an altar in an auspicious place, one should draw a lotus there as before; having strewn leaves, flowers and so on, and having set a pot in the middle, ॥51॥
7.2.36.52: one should place four vessels around it in the four directions. The five Brahman mantras, with their five seed-syllables, in those five vessels— ॥52॥
7.2.36.53: having placed them, worshipped them, shown the mudrās and so on, and protected them; having purified the liṅga or image with earth, water and the like as before, ॥53॥
7.2.36.54: one should set it, covered with flowers, on an excellent seat placed to the north; placing a flower on its head, one should sprinkle it with the sprinkling-water. ॥54॥
7.2.36.55: Having again worshipped it with flowers, preceded by cries of victory and the like, one should bathe it with the root mantra, using the pots charged with the mantras ending with Īśāna. ॥55॥
7.2.36.56: Then, having performed the placement of the five kalās and the worship as before, one should daily worship there the three-eyed God together with the Goddess. ॥56॥
7.2.36.57: Or else, having placed a single pot, furnished with the mantra of the form (mūrti-mantra), within the lotus, one should perform all the rest as before. ॥57॥
7.2.36.58: A liṅga that has been severely defiled should be purified and installed again; one that is defiled should be re-consecrated by sprinkling; one slightly defiled should simply be worshipped. ॥58॥
7.2.36.59: Liṅgas called Bāṇa may or may not be installed, since they were already consecrated by Śiva himself beforehand. ॥59॥
7.2.36.60: The remaining ones are to be installed; but those seen to be like the Bāṇa liṅgas—in the case of a self-manifested liṅga, a divine one, and likewise one established by sages— ॥60॥
7.2.36.61: if it lacks a pedestal, one should fit a pedestal, perform the rite of sprinkling, and worship Śiva there; installation is not prescribed for them. ॥61॥
7.2.36.62: A liṅga that is burnt, loosened, or with damaged parts should be cast into a body of water; one fit for repair should be joined together and then the installation rite performed. ॥62॥
7.2.36.63: From a defective image or liṅga, after first worshipping the deity, one should withdraw the deity into the heart and then carry out repair or abandonment, as appropriate. ॥63॥
7.2.36.64: If worship is interrupted for one day, one should perform double worship; for two nights, a great worship; beyond that, re-consecration by sprinkling. ॥64॥
7.2.36.65: If worship is interrupted for many days, beyond a month, some prescribe fresh installation, others the procedure of re-consecration by sprinkling. ॥65॥
7.2.36.66: In the re-consecration of a liṅga and the like, having withdrawn the deity as before, having bathed it with earth and water in the order of eight and five, ॥66॥
7.2.36.67: and having bathed it with the products of the cow and purified it with darbha-water, one should sprinkle it with the sprinkling-water a hundred and eight times with the root mantra. ॥67॥
7.2.36.68: Placing his hand, holding flowers and kuśa grass, on the top of the liṅga, he should repeat the root mantra five times over a hundred and eight times. ॥68॥
7.2.36.69: Then with the root mantra he should also touch it from the top down to the pedestal, and, having invoked the deity as before, perform a great worship. ॥69॥
7.2.36.70: When an installed liṅga is not available, one should worship the Lord Śiva at a place sacred to Śiva, or in water, in fire, in the sun, or likewise in the sky. ॥70॥
7.2.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The rite of installation, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥36॥
7.2.37.1: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: All that the Lord has taught in summary, drawing out the essence of knowledge, ritual action and conduct, I have heard, and it is equal to the Veda. ॥1॥
7.2.37.2: Now I wish to hear about yoga, which is supremely hard to attain, together with who is qualified for it, its limbs, its procedure and its purpose. ॥2॥
7.2.37.3: If death comes first, before yoga and the rest have been brought to completion, tell me the means by which the goal can be accomplished at once, so that a man does not become a destroyer of his own self. ॥3॥
7.2.37.4: Please explain truly that means, its cause, its proper time and instruments, and the gradation of its varieties. ॥4॥
7.2.37.5: Upamanyu said: Fittingly have you asked, O Kṛṣṇa, you who know the purport of every question. So I shall tell all of it in order; listen attentively. ॥5॥
7.2.37.6: The steady activity, fixed on Śiva, of a mind whose other activities have been restrained—that, in brief, is yoga; and it is indeed fivefold. ॥6॥
7.2.37.7: Mantra-yoga, sparśa-yoga, bhāva-yoga, and another, abhāva-yoga; and mahā-yoga is held to be the highest of all. ॥7॥
7.2.37.8: The undistracted activity of the mind, resting on the meaning signified by the mantra, arising solely through the power of repeated practice of the mantra, is called mantra-yoga. ॥8॥
7.2.37.9: That same mental activity, led by breath-control, is called sparśa-yoga; when it is free of both mantra and touch, it is declared bhāva-yoga. ॥9॥
7.2.37.10: That in which the universe is contemplated as a form whose parts have dissolved is called abhāva-yoga, because the existing object no longer appears. ॥10॥
7.2.37.11: The mental activity in which Śiva's own nature alone, without any limiting adjunct, is contemplated—that Śaiva state of mind is here called mahā-yoga. ॥11॥
7.2.37.12: He whose mind is detached from objects, both those seen in this world and those heard of in scripture—he alone is qualified for yoga, no one else. ॥12॥
7.2.37.13: The mind becomes detached simply by constantly seeing the faults of both kinds of objects and the virtues of the Lord. ॥13॥
7.2.37.14: All yoga, in brief, has either eight limbs or six limbs: yama, niyama, and posture beginning with svastika; ॥14॥
7.2.37.15: breath-control, withdrawal of the senses, concentration, meditation and absorption—these eight limbs of yoga are declared by the wise. ॥15॥
7.2.37.16: Posture, restraint of breath, withdrawal, then concentration, meditation and absorption—these, in brief, are the six limbs of yoga. ॥16॥
7.2.37.17: The distinct definitions of these are set forth in the Śiva-śāstra, and in the other Śiva-āgamas, especially the Kāmika and the rest, ॥17॥
7.2.37.18: and likewise in the Yoga-śāstras and in certain Purāṇas. Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy and non-possession—this is called yama by the good, as it consists of five components. ॥18॥
7.2.37.19: Purity, contentment, austerity, recitation and devotion to the Lord—thus niyama is of five kinds according to the division of its parts. ॥19॥
7.2.37.20: Svastika, padma, the half-moon, vīra, yoga, prasādhita, paryaṅka and yatheṣṭa (as one pleases)—posture is declared to be eightfold. ॥20॥
7.2.37.21: Prāṇa is the air arising in one's own body; its āyāma is its restraint. It is said to be threefold: recaka, pūraka and kumbhaka. ॥21॥
7.2.37.22: Pressing one nostril with a finger, one should expel the air of the belly through the other; this is known as recaka. ॥22॥
7.2.37.23: One should fill the body with external air through the other nostril, like a leather bag; from this filling it is held to be pūraka. ॥23॥
7.2.37.24: When one neither releases nor takes in the air, which remains within and without, and stays motionless, full like a pot, that is kumbhaka. ॥24॥
7.2.37.25: This triad beginning with recaka should be neither hurried nor slow; the practitioner of yoga, self-controlled, should practise it by gradual progression. ॥25॥
7.2.37.26: The practice of recaka and the rest, preceded by purification of the channels and culminating in voluntary departure from the body, is taught in the instruction of yoga. ॥26॥
7.2.37.27: The restraint in breath-control, following the sequence beginning with kanyaka, is taught as fourfold according to the division of measure and quality. ॥27॥
7.2.37.28: Of the four, the kanyaka consists of twelve measures; the middle one has two udghātas and consists of twenty-four measures. ॥28॥
7.2.37.29: The highest has three udghātas and is of thirty-six measures; the prāṇāyāma beyond that produces sweating, trembling and the like. ॥29॥
7.2.37.30: For the yogin there then arise horripilation born of bliss, the shedding of tears from the eyes, babbling, whirling, fainting and the like. ॥30॥
7.2.37.31: Circling the knee with the hand, neither fast nor slow, one should snap the fingers; that duration is declared a mātrā. ॥31॥
7.2.37.32: The measures are to be understood in order according to the sequence of udghātas. One should practise breath-control preceded by purification of the channels. ॥32॥
7.2.37.33: Breath-control is known to be twofold: agarbha and sagarbha. Agarbha is without recitation and meditation; sagarbha is accompanied by them. ॥33॥
7.2.37.34: Breath-control joined with the seed is a hundred times greater than the seedless; therefore yogins practise breath-restraint with the seed. ॥34॥
7.2.37.35: By the very conquest of prāṇa the winds of the body are conquered: prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna and vyāna, ॥35॥
7.2.37.36: nāga, kūrma, kṛkala, devadatta and dhanañjaya. Because it makes the going-forth (prayāṇa), it is called prāṇa. ॥36॥
7.2.37.37: The one called apāna leads downward the food and other things that are eaten; vyāna pervades all the limbs, making them grow. ॥37॥
7.2.37.38: Because it stirs up the vital points, the wind is called udāna; because it carries nourishment evenly to all the limbs, it is called samāna. ॥38॥
7.2.37.39: Nāga is said to act in belching, kūrma resides in opening the eyes, kṛkala is to be known in sneezing, devadatta in yawning. ॥39॥
7.2.37.40: All-pervading dhanañjaya does not leave even the dead body. This breath-control, practised gradually, becomes effective. ॥40॥
7.2.37.41: Prāṇāyāma burns away every fault and protects the practitioner's body. When the breath has been properly mastered, one should look for its signs. ॥41॥
7.2.37.42: First, feces, urine and phlegm become scanty; there arises the capacity to eat much, and likewise breathing out only after a long interval. ॥42॥
7.2.37.43: Lightness, swiftness of movement, vigour, excellence of voice, the destruction of all diseases, strength, radiance, beauty of form, ॥43॥
7.2.37.44: steadfastness, intelligence, youthfulness, stability and serenity are its signs. Austerities, the destruction of sins, sacrifices, gifts, vows and the like — ॥44॥
7.2.37.45: these do not equal a sixteenth part of that prāṇāyāma. The senses here are attached each to its own objects; ॥45॥
7.2.37.46: that by which one forcibly withdraws and restrains them is called pratyāhāra. The senses, with the mind foremost, lead to heaven and to hell: ॥46॥
7.2.37.47: when restrained they lead to heaven, when let loose to hell. Therefore the wise person who seeks happiness, established in knowledge and dispassion, ॥47॥
7.2.37.48: should quickly rein in the horses of the senses and lift up the self by the self. Dhāraṇā, in brief, is the binding of the mind to a place. ॥48॥
7.2.37.49: And the place is Śiva alone, nothing else, since anything else is subject to the threefold fault. When the mind, fixed on that place for some set period of time, ॥49॥
7.2.37.50: does not slip from its target, that is dhāraṇā, and not otherwise. The first steadiness of the mind arises from dhāraṇā. ॥50॥
7.2.37.51: Therefore one should make the mind firm through the persistent practice of dhāraṇā. The root dhyai is taught in the sense of thinking; thinking of Śiva again and again ॥51॥
7.2.37.52: with an undistracted mind — that is called dhyāna. And that uniform awareness of a mind settled on the object of meditation, ॥52॥
7.2.37.53: a stream free of any other cognition, is called dhyāna. Abandoning everything else, Śiva alone, the bestower of welfare, ॥53॥
7.2.37.54: the supreme Lord over the lords of the gods, is to be meditated upon — so the Atharvan scripture concludes. Likewise the supreme Śivā is to be meditated upon; the two, Śiva and Śivā, pervade all beings. ॥54॥
7.2.37.55: Those two, known from śruti, smṛti and the śāstras, all-pervading, ever risen, omniscient, are to be meditated upon constantly in the distinctions of their many forms. ॥55॥
7.2.37.56: Liberation is the first result, and the other result is the powers such as aṇimā; thus the purpose of this meditation is to be known as twofold. ॥56॥
7.2.37.57: The meditator, meditation, the object of meditation, and the purpose of meditation — knowing this fourfold set, the knower of yoga should practise yoga. ॥57॥
7.2.37.58: Endowed with knowledge and dispassion, full of faith, possessed of patience, free from possessiveness and ever zealous — such a person is declared a fit meditator. ॥58॥
7.2.37.59: Tired of japa, one should meditate again; tired of meditation, one should do japa again. For one devoted to japa and meditation, yoga is quickly accomplished. ॥59॥
7.2.37.60: Dhāraṇā lasts twelve prāṇāyāmas; dhyāna lasts twelve dhāraṇās; the span of twelve dhyānas is called samādhi. ॥60॥
7.2.37.61: Samādhi is declared to be the final limb of yoga; and through samādhi the light of wisdom spreads everywhere. ॥61॥
7.2.37.62: That shining in which only the object appears, which stands still like a calm ocean, as though empty of its own form, is called samādhi. ॥62॥
7.2.37.63: Having merged the mind in the object of meditation, he should behold it very steadily. The yogin so absorbed, like a fire that has gone out, is said to be established in samādhi. ॥63॥
7.2.37.64: He does not hear, nor smell, nor speak, nor see; nor does he perceive touch, nor does his mind form intentions. ॥64॥
7.2.37.65: Nor does he identify with anything, nor is he bound; like a piece of wood — one whose self is thus dissolved in Śiva is here called established in samādhi. ॥65॥
7.2.37.66: Just as a lamp placed where there is no wind never flickers, so too is one fixed in samādhi; therefore the wise one should not waver from it. ॥66॥
7.2.37.67: For the yogin who thus diligently practises the supreme yoga, all the obstacles to it gradually perish, O wise ones. ॥67॥
7.2.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named The course of yoga, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa, within the dialogue of Vāyu and the sages of Naimiṣa, of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥37॥
7.2.38.1: Upamanyu said: Sloth, severe diseases, negligence, doubt about the yogic stage, instability of mind, lack of faith, erroneous perception, ॥1॥
7.2.38.2: sorrows, dejection, and fickleness toward sense objects — these ten are declared to be the obstacles for men who practise yoga. ॥2॥
7.2.38.3: Sloth is the indolence of the body and mind of yogins; diseases are disorders born of imbalance of the bodily elements, arising from faults of karma. ॥3॥
7.2.38.4: Negligence means failure in the cultivation of the means of yoga. Knowledge seized by both alternatives — is it this, or that? — is doubt about the stage. ॥4॥
7.2.38.5: The lack of firm footing of the mind is called instability. Lack of faith is an attitude devoid of devotion toward the path of yoga. ॥5॥
7.2.38.6: The understanding that is inverted is called delusion. The sorrow of the mind in men, born of ignorance, they know as the ādhyātmika sorrow. ॥6॥
7.2.38.7: The sorrow that arises from the body because of deeds done formerly is ādhibhautika; that caused by thunderbolts, weapons, poison and the like is declared ādhidaivika. ॥7॥
7.2.38.8: Agitation born of the frustration of desire they call dejection. Wandering among varied sense objects is fickleness. ॥8॥
7.2.38.9: When these obstacles are pacified, for the yogin intent on yoga there arise divine disturbances (upasargas); they are indicators of attainment. ॥9॥
7.2.38.10: Intuition, hearing, understanding of speech, seeing, tasting and feeling — these six are the upasargas; they are attainments that lead to the loss of yoga. ॥10॥
7.2.38.11: Pratibhā is said to be the manifestation, exactly as it is, of an object that is subtle, concealed, past, remote or yet to come. ॥11॥
7.2.38.12: Śravaṇa is the hearing of all sounds without effort; vārttā is the understanding of the speech of all embodied beings. ॥12॥
7.2.38.13: Darśana is the seeing of divine things without effort; likewise āsvāda is said to be the tasting of divine flavours. ॥13॥
7.2.38.14: Likewise the one renowned as vedanā is the perception of touch and of divine smells and the rest. The lords of the worlds up to that of Brahmā — ॥14॥
7.2.38.15: stand before him and give many jewels; speech, sweet at will and of many kinds, flows forth. ॥15॥
7.2.38.16: All elixirs and likewise divine herbs become effective for him; celestial women, bowing to him, offer their gifts. ॥16॥
7.2.38.17: When even a single part of yogic attainment is seen, the mind should turn to liberation, thinking: Just as this has been seen by me, so too liberation will come. ॥17॥
7.2.38.18: Thinness, stoutness, childhood, old age and youth, assuming the forms of various species, bearing a body of four elements, ॥18॥
7.2.38.19: without the earthly portion, and constant possession of fragrant scent — thus they declare the eightfold paiśāca, earthly state. ॥19॥
7.2.38.20: Dwelling in water, and likewise emerging from the earth; if he wishes, he is able himself to drink even the ocean without distress; ॥20॥
7.2.38.21: wherever in this world he wishes, there water appears; holding a mass of water in the hand without a pot or the like; ॥21॥
7.2.38.22: whatever thing, even tasteless, he wishes to eat acquires flavour and other qualities at that very moment; and bearing a body of three elements; ॥22॥
7.2.38.23: freedom of the body from wounds, together with the earthly powers — this is the wondrous sixteenfold watery lordship. ॥23॥
7.2.38.24: Producing fire from the body, freedom from fear of its heat, the power to burn this world effortlessly if he should wish, ॥24॥
7.2.38.25: or placing fire in water, holding fire in the hand, restoring creation as before when it has been burnt, cooking food and the like in the mouth, forming a body from two elements, together with the watery lordship — ॥25॥
7.2.38.26: this they call the twenty-fourfold fiery lordship. Swiftness like the mind, entering into beings in an instant, ॥26॥
7.2.38.27: bearing great loads such as mountains without effort, heaviness and lightness, holding the wind in the hand, ॥27॥
7.2.38.28: shaking even the earth by the touch of a fingertip and the like, forming a body from one element, joined with the fiery enjoyments — ॥28॥
7.2.38.29: the sages know as the thirty-twofold airy lordship. Producing a body without shadow, invisibility of the senses, ॥29॥
7.2.38.30: moving through the sky at will, contact with the objects of the senses, crossing through space, and placing it within one's own body, ॥30॥
7.2.38.31: making space into a solid mass, and bodilessness, joined with the airy lordship — this great forty-fold ॥31॥
7.2.38.32: is declared the Aindra lordship; they call it the ethereal. Obtaining things at will and departing at will, ॥32॥
7.2.38.33: overpowering everything, seeing all secret matters, creating according to beings' actions, control, a pleasing appearance, ॥33॥
7.2.38.34: and seeing the course of saṃsāra, together with the Aindra enjoyments — this is the lunar lordship, mental, superior in qualities. ॥34॥
7.2.38.35: Cutting, striking, binding and likewise releasing, seizing all beings who are subject to saṃsāra, ॥35॥
7.2.38.36: and granting favour to all, and likewise conquest of death and time — this egoic lordship they call the Prājāpatya. ॥36॥
7.2.38.37: This, with the lunar enjoyments, is great and fifty-sixfold. Creation by mere resolve, protection and likewise destruction, ॥37॥
7.2.38.38: one's own authority over all, directing the minds of beings, being unequalled by anything, creating a world separately, ॥38॥
7.2.38.39: bringing about good and evil, joined with the Prājāpatya powers — this they call the sixty-fourfold Brāhma lordship. ॥39॥
7.2.38.40: Beyond this intellectual lordship they know the secondary, prakṛtic lordship; that is declared the Vaiṣṇava, and to it alone belongs the maintenance of the world. That entire state cannot be described by Brahmā or by others. ॥40॥
7.2.38.41: That is the station of Puruṣa, the station of the guṇas, the station of Gaṇeśa, and the station of the Lord (Aiśvara). That highest station cannot be known even slightly by Viṣṇu or by others. ॥41॥
7.2.38.42: And all the attainments of knowledge, too, are indeed obstacles; they must be held in check with effort, through supreme dispassion. ॥42॥
7.2.38.43: For one whose mind is attached to impure appearances and to the qualities of powers, the supreme lordship—fearless and fulfilling all desires—is not attained. ॥43॥
7.2.38.44: Therefore, he who abandons like straw the qualities and enjoyments of gods, asuras and kings—his is the supreme success in yoga. ॥44॥
7.2.38.45: Or else, wishing to bestow grace on the world, the sage may wander about; having enjoyed qualities and pleasures as he wishes, he will attain liberation. ॥45॥
7.2.38.46: Now I shall tell the practice of yoga; listen attentively. It should be done at an auspicious time, in an auspicious place such as a shrine of Śiva, solitary, free of creatures, silent, and free from disturbance; ॥46॥
7.2.38.47: on ground well smeared with cow-dung, pleasant, perfumed with scents, incense and the like, strewn with loose flowers, and adorned with canopies and so on; ॥47॥
7.2.38.48: furnished with kuśa grass, flowers, fuel-sticks, water, fruits and roots; not near fire, not near water, nor on a heap of dry leaves; ॥48॥
7.2.38.49: not in a place swarming with gnats and mosquitoes, crowded with snakes and beasts of prey, nor full of vicious animals, nor where there is fear, nor surrounded by wicked people; ॥49॥
7.2.38.50: not in a cremation ground, at a shrine or an anthill, in a ruined house, at a crossroads, on the bank of rivers, streams or the ocean, or in the middle of a street; ॥50॥
7.2.38.51: not in an old garden, a cowpen and the like, not in an undesirable or censured place; not when one has belching from indigestion or sour taste, nor in a place defiled by excrement and urine; ॥51॥
7.2.38.52: nor when suffering vomiting, indigestion or diarrhoea, nor after overeating, nor when tired; nor should one be troubled by excessive worry, nor excessively hungry and thirsty; ॥52॥
7.2.38.53: nor should one practise yoga while engaged in duties for one's guru and the like. Moderate in food and recreation, moderate in effort in one's actions, ॥53॥
7.2.38.54: moderate in sleep and waking, free from all strain, he should take a seat that is soft, pleasing, broad, quite even and clean. ॥54॥
7.2.38.55: He should practise among the postures such as padmaka and svastika. Having bowed in due order to those worthy of salutation, ending with his own guru, ॥55॥
7.2.38.56: with neck, head and chest straight, he should not remain with eyes tightly shut; with head slightly raised, he should not let his teeth touch each other. ॥56॥
7.2.38.57: Placing the tongue motionless, resting at the tips of the teeth, guarding the testicles and also the genital with the heels, ॥57॥
7.2.38.58: placing the arms crosswise, without strain, upon the thighs, and setting the back of the right hand upon the left palm, ॥58॥
7.2.38.59: gently raising the back and pushing the chest forward, gazing at the tip of his own nose and not looking about in the directions, ॥59॥
7.2.38.60: with the movement of breath held in check, motionless like a stone, contemplating Śiva together with Ambā within the shrine of his own body, ॥60॥
7.2.38.61: he should worship them by the sacrifice of meditation in the middle of the pedestal of the heart-lotus. Or at the root, at the tip of the nose, at the navel, at the throat, or in the cavities of the palate, ॥61॥
7.2.38.62: between the brows, at the place of the aperture, at the forehead, or at the crown of the head, he should meditate, having duly imagined the supreme seat of Śiva and Śivā. ॥62॥
7.2.38.63: There, either with the surrounding retinue (āvaraṇa) or without it, he should meditate on Śiva according to rule in a two-petalled, sixteen-spoked or twelve-spoked lotus, ॥63॥
7.2.38.64: or in a ten-spoked, six-cornered or four-cornered one, he should meditate on Śiva. Between the brows is a two-petalled lotus, bright as lightning. ॥64॥
7.2.38.65: On the southern and northern petals of the lotus situated between the brows, in order, which are of the colour of lightning, are the letters at the end of the alphabet. ॥65॥
7.2.38.66: The petals of the sixteen-spoked lotus are the sixteen vowels, beginning from the east in order; this lotus lies from the root of the kanda. ॥66॥
7.2.38.67: The letters beginning with ka and ending with ṭha are, in order, the petals of the sun-coloured lotus; that is to be meditated upon within the heart. ॥67॥
7.2.38.68: The letters ḍa through pha, in order, are declared to be the petals of the lotus white as cow's milk, above the navel towards the back. And below, this lotus has six petals, ॥68॥
7.2.38.69: of the lotus coloured like smokeless embers, the letters beginning with ba and ending with la. Of the golden lotus of the mūlādhāra, the letters from va to sa are, in order, set as its petals. ॥69॥
7.2.38.70: Now, among these lotuses, wherever the mind delights, there alone he should contemplate the god and the goddess with a steady intellect. ॥70॥
7.2.38.71: He should meditate on him as thumb-sized, stainless, shining all around, shaped like the flame of a pure lamp, fully adorned with his own Śakti; ॥71॥
7.2.38.72: or shaped like the crescent of the moon, or in the form of a star, or like the awn of nīvāra rice, or resembling a lotus-stalk fibre; ॥72॥
7.2.38.73: shaped like a kadamba ball, or like a drop of dew. If the meditator desires mastery over the principles beginning with earth, ॥73॥
7.2.38.74: he should contemplate the gross form presiding over each respective principle. The eight forms beginning with Brahmā and ending with Sadāśiva, and those beginning with Bhava, ॥74॥
7.2.38.75: are the gross forms of Śiva, as determined in the Śaiva scriptures. These forms are terrible, mixed, and tranquil; by the lords among sages, ॥75॥
7.2.38.76: free from desire for fruits and skilled in contemplation, they are to be contemplated. If the terrible ones are contemplated, they bring about the destruction of sin and disease. ॥76॥
7.2.38.77: With the mixed forms the result comes after a long time; with the gentle, neither immediately nor after a long time. Through the gentle ones especially, liberation, peace and wisdom are attained. ॥77॥
7.2.38.78: And the attainments are accomplished here step by step; of this there is no doubt. ॥78॥
7.2.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named The obstacles that arise in the course of yoga, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥38॥
7.2.39.1: Upamanyu said: Some yogins meditate on him alone, thinking that for those who remember Śrīkaṇṭha, the Lord, the accomplishment of all aims comes about at once. ॥1॥
7.2.39.2: Some practise gross meditation for the steadying of the mind. On the gross the mind becomes motionless, and then on the subtle it becomes firm. ॥2॥
7.2.39.3: When Śiva himself is contemplated directly, all the siddhis are accomplished. Even when other forms are meditated upon, one should contemplate in them the form of Śiva. ॥3॥
7.2.39.4: One should observe the steadiness of the mind and meditate on that object again and again. They have declared meditation to be at first with an object, and afterwards without an object. ॥4॥
7.2.39.5: Of these, the view of the wise is that meditation without any object does not strictly exist, for it is a certain continuous flow of the intellect that is called meditation. ॥5॥
7.2.39.6: Therefore, in objectless meditation, the intellect alone, without an object, functions here. Hence meditation with an object is that which rests on the image of the rays of the rising sun; ॥6॥
7.2.39.7: that resting on the subtle is objectless; in ultimate truth there is no other. Alternatively, meditation with an object is that which depends on a form, ॥7॥
7.2.39.8: and awareness of the formless Self is held to be objectless meditation. That same meditation is called seedless and with seed, ॥8॥
7.2.39.9: according as it rests on the formless or likewise on a form. Therefore, having first practised meditation with an object and with seed, ॥9॥
7.2.39.10: at the end one should practise the objectless, seedless meditation for complete accomplishment. Through prāṇāyāma the states of the Goddess, śānti and the rest, are attained in sequence: ॥10॥
7.2.39.11: śānti, praśānti, dīpti, and after that prasāda. The calming of all calamities is called śānti. ॥11॥
7.2.39.12: The destruction of darkness within and without is declared to be praśānti. The illumination that is outward and inward is called dīpti. ॥12॥
7.2.39.13: The healthy, settled state of the intellect is proclaimed to be prasāda. And all the instruments, external and internal, ॥13॥
7.2.39.14: quickly become clear through the clarity of the intellect. The meditator, meditation, the object of meditation, and the purpose of meditation — knowing this fourfold set, the meditator should practise meditation. ॥14॥
7.2.39.15: One endowed with knowledge and dispassion, ever of unagitated mind, full of faith, and serene in spirit, is declared by the wise to be a meditator. ॥15॥
7.2.39.16: The verbal root dhyai is known to be used in the sense of thinking; so thinking of Śiva again and again ॥16॥
7.2.39.17: — just as even a little practice of yoga would destroy sin — and the thought of one who meditates with faith on the Supreme Lord even for a moment, ॥17॥
7.2.39.18: with an undistracted mind, is called meditation. ॥18॥
7.2.39.19: The support of this meditation, which has the form of a flow of the intellect, is called by the wise the object of meditation; and that is Śiva himself together with Ambā. ॥19॥
7.2.39.20: The certainty of liberation and full lordly power, beginning with aṇimā, are declared to be the direct purpose of complete meditation on Śiva. ॥20॥
7.2.39.21: Since from meditation one obtains both happiness and liberation, a man should therefore abandon everything and devote himself to meditation. ॥21॥
7.2.39.22: There is no knowledge without meditation, and no meditation for one who is not a yogin. He who has both meditation and knowledge has crossed the ocean of worldly existence. ॥22॥
7.2.39.23: Knowledge that is clear, one-pointed, and free from all limiting adjuncts is attained only by the yogin who is engaged in the practice of yoga. ॥23॥
7.2.39.24: The mind of those whose sins are wholly destroyed turns to knowledge and meditation; for those whose intellect is struck by sin, even talk of it is very hard to come by. ॥24॥
7.2.39.25: Just as a greatly blazing fire burns up both the dry and the wet, so the fire of meditation burns good and bad karma in an instant. ॥25॥
7.2.39.26: Just as even a very small lamp dispels a vast darkness, so even a little practice of yoga destroys great sin. ॥26॥
7.2.39.27: For one who meditates with faith on the Supreme Lord even for a moment, the very great good that arises has no end at all. ॥27॥
7.2.39.28: There is no pilgrimage place equal to meditation, no austerity equal to meditation, no sacrifice equal to meditation; therefore one should practise meditation. ॥28॥
7.2.39.29: Yogins do not resort to sacred places full of water or to gods made of stone and clay, because of their conviction in their own Self. ॥29॥
7.2.39.30: For yogins the subtle divine body of the Lord becomes directly perceptible, just as for those not yoked in yoga it is the gross form fashioned of clay, wood and the like. ॥30॥
7.2.39.31: Just as here the king's inner attendants are dear to him, not the outer ones, so those devoted to inner meditation are dear to Śambhu, not the performers of rites. ॥31॥
7.2.39.32: Just as in the world the outer servants in a king's palace, though they see its riches, do not greatly enjoy its fruits, so too here the ritualists. ॥32॥
7.2.39.33: If such aspirants perish midway, one who has striven for jñānayoga will, by the mere effort at yoga, go to the world of Rudra. ॥33॥
7.2.39.34: Having enjoyed happiness there, he is born in a family of yogins; obtaining jñānayoga again, he passes beyond saṃsāra. ॥34॥
7.2.39.35: The state that a man attains even by merely desiring to know yoga, he does not attain even by all the great sacrifices. ॥35॥
7.2.39.36: The fruit gained by worshipping ten million twice-born men learned in the Vedas — that fruit is gained by giving merely alms to a Śiva-yogin. ॥36॥
7.2.39.37: Whatever fruit lies in sacrifices, the agnihotra, gifts, pilgrimages and fire-offerings — all that fruit one obtains by giving food to yogins. ॥37॥
7.2.39.38: Those deluded ones who slander Śiva-yogins fall, together with their listeners, into the hells until the destruction of the earth. ॥38॥
7.2.39.39: Only when there is a listener can there be a speaker of slander against yogins; therefore the listener is held by the very great to be the more sinful and deserving of punishment. But those who constantly honour Śiva-yogins with devotion ॥39॥
7.2.39.40: obtain great enjoyments and, at the end, the yoga of Śaṅkara. Therefore Śiva-yogins should be duly worshipped by men who desire enjoyments. ॥40॥
7.2.39.41: Yogins should be served with shelter, food, drink and the like, and with beds, coverings and so on. Because it is full of essence, the dharma of yoga cannot be broken by the mallets of sin. ॥41॥
7.2.39.42: It should be known to be like a diamond-grain. So too yogins are not stained by sin or by floods of sins, just as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water. ॥42॥
7.2.39.43: In whatever land a sage devoted to Śiva-yoga constantly dwells, even that land becomes purified; what then need be said of his being pure? ॥43॥
7.2.39.44: Therefore the wise man, abandoning every other duty, should diligently practise Śiva-yoga for the removal of all sorrows. ॥44॥
7.2.39.45: The yogin who has attained the fruit of yoga may, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds, enjoy pleasures as he wishes and roam about, or remain here. ॥45॥
7.2.39.46: Or else, regarding sensual pleasure as merely petty and renouncing it through the yoga of dispassion, let him at his own will be freed from action. ॥46॥
7.2.39.47: But the mortal who sees death approaching and ill omens in abundance should, intent on undertaking yoga, take refuge in a holy place of Śiva. ॥47॥
7.2.39.48: While dwelling there, if that man is steadfast of mind, he may of his own accord give up his life-breaths even without disease and the like, ॥48॥
7.2.39.49: having undertaken fasting, or having offered his body into Śiva's fire, or having cast his own body into Śiva's sacred waters by immersion — ॥49॥
7.2.39.50: whoever gives up his life according to the rule stated in the Śaiva scriptures is liberated at once; there is no need for deliberation on this. ॥50॥
7.2.39.51: Or if one who has taken refuge in a holy place of Śiva dies helplessly through disease and the like, he too is likewise liberated; there is no doubt of this. ॥51॥
7.2.39.52: For they declare death through fasting and the like to be the best, since it is undertaken with a mind made steadfast by trust in scripture. ॥52॥
7.2.39.53: Whoever, having killed one given to reviling Śiva, or being himself afflicted in the attempt, gives up his life-breaths so hard to give up, is not born again. ॥53॥
7.2.39.54: He who, unable to kill one given to reviling Śiva, dies by his own hand is liberated at once, together with twenty-one generations of his family. ॥54॥
7.2.39.55: Whoever gives up his life for Śiva's sake, or for the sake of a devotee of Śiva — no man standing on the path of liberation is equal to him. ॥55॥
7.2.39.56: Therefore his liberation from the circle of saṃsāra is swifter. Or, having somehow adopted any one of these means — ॥56॥
7.2.39.57: or if one who has duly received the purification of the six paths dies, one should not perform for him here the after-death rites as is done for bound souls (paśus). ॥57॥
7.2.39.58: Nor should his son and others in particular incur ritual impurity. For the sake of Śaiva practice or for the sake of Śaiva knowledge, one may either bury his body in the ground or burn it with pure fire, ॥58॥
7.2.39.59: or cast it into auspicious waters, or leave it like a piece of wood or a clod of earth. And if one wishes to perform a rite with reference to him, ॥59॥
7.2.39.60: one should perform only an auspicious rite and satisfy devotees according to one's ability. A Śaiva may take his wealth if his offspring are Śaiva; if there are none, one should give it to Śiva; offspring who are paśus (uninitiated) should not receive it. ॥60॥
7.2.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named Śaiva yoga, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥39॥
7.2.40.1: Sūta said: Thus Vāyu related to the sages, who had bowed before him, the yoga of knowledge that the Yādava Kṛṣṇa had received from Upamanyu, the conqueror of anger. Then, his own form made manifest, he vanished at once into the sky in the evening. ॥1॥
7.2.40.2: Then at daybreak all the ascetics of Naimiṣa set out to perform the avabhṛtha concluding bath at the end of the sacrificial session. ॥2॥
7.2.40.3: Then, at Brahmā's command, the goddess Sarasvatī herself began to flow as an auspicious river, clear and with sweet waters. ॥3॥
7.2.40.4: Seeing the river Sarasvatī, the sages, delighted at heart, completed the sacrificial session they had begun and bathed there. ॥4॥
7.2.40.5: Then, having satisfied the gods and others with its auspicious waters, and recalling what had happened before, they went toward Vārāṇasī. ॥5॥
7.2.40.6: Then, seeing the Bhāgīrathī Gaṅgā descending from the foot of the Himālaya and flowing southward, they bathed there and went on along her bank. ॥6॥
7.2.40.7: Then, reaching Vārāṇasī, all of them rejoiced, and they bathed in the Gaṅgā where she flows northward, ॥7॥
7.2.40.8: and having seen the Avimukteśvara liṅga and worshipped it according to rule, as they were about to depart they saw there, in the sky, something shining— ॥8॥
7.2.40.9: a divine, most wondrous radiance, like ten million suns, which with the expanse of its own lustre pervaded the spaces of all the directions. ॥9॥
7.2.40.10: Then Pāśupata adepts, sages whose bodies were covered with ash, approached in hundreds and became merged in that radiance. ॥10॥
7.2.40.11: When those great-souled ascetics had thus dissolved into it, the radiance at once disappeared; it was like a marvel. ॥11॥
7.2.40.12: Seeing that great wonder, the great sages of Naimiṣa, not knowing what it was, went toward Brahmā's forest. ॥12॥
7.2.40.13: Even before their going, Vāyu, the purifier of the worlds, had reported his meeting with the Naimiṣa sages and the great-souled one's dialogue with them, ॥13॥
7.2.40.14: then their pure understanding directed to Śiva together with Ambā and his attendants, and also the completion of the long sacrificial session of those sacrificers— ॥14॥
7.2.40.15: having reported all this to Brahmā, the sustainer of the worlds and source of the Veda, and permitted by him, he had gone to his own city for his own business. ॥15॥
7.2.40.16: Now Brahmā, seated in his abode, was attending to Tumburu and Nārada, who were competing with each other and disputing about singing; ॥16॥
7.2.40.17: acting as arbiter, enjoying the rasas arising from the songs they produced, he sat at ease, attended by Gandharvas and Apsarases. ॥17॥
7.2.40.18: At that time, because it was not an opportune moment, the sages were stopped at the door by the doorkeepers and sat down to one side outside Brahmā's palace. ॥18॥
7.2.40.19: Then Nārada, having attained equality with Tumburu in singing, and permitted by Brahmā, the Supreme Lord, to keep company with him, ॥19॥
7.2.40.20: abandoning their mutual rivalry and reaching the highest friendship, together with him, and surrounded by Apsarases and Gandharvas, ॥20॥
7.2.40.21: came out of the Creator's palace, like the sun from a cloud, to sing with the vīṇā before the god Nakulīśvara, the Lord. ॥21॥
7.2.40.22: Seeing him, Nārada, the bull among sages, those sages of the six clans bowed and with great respect asked whether it was a suitable time to see the Lord. ॥22॥
7.2.40.23: Saying, this is indeed the right moment, go in from here, he went off, intent on other matters and in great haste. ॥23॥
7.2.40.24: Then those stationed at the door announced them to Brahmā, and thereupon they, forming a group, entered the dwelling of the Egg-born Brahmā. ॥24॥
7.2.40.25: Having entered, they bowed to the god from afar, prostrating on the ground like a staff; then, permitted by him, they gathered around and stood near him. ॥25॥
7.2.40.26: The Lotus-seated one, having asked about the welfare of those standing there, said: Your story is known to me, since Vāyu himself told us. ॥26॥
7.2.40.27: What did you do afterwards, when the Wind had vanished? When the Lord of gods had said this, the sages—about what happened after the avabhṛtha bath: ॥27॥
7.2.40.28: their going to the sacred ford of the Gaṅgā, the journey to Vārāṇasī, the seeing there of the liṅgas established by the lords of the gods, ॥28॥
7.2.40.29: the single worship of the Avimukteśvara liṅga as well, and the sight in the sky of that great mass of radiance, ॥29॥
7.2.40.30: the dissolution of the sages there, then the withdrawal of the radiance, and their wish for knowledge of its true nature, though they had pondered it themselves— ॥30॥
7.2.40.31: all this they told him in detail, bowing again and again. Having heard what the sages related, the four-faced Creator of all, ॥31॥
7.2.40.32: shook his head slightly and spoke in a deep voice: Supreme otherworldly perfection is drawing near to you. ॥32॥
7.2.40.33: The Lord, long worshipped by you through the long sacrificial session, has become inclined to grace—this is indicated by what has happened. ॥33॥
7.2.40.34: What you saw shining in the sky at Vārāṇasī was the supreme radiance of Maheśvara itself, known as the Liṅga. ॥34॥
7.2.40.35: And the sages who merged there, keepers of the Vedic Pāśupata vow, lifelong celibates whose sins were burnt away, became liberated and established in themselves. ॥35॥
7.2.40.36: That liberation is soon to be attained by you too through this Lord—this very meaning is indicated by the radiance you saw. ॥36॥
7.2.40.37: So this time has come to you of its own accord by destiny. Go to the southern peak of Meru, frequented by the gods, ॥37॥
7.2.40.38: where my son Sanatkumāra, the supreme sage, dwells, awaiting the coming in person of Nandin, lord of the bhūtas. ॥38॥
7.2.40.39: Long ago Sanatkumāra, even on seeing the Supreme Lord, out of ignorance thought himself the chief of all yogins and was spoiled in humility; ॥39॥
7.2.40.40: and, utterly fearless, he did not perform the proper courtesies such as rising to greet him. For that offence the angered Nandin turned him into a great camel. ॥40॥
7.2.40.41: Then, after a long time, I, grieving on his account, worshipped the God and the Goddess, and also propitiated Nandin, ॥41॥
7.2.40.42: and somehow, with effort, his wickedness was removed, and he was restored as before to the state of youth prefixed by Sanat, that is, to being Sanatkumāra. ॥42॥
7.2.40.43: Then Mahādeva, as if smiling, said to the lord of the gaṇas: Disregarding me myself, the sage became so arrogant. ॥43॥
7.2.40.44: Therefore you yourself, O sinless one, tell him my true nature—Brahmā's firstborn son, who regards me as though I were deluded. ॥44॥
7.2.40.45: By me alone he is given to you as a disciple, to be the promulgator of my knowledge; and he will perform your consecration as overseer of dharma. ॥45॥
7.2.40.46: Thus addressed again, the foremost of all the hosts of beings accepted the command, receiving it on his head, as he had before. ॥46॥
7.2.40.47: Likewise Sanatkumāra too, at my instruction, is performing on Meru austerity hard to perform, to win the grace of this gaṇa Nandin. ॥47॥
7.2.40.48: He should be seen by you before his meeting with the lord of the gaṇas; to bestow grace on him, Nandī will soon come there. ॥48॥
7.2.40.49: Thus quickly instructed and sent off by the universal yogin, the sages went to the Kumāra peak, south of Meru. ॥49॥
7.2.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named The journey of the sages of Naimiṣa, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥40॥
7.2.41.1: Sūta said: There was a lake named Skandasaras, like an ocean, whose water was sweet as nectar, cool, clear, deep and light. ॥1॥
7.2.41.2: It was enclosed all around by heaps of crystal stones, and all its quarters were covered with the blooming flowers of every season. ॥2॥
7.2.41.3: With its moss, blue lotuses, lotuses, and white water-lilies like stars, and its waves like clouds, it was like the sky come down to earth. ॥3॥
7.2.41.4: Its eight quarters shone with lovely stairways and landings made of blue stone, easy for going down and coming up. ॥4॥
7.2.41.5: It was frequented by young sages who had gone down into it and in great numbers come up out of it, bathed, wearing white sacred threads, white loincloths and bark garments, ॥5॥
7.2.41.6: some with matted locks and topknots, some shaven, adorned with the tripuṇḍra mark, their faces smiling and overcome by dispassion — young sons of sages, ॥6॥
7.2.41.7: with pots, cups of lotus leaves, auspicious jars, water-pots, and other such vessels like karakas, ॥7॥
7.2.41.8: its water was carried daily for themselves, for others, and especially for the deities, and flowers were gathered there. ॥8॥
7.2.41.9: It was frequented by sages of right conduct, standing on rocks in the water for fear of touching the lowly, their limbs grey with the ash they had applied, ॥9॥
7.2.41.10: by them diving here and there in the waters, cultured and dear ones seated on rocks, offering sesame, unbroken rice and flowers, having laid aside their darbha rings, ॥10॥
7.2.41.11: having completed the libations — first to the gods, in the middle to the sages, then to the ancestors — as one should, presenting offerings to the learned twice-born who had come for the daily bath, ॥11॥
7.2.41.12: with breezes laden with the scent of the many bali-offerings and flowers made at place after place, by those performing worship and the like on the altars, preceded by the arghya to the Sun. ॥12॥
7.2.41.13: In some places herd-leading elephants were diving, surfacing and wandering loose; in others does, deer and horses had come, driven by thirst; ॥13॥
7.2.41.14: in some places peacocks and fine elephants came out after drinking water; in others it was resplendent with bulls and rival bulls butting against the banks. ॥14॥
7.2.41.15: In places with the cries of kāraṇḍava ducks, in places with the calls of sārasa cranes, in places with the cries of cakravāka birds, in places with the songs of bees, ॥15॥
7.2.41.16: it seemed to be speaking again and again, with affection, to all those creatures who used it for bathing, drinking and the like and lived on the wealth of its trees. ॥16॥
7.2.41.17: With the calls of crowds of cuckoos nestled in the tops of the trees on its banks, it was inviting day and night all who were afflicted by the heat. ॥17॥
7.2.41.18: On the northern shore of that lake, beneath a wish-fulfilling tree, on an altar made of diamond-stone, on a soft deerskin, ॥18॥
7.2.41.19: they saw Sanatkumāra seated, ever bearing the body of a child, steady of mind, having just then come out of samādhi, ॥19॥
7.2.41.20: being attended by sages and worshipped even by the lords of yogins. Those Naimiṣa sages saw him, and bowing, approached him. ॥20॥
7.2.41.21: Just as they were telling him, who had asked, the reason for their coming, a tumultuous sound of drums was heard in the sky. ॥21॥
7.2.41.22: At that very moment a celestial car, radiant as the sun, was seen, surrounded on all sides by countless lords of the gaṇas, ॥22॥
7.2.41.23: crowded with troops of apsarases, surrounded by Rudra's maidens, resounding with mṛdaṅga and muraja drums, filled with the sound of flutes and vīṇās, ॥23॥
7.2.41.24: rich with canopies of many-coloured gems, shining with strings of pearls, and by sages, siddhas, gandharvas, yakṣas, cāraṇas and kinnaras ॥24॥
7.2.41.25: dancing, singing and playing instruments, it was surrounded; with a banner bearing the emblem of the heroic bull, on a staff of coral, ॥25॥
7.2.41.26: its gateway honoured by that banner, the sign of its dignity. In the middle of that celestial car, between a pair of chowries, ॥26॥
7.2.41.27: beneath a parasol with a jewelled handle, pure like the moon, seated on a divine lion-throne together with the goddess Suyaśā, ॥27॥
7.2.41.28: by his splendour, his form and his three eyes and other features making those who approached recognise in him the likeness of the Lord, ॥28॥
7.2.41.29: like the inviolable command of the Maker of the world come in person, like Śambhu's grace to all standing visibly before them, ॥29॥
7.2.41.30: — the son of Śilāda himself, bearing the glorious, excellent trident as his weapon, chief of the gaṇas of the Lord of the universe, like a second Viśveśvara, ॥30॥
7.2.41.31: able to restrain and to favour even the creators of the universe, four-armed, noble of limb, adorned with a crescent of the moon, ॥31॥
7.2.41.32: adorned with a serpent on his neck and the moon on his crown, like sovereignty embodied, like power in action, ॥32॥
7.2.41.33: like liberation fulfilled, like omniscience in company — seeing him, Brahmā's son, his face beaming with joy, together with the sages, ॥33॥
7.2.41.34: rose and stood with folded hands, as if offering himself to him. Then, meanwhile, when that celestial car had come down to earth, ॥34॥
7.2.41.35: having prostrated like a staff before the lord and praised him, he presented the sages: These sages of the six lineages, long engaged in a sacrificial session at Naimiṣa, have come, directed by Brahmā, out of a longing to see you from long before. ॥35॥
7.2.41.36: Hearing the words of Brahmā's son, Nandī at once cut their bonds with a glance, and having bestowed the Śaiva dharma and the lordly yoga of knowledge, went back to the side of the god. ॥36॥
7.2.41.37: All that was told by Sanatkumāra directly to Vyāsa, my teacher; and it was told to me by the revered Vyāsa; and by me it has been related to you in brief. ॥37॥
7.2.41.38: This jewel among Purāṇas, belonging to the Chastiser of the Cities, should not be told to those who do not know the Veda, nor to an undevoted disciple, nor to unbelievers; for if given out of delusion it brings hell. ॥38॥
7.2.41.39: Those by whom it is given, received, read or heard in the proper way, accompanied by service — to them it surely grants happiness, the triad of aims headed by dharma, and at the end liberation. ॥39॥
7.2.41.40: A mutual service has been rendered by you and by me through our joining on the path of the Purāṇas. Therefore I shall go, my desire fulfilled. May everything always be auspicious for us. ॥40॥
7.2.41.41: When Sūta had given his blessings and departed, and the sacrifice, that great undertaking, had come to its end, and when the age of Kali was growing polluted by attachment to sense-objects, the sages of good conduct took up their dwelling in the environs of Vārāṇasī. ॥41॥
7.2.41.42: Then those blameless ones, out of the desire to be freed from the bonds of the bound soul (paśu), performed the Pāśupata vow in its entirety, and, having mastered complete knowledge and meditative absorption, attained supreme bliss. ॥42॥
7.2.41.43: Vyāsa said: Thus this beneficial Śiva Purāṇa is complete. It should be read with care and reverence, and in the same way it should be heard. ॥43॥
7.2.41.44: It should not be recited to an unbeliever, to one without faith, or to a deceitful person, nor to one not devoted to Maheśa, nor likewise to a hypocrite who makes a show of dharma. ॥44॥
7.2.41.45: By hearing this even once, sin is reduced to ashes; one without devotion obtains devotion, and a devotee comes to share in an abundance of devotion. ॥45॥
7.2.41.46: When it is heard again, true devotion arises; and from hearing it yet again, liberation results. Therefore those who seek liberation should hear it again and again. ॥46॥
7.2.41.47: Five recitations of this Purāṇa should be performed with a pure mind; one who does so with the supreme fruit in view attains it, without doubt. ॥47॥
7.2.41.48: Kings of old, brāhmaṇas, and excellent vaiśyas, having recited it seven times, obtained the vision of Śiva. ॥48॥
7.2.41.49: Even now, whatever human being, intent on devotion, hears this shall enjoy all pleasures here and at the end attain liberation. ॥49॥
7.2.41.50: This Śiva Purāṇa is supremely dear to Śiva; it grants enjoyment and liberation, is equal to the Veda, and increases devotion. ॥50॥
7.2.41.51: May that Śaṅkara, together with his gaṇas, his sons, and Ambā, always bestow welfare upon the reciter and the listener of this Śiva Purāṇa. ॥51॥
7.2.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named Vyāsa's teaching and the greatness of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the seventh saṃhitā, the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥41॥
